{{c|{{larger|'''PREFACE'''}}

{{rule|4em}}}}

{{di|A}}MONG the priceless teachings that may be found in the great Hindu poem of the ''Mahâbhârata'', there is none so rare and precious as this—"The Lord's Song." Since it fell from the divine lips of Shrî Krishna on the field of battle, and stilled the surging emotions of his disciple and friend, how many troubled hearts has it quieted and strengthened, how many weary souls has it led to Him! It is meant to lift the aspirant from the lower levels of renunciation, where objects are renounced, to the loftier heights where desires are dead, and where the Yogi dwells in calm and ceaseless contemplation, while his body and mind are actively employed in discharging the duties that fall to his lot in life. That the spiritual man need not be a recluse, that union with the divine Life may be achieved and maintained in the midst of worldly affairs, that the obstacles to that union lie not outside us but within us—such is the central lesson of the {{sc|Bhagavad-Gita}}.

It is a scripture of Yoga; now Yoga is literally union, and it means harmony with the divine Law, the becoming one with the divine Life, by the subdual of all outward-going energies. To reach this, balance<noinclude></noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="4" user="EncycloPetey" />{{RunningHeader|iv|PREFACE|}}</noinclude>must be gained, equilibrium, so that the self, joined to the Self, shall not be affected by pleasure or pain, desire or aversion, or any of the "pairs of opposites" between which untrained selves swing backwards and forwards. Moderation is therefore the keynote of the Gita, and the harmonising of all the constituents of man, till they vibrate in perfect attunement with the One, the Supreme Self. This is the aim the disciple is to set before him. He must learn not to be attracted by the attractive, nor repelled by the repellent, but must see both as manifestations of the one Lord, so that they may be lessons for his guidance, not fetters for his bondage. In the midst of turmoil he must rest in the Lord of Peace, discharging every duty to the fullest, not because he seeks the results of his actions, but because it is his duty to perform them. His heart is an altar, love to his Lord the flame burning upon it; all his acts, physical and mental, are sacrifices offered on the altar; and once offered, he has with them no further concern.

As though to make the lesson more impressive, it was given on a field of battle. Arjuna, the warrior-prince, was to vindicate his brother's title, to destroy a usurper who was oppressing the land; it was his duty as prince, as warrior, to fight for the deliverance of his nation and to restore order and peace. To make the contest more bitter, loved comrades and friends stood on both sides, wringing his heart with personal anguish, and making a conflict of duties as well as physical strife. Could he slay those to whom he owed love and duty, and trample on ties of kindred?<noinclude></noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="4" user="EncycloPetey" />{{RunningHeader||PREFACE|v}}</noinclude>To break family ties was a sin; to leave the people in cruel bondage was a sin; where was the right way? Justice must be done, else law would be disregarded; but how slay without sin? The answer is the burden of the book: Have no personal interest in the event; carry out the duty imposed by the position in life, realise that Ishvara, at once Lord and Law is the doer, working out the mighty evolution that ends in bliss and peace; be identified with Him by devotion, and then perform duty as duty, fighting without passion or desire, without anger or hatred; thus activity forges no bonds, Yoga is accomplished and the soul is free.

Such is the obvious teaching of this sacred book. But as all the acts of an Avatâra are symbolical, we may pass from the outer to the inner planes, and see in the fight of Kurukshetra the battlefield of the soul, and in the sons of Dhritarâshtra enemies it meets in its progress; Arjuna becomes the type of the struggling soul of the disciple, and Shrî Krishna is the Logos of the soul. Thus the teaching of the ancient battlefield gives guidance in all later days, and trains the aspiring soul in treading the steep and thorny path that leads to peace. To all such souls in East and West come these divine lessons, for the path is one, though it has many names, and all souls seek the same goal, though they may not realise their unity.

In order to preserve the precision of the Sanskrit, a few technical terms have been given in the original in foot-notes; Manah is the mind, both in the lower mental processes in which it is swayed by the senses,<noinclude></noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="4" user="EncycloPetey" />{{RunningHeader|vi|PREFACE|}}</noinclude>by passions and emotions, and in the higher processes of reasoning; Buddhi is the faculty above the ratiocinating mind, and is the Pure Reason, exercising the discriminative faculty of intuition, of spiritual discernment; if these original words are not known to the reader, the {{sc|Bhagavad-Gita}} loses much of its practical value as a treatise on Yoga, and the would-be learner becomes confused.

The epithets applied to Shrî Krishna and Arjuna—the variety of which is so characteristic of Sanskrit conversation—are for the most part left untranslated, as being musical they thus add to the literary charm, whereas the genius of English is so different from that of Sanskrit, that the many-footed epithets become sometimes almost grotesque in translation. Names derived from that of an ancestor, as Pârtha, meaning the son of Prithâ, Kaunteya, meaning the son of Kuntî, are used in one form or the other, according to the rhythm of the sentence. One other trifling matter, which is yet not trifling, if it aids the student: when Atmâ means the One Self, the {{sc|Self}} of all, it is printed in small capitals; where it means the lower, the personal self, it is printed in ordinary type; this is done because there is sometimes a play on the word, and it is difficult for an untrained reader to follow the meaning without some such assistance. The word Brahman, the {{sc|One}}, the Supreme, is throughout translated the "{{sc|Eternal}}." The word "Deva," literally "Shining One," is thus translated throughout. The use of the Western word "God" alike for "Brahman" and for the "Devas" is most misleading; the Hindu<noinclude></noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="4" user="EncycloPetey" />{{RunningHeader||PREFACE|vii}}</noinclude>never uses the one for the other, and never blurs the unity of the Supreme by the multiplicity of ministering Intelligences.

My wish, in adding this translation to those already before the public, was to preserve the spirit of the original, especially in its deeply devotional tone, while at the same time giving an accurate translation, reflecting the strength and the terseness of the Sanskrit. In order that mistakes, due to my imperfect knowledge, might be corrected, all of this translation has passed through the hands of one or other of the following gentlemen—friends of mine at Benares—to whom I here tender my grateful acknowledgments: Bâbus Pramada Das Mitra, Gangânath Jhâ, Kâli Charan Mitra, and Upendranath Basu. A few of the notes are also due to them. In the third and fourth editions I have also been much helped by Bâbu Bhagavân Dâs, to whom I add my cordial thanks.

{{c|{{larger|NOTE TO THE FIRST EDITION.}}

{{rule|3em}}}}

It has long been my ambition to place within the easy reach of the English-reading public a cheap edition of the Bhagavad-Gita with the text in Devanagari and an English translation of the same. Mrs. Annie Besant, that warm and tried friend of India whose services to our land it were vain to count, has enabled me to realise that ambition by generously granting the use of her English translation. It is devoutly hoped that this great scripture of the Hindus will find a place in thousands of homes both in India and elsewhere.


Nov. 1907. {{float right|[[Author:Ganapathi Agraharam Annadhurai Ayyar Natesan|G. A. NATESAN]]}}

FIRST DISCOURSE.}}}} {{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa| {{c|धृतराष्ट्र उवाच ।}} धर्मक्षेत्रे कुरुक्षेत्रे समवेता युयुत्सवः । मामकाः पाण्डवाश्चैव किमकुर्वत सञ्जय ॥ १ ॥ }} }} }} {{c|Dhritarâshtra said:}} On the holy plain, on the field of Kuru,The common ancestor of the contending parties, the Kurus and the Pândavas, in the impending battle. gathered together, eager for battle, what did they, O Sanjaya, my people and the Pândavas? {{float right|{{larger|(1)}}}} {{-}} {{dhr}} {{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa| {{c|सञ्जय उवाच ।}} दृष्ट्वा तु पाण्डवानीकं व्यूढं दुर्योधनस्तदा । आचार्यमुपसङ्गम्य राजा वचनमब्रवीत् ॥ २ ॥ }} }} }} {{nop}}{{rule}} {{smallrefs}}

<noinclude><pagequality level="4" user="Kdbhalerao" />{{rh|2|THE BHAGAVAD-GITA.|}}</noinclude>{{c|Sanjaya said:}}

Having seen arrayed the army of the Pândavas, the Prince Duryodhana approached his teacher,<ref>Drona, the son of Bharadvâja.</ref> and spake these words: {{float right|{{larger|(2)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
पश्यैतां पाण्डुपुत्राणामाचार्य महतीं चमूम् ।

व्यूढां द्रुपदपुत्रेण तव शिष्येण धीमता ॥ ३ ॥
}} }} }}

"Behold this mighty host of the sons of Pându, O teacher, arrayed by the son of Drupada, thy wise disciple. {{float right|{{larger|(3)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
अत्र शूरा महेष्वासा भीमार्जुनसमा युधि ।

युयुधानो विराटश्च द्रुपदश्च महारथः ॥ ४ ॥
}} }} }}

Heroes are these, mighty bowmen, to Bhîma and Arjuna equal in battle: Yuyudhâna, Virâta, and Drupada of the great car.<ref>One able to fight alone ten thousand bowmen.</ref> {{float right|{{larger|(4)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
धृष्टकेतुश्चेकितानः काशिराजश्च वीर्यवान् ।

पुरुजित्कुन्तिभोजश्च शैब्यश्च नरपुङ्गवः ॥ ५ ॥
}} }} }}
{{nop}}<noinclude>{{rule}}
{{smallrefs}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="4" user="Kdbhalerao" />{{RunningHeader||FIRST DISCOURSE.|3}}</noinclude>Drishtaketu, Chekitâna and the valiant King of Kâshi, Purujit and Kuntibhoja, and Shaivya, bull<ref>The bull, as the emblem of manly strength and vigour, is often used as an epithet of honour.</ref> among men; {{float right|{{larger|(5)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
युधामन्युश्च विक्रान्त उत्तमौजाश्च वीर्यवान् ।

सौभद्रो द्रौपदेयाश्च सर्व एव महारथाः  ॥ ६ ॥
}} }} }}

Yudhâmanyu the strong, and Uttamaujas the brave; Saubhadra<ref>Abhimanyu, the son of Subhadrâ and Arjuna.</ref> and the Draupadeyas,<ref>The sons and grandsons of Drupada.</ref> all of great cars. {{float right|{{larger|(6)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
अस्माकं तु विशिष्टा ये तान्निबोध द्विजोत्तम ।

नायका मम सैन्यस्य संज्ञार्थं तान्ब्रवीमि ते  ॥ ७ ॥
}} }} }}

Know further all those who are our chiefs, O best of the twice-born, the leaders of my army; these I name to thee for thy information: {{float right|{{larger|(7)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
भवान्भीष्मश्च कर्णश्च कृपश्च समितिञ्जयः ।

अश्वत्थामा विकर्णश्च सौमदत्तिस्तथैव च  ॥ ८ ॥
}} }} }}
{{nop}}<noinclude>{{rule}}
{{smallrefs}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="4" user="Kdbhalerao" />{{RunningHeader|4|THE BHAGAVAD-GITA.|}}</noinclude>Thou, Lord, and Bhîshma, and Karna and Kripa, conquering in battle; Ashvatthâmâ, Vikarna, and Saumadatti<ref>The son of Somadatta.</ref> also; {{float right|{{larger|(8)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
अन्ये च बहवः शूरा मदर्थे त्यक्तजीविताः ।

नानाशस्त्रप्रहरणाः सर्वे युद्धविशारदाः  ॥ ९ ॥
}} }} }}

And many others, heroes, for my sake renouncing their lives, with {{SIC|divers|diverse}} weapons and missiles, and all well-skilled in war. {{float right|{{larger|(9)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
अपर्याप्तं तदस्माकं बलं भीष्माभिरक्षितम् ।

पर्याप्तं त्विदमेतेषां बलं भीमाभिरक्षितम्  ॥ १० ॥
}} }} }}

Yet insufficient seems this army of ours, though marshalled by Bhîshma, while that army of theirs seems sufficient, though marshalled by Bhîma;<ref>The commentators differ in their interpretation of this verse; Anandagiri takes it to mean just the reverse of Shridhara Svâmi, "aparyâptam" being taken by the one as "insufficient," by the other as "unlimited." </ref> {{float right|{{larger|(10)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}<noinclude>{{rule}}
{{smallrefs}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="4" user="Kdbhalerao" />{{RunningHeader||FIRST DISCOURSE.|5}}</noinclude>{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
अयनेषु च सर्वेषु यथाभागमवस्थिताः ।

भीष्ममेवाभिरक्षन्तु भवन्तः सर्व एव हि ॥ ॥ ११ ॥
}} }} }}

Therefore in the rank and file let all, standing firmly in their respective divisions, guard Bhîshma, even all ye generals. {{float right|{{larger|(11)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
तस्य सञ्जनयन्हर्षं कुरुवृद्धः पितामहः ।

सिंहनादं विनद्योच्चैः शङ्खं दध्मौ प्रतापवान् ॥ १२ ॥
}} }} }}

To enhearten him, the Ancient of the Kurus, the Grandsire,<ref>Bhishma.</ref> the glorious, blew his conch, sounding on high a lion's roar. {{float right|{{larger|(12)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
ततः शङ्खाश्च भेर्यश्च पणवानकगोमुखाः ।

सहसैवाभ्यहन्यन्त स शब्दस्तुमुलोऽभवत् ॥ १३ ॥
}} }} }}

Then conches and kettledrums, tabors and drums and cowhorns, suddenly blared forth, and the sound was tumultuous. {{float right|{{larger|(13)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}<noinclude>{{rule}}
{{smallrefs}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="4" user="Kdbhalerao" />{{RunningHeader|6|THE BHAGAVAD-GITA.|}}</noinclude>{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
ततः श्वेतैर्हयैर्युक्ते महति स्यन्दने स्थितौ ।

माधवः पाण्डवश्चैव दिव्यौ शङ्खौ प्रदध्मतुः ॥ १४ ॥
}}}}}}

Then, stationed in their great war-chariot, yoked to white horses, Mâdhava<ref>Shri Krishna.</ref> and the son of Pându<ref>Arjuna.</ref> blew their divine conches. {{float right|{{larger|(14)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
पाञ्चजन्यं हृषीकेशो देवदत्तं धनञ्जयः ।

पौण्ड्रं दध्मौ महाशङ्खं भीमकर्मा वृकोदरः ॥ १५ ॥
}}}}}}

Pânchajanya by Hrishîkesha, and Devadatta by Dhananjaya.<ref>Pânchajanya, Shri Krishna's conch, was made from the bones of the giant Panchajana, slain by him. The title Hrishîkesha is "Lord of the senses." Dhananjaya, the "conqueror of wealth," is a title often given to Arjuna, whose conch is the "God-given."</ref> Vrikodara<ref>Bhîma; the meaning of the name of his conch is doubtful.</ref> of terrible deeds blew his mighty conch, Paundra; {{float right|{{larger|(15)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
अनन्तविजयं राजा कुन्तीपुत्रो युधिष्ठिरः ।

नकुलः सहदेवश्च सुघोषमणिपुष्पकौ ॥ १६ ॥
}}}}}}
{{nop}}<noinclude>{{rule}}
{{smallrefs}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="4" user="Kdbhalerao" />{{RunningHeader||FIRST DISCOURSE.|7}}</noinclude>The King Yudhishthira, the son of Kuntî, blew Anantavijaya; Nakula and Sahadeva, Sughosha and Manipushpaka.<ref>The conches of the remaining three brothers were named respectively "endless victory," "honey-tone," and "jewel-blossom."</ref> {{float right|{{larger|(16)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
काश्यश्च परमेष्वासः शिखण्डी च महारथः ।

धृष्टद्युम्नो विराटश्च सात्यकिश्चापराजितः ॥ १७ ॥
}} }} }}

And Kâshya,<ref>The King of Kâshi, the modern Benares.</ref> of the great bow and Shikhandî, the mighty car-warrior, {{SIC|Drishtadyumna|Dhrishtadyumna}} and Virâta and Sâtyaki, the unconquered. {{float right|{{larger|(17)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
द्रुपदो द्रौपदेयाश्च सर्वशः पृथिवीपते ।

सौभद्रश्च महाबाहुः शङ्खान्दध्मुः पृथक्पृथक् ॥ १८ ॥
}} }} }}

Drupada and the Draupadeyas, O Lord of earth, and Saubhadra, the mighty-armed, on all sides their several conches blew. {{float right|{{larger|(18)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
स घोषो धार्तराष्ट्राणां हृदयानि व्यदारयत् ।

नभश्च पृथिवीं चैव तुमुलो व्यनुनादयन् ॥ १९ ॥ 
}} }} }}

<noinclude><pagequality level="4" user="Kdbhalerao" />{{RunningHeader|8|THE BHAGAVAD-GITA.|}}</noinclude>That tumultuous uproar rent the hearts of the sons of Dhritarâshtra, filling the earth and sky with sound. {{float right|{{larger|(19)}}}}

{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
अथ व्यवस्थितान्दृष्ट्वा धार्तराष्ट्रान्कपिध्वजः ।

प्रवृत्ते शस्त्रसम्पाते धनुरुद्यम्य पाण्डवः ॥ २० ॥
}} }} }}

Then, beholding the sons of Dhritarâshtra standing arrayed, and flight of missiles about to begin, he whose crest is an ape, the son of Pându, took up his bow, {{float right|{{larger|(20)}}}}

{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
हृषीकेशं तदा वाक्यमिदमाह महीपते ।

{{c|अर्जुन उवाच ।}}

सेनयोरुभयोर्मध्ये रथं स्थापय मेऽच्युत ॥ २१ ॥
}} }} }}

And spake this word to Hrishîkesha, O Lord of Earth:

{{c|Arjuna said:}}

In the midst, between the two armies, stay my chariot, O Achyuta,<ref>The changeless, the immovable.</ref> {{float right|{{larger|(21)}}}}
{{-}}

{{smallrefs}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="4" user="Kdbhalerao" />{{RunningHeader||FIRST DISCOURSE.|9}}</noinclude>{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
यावदेतान्निरीक्षेऽहं योद्‌धुकामानवस्थितान् ।

कैर्मया सह योद्धव्यमस्मिन्रणसमुद्यमे ॥ २२ ॥
}} }} }}

That I may behold these standing, longing for battle, with whom I must strive in this outbreaking war, {{float right|{{larger|(22)}}}}
{{-}}

Then Hrishîkesha, smiling, as it were, O Bhârata, spake these words to him, despondent, in the midst of the two armies: {{float right|{{larger|(10)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
{{c|श्रीभगवानुवाच ।}}

अशोच्यानन्वशोचस्त्वं प्रज्ञावादांश्च भाषसे ।

गतासूनगतासूंश्च नानुशोचन्ति पण्डिताः ॥ ११ ॥
}} }} }}

{{c|The Blessed Lord said:}}

Thou grievest for those that should not be griev-<noinclude></noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader||SECOND DISCOURSE.|23}}</noinclude>ed for, yet speakest words of wisdom.<ref>Words that sound wise, but miss the deeper sense of wisdom.</ref> The wise grieve neither for the living nor for the dead. {{float right|{{larger|(11)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
न त्वेवाहं जातु नासं न त्वं नेमे जनाधिपाः ।

न चैव न भविष्यामः सर्वे वयमतः परम् ॥ १२ ॥
}} }} }}

Nor at any time verily was I not, nor thou, nor these princes of men, nor verily shall we ever cease to be, hereafter. {{float right|{{larger|(12)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
देहिनोऽस्मिन्यथा देहे कौमारं यौवनं जरा ।

तथा देहान्तरप्राप्तिर्धीरस्तत्र न मुह्यति ॥ १३ ॥
}} }} }}

As the dweller in the body experienceth in the body childhood, youth, old age, so passeth he on to another body; the steadfast one grieveth not thereat. {{float right|{{larger|(13)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
मात्रास्पर्शास्तु कौन्तेय शीतोष्णसुखदुःखदाः ।

आगमापायिनोऽनित्यास्तांस्तितिक्षस्व भारत ॥ १४ ॥
}} }} }}
{{nop}}<noinclude>{{rule}}
{{smallrefs}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader|24|THE BHAGAVAD-GITA.|}}</noinclude>The contacts of matter, O son of Kuntî, giving cold and heat, pleasure and pain, they come and go, impermanent; endure them bravely, O Bhârata. {{float right|{{larger|(14)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
यं हि न व्यथयन्त्येते पुरुषं पुरुषर्षभ ।

समदुःखसुखं धीरं सोऽमृतत्वाय कल्पते ॥ १५ ॥
}} }} }}

The man whom these torment not, O chief of men, balanced in pain and pleasure, steadfast, he is fitted for immortality. {{float right|{{larger|(15)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
नासतो विद्यते भावो नाभावो विद्यते सतः ।

उभयोरपि दृष्टोऽन्तस्त्वनयोस्तत्त्वदर्शिभिः ॥ १६ ॥
}} }} }}

The unreal hath no being; the real never ceaseth to be; the truth about both hath been perceived by the seers of the essence of things.<ref>Tattva.</ref>  {{float right|{{larger|(16)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
अविनाशि तु तद्विद्धि येन सर्वमिदं ततम् ।

विनाशमव्ययस्यास्य न कश्चित्कर्तुमर्हति ॥ १७ ॥
}} }} }}
{{nop}}<noinclude>{{rule}}
{{smallrefs}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader||SECOND DISCOURSE.|25}}</noinclude>Know {{small-caps|That}} to be indestructible by whom all this is pervaded. Nor can any work the destruction of that imperishable One. {{float right|{{larger|(17)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
अन्तवन्त इमे देहा नित्यस्योक्ताः शरीरिणः ।

अनाशिनोऽप्रमेयस्य तस्माद्युध्यस्व भारत ॥ १८ ॥
}} }} }}

These bodies of the embodied One, who is eternal, indestructible and immeasurable, are known as finite. Therefore fight, O Bhârata. {{float right|{{larger|(18)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
य एनं वेत्ति हन्तारं यश्चैनं मन्यते हतम् ।

उभौ तौ न विजानीतो नायं हन्ति न हन्यते ॥ १९ ॥
}} }} }}

He who regardeth this<ref>The dweller in the body.</ref> as a slayer, and he who thinketh he is slain, both of them are ignorant. He slayeth not, nor is he slain. {{float right|{{larger|(19)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
न जायते म्रियते वा कदाचिन्नायं भूत्वा भविता वा न भूयः ।

अजो नित्यः शाश्वतोऽयं पुराणो न हन्यते हन्यमाने शरीरे ॥ २० ॥
}} }} }}
{{nop}}<noinclude>{{rule}}
{{smallrefs}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader|26|THE BHAGAVAD-GITA.|}}</noinclude>He is not born, nor doth he die; nor having been, ceaseth he any more to be; unborn, perpetual, eternal and ancient, he is not slain when the body is slaughtered. {{float right|{{larger|(20)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
वेदाऽविनाशिनं नित्यं य एनमजमव्ययम् ।

कथं स पुरुषः पार्थ कं घातयति हन्ति कम् ॥ २१ ॥
}} }} }}

Who knoweth him indestructible, perpetual, unborn, undiminishing, how can that man slay, O Pârtha, or cause to be slain? {{float right|{{larger|(21)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
वासांसि जीर्णानि यथा विहाय नवानि गृह्णाति नरोऽपराणि ।

तथा शरीराणि विहाय जीर्णान्यन्यानि संयाति नवानि देही ॥ २२ ॥
}} }} }}

As a man, casting off worn-out garments, taketh new ones, so the dweller in the body, casting off worn-out bodies, entereth into others that are new. {{float right|{{larger|(22)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}<noinclude></noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader||SECOND DISCOURSE.|27}}</noinclude>{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
नैनं छिन्दन्ति शस्त्राणि नैनं दहति पावकः ।

न चैनं क्लेदयन्त्यापो न शोषयति मारुतः ॥ २३ ॥
}} }} }}

Weapons cleave him not, nor fire burneth him, nor waters wet him, nor wind drieth him away. {{float right|{{larger|(23)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
अच्छेद्योऽयमदाह्योऽयमक्लेद्योऽशोष्य एव च ।

नित्यः सर्वगतः स्थाणुरचलोऽयं सनातनः ॥ २४ ॥
}} }} }}

Uncleavable he, incombustible he, and indeed neither to be wetted nor dried away; perpetual, all-pervasive, stable, immovable, ancient. {{float right|{{larger|(24)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
अव्यक्तोऽयमचिन्त्योऽयमविकार्योऽयमुच्यते ।

तस्मादेवं विदित्वैनं नानुशोचितुमर्हसि ॥ २५ ॥
}} }} }}

Unmanifest, unthinkable, immutable, he is called; therefore knowing him as such, thou shouldst not grieve. {{float right|{{larger|(25)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
अथ चैनं नित्यजातं नित्यं वा मन्यसे मृतम् ।

तथापि त्वं महाबाहो नैनं शोचितुमर्हसि ॥ २६ ॥
}} }} }}

Or if thou thinkest of him as being constantly<noinclude></noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader|28|THE BHAGAVAD-GITA.|}}</noinclude>born and constantly dying, even then, O mighty-armed, thou shouldst not grieve. {{float right|{{larger|(26)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
जातस्य हि ध्रुवो मृत्युर्ध्रुवं जन्म मृतस्य च ।

तस्मादपरिहार्येऽर्थे न त्वं शोचितुमर्हसि ॥ २७ ॥
}} }} }}

For certain is death for the born, and certain is birth for the dead; therefore over the inevitable thou shouldst not grieve. {{float right|{{larger|(27)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
अव्यक्तादीनि भूतानि व्यक्तमध्यानि भारत ।

अव्यक्तनिधनान्येव तत्र का परिदेवना ॥ २८ ॥
}} }} }}

Beings are unmanifest in their origin, manifest in their midmost state, O Bhârata, unmanifest likewise are they in dissolution. What room then for lamentation? {{float right|{{larger|(28)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
आश्चर्यवत्पश्यति कश्चिदेनमाश्चर्यवद्वदति तथैव चान्यः ।

आश्चर्यवच्चैनमन्यः शृणोति श्रुत्वाऽप्येनं वेद न चैव कश्चित् ॥ २९ ॥
}} }} }}
{{nop}}<noinclude></noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader||SECOND DISCOURSE.|29}}</noinclude>As marvellous one regardeth him; as marvellous another speaketh thereof; as marvellous another heareth thereof; yet having heard none indeed understandeth. {{float right|{{larger|(29)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
देही नित्यमवध्योऽयं देहे सर्वस्य भारत ।

तस्मात्सर्वाणि भूतानि न त्वं शोचितुमर्हसि ॥ ३० ॥
}} }} }}
 
This dweller in the body of everyone is ever invulnerable, O Bhârata; therefore thou shouldst not grieve for any creature. {{float right|{{larger|(30)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
स्वधर्ममपि चावेक्ष्य न विकम्पितुमर्हसि ।

धर्म्याद्धि युद्धाच्छ्रेयोऽन्यत्क्षत्रियस्य न विद्यते ॥ ३१ ॥
}} }} }}

Further, looking to thine own duty<ref>Dharma.</ref> thou shouldst not tremble; for there is nothing more welcome to a Kshattriya<ref>A person of the second, the warrior, caste.</ref> than righteous war. {{float right|{{larger|(31)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
यदृच्छया चोपपन्नं स्वर्गद्वारमपावृतम् ।

सुखिनः क्षत्रियाः पार्थ लभन्ते युद्धमीदृशम् ॥ ३२ ॥
}} }} }}
{{nop}}<noinclude>{{rule}}
{{smallrefs}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader|30|THE BHAGAVAD-GITA.|}}</noinclude>Happy the Kshattriyas, O Pârtha, who obtain such a fight, offered unsought as an open door to heaven. {{float right|{{larger|(32)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
अथ चेत्त्वमिमं धर्म्यं सङ्ग्रामं न करिष्यसि ।

ततः स्वधर्मं कीर्तिं च हित्वा पापमवाप्स्यसि ॥ ३३ ॥
}} }} }}

But if thou wilt not carry on this righteous warfare, then casting away thine own duty<ref>Dharma.</ref> and thine honour, thou wilt incur sin. {{float right|{{larger|(33)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
अकीर्तिं चापि भूतानि कथयिष्यन्ति तेऽव्ययाम् ।

सम्भावितस्य चाकीर्तिर्मरणादतिरिच्यते ॥ ३४ ॥
}} }} }}

Men will recount thy perpetual dishonour, and, to one highly esteemed, dishonour exceedeth death. {{float right|{{larger|(34)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
भयाद्रणादुपरतं मंस्यन्ते त्वां महारथाः ।

येषां च त्वं बहुमतो भूत्वा यास्यसि लाघवम् ॥ ३५ ॥
}} }} }}

The great car-warriors<ref>The generals.</ref> will think thee fled from<noinclude>{{rule}}
{{smallrefs}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader||SECOND DISCOURSE.|31}}</noinclude>the battle from fear, and thou, that wast highly thought of by them, wilt be lightly held. {{float right|{{larger|(35)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
अवाच्यवादांश्च बहून्वदिष्यन्ति तवाहिताः ।

निन्दन्तस्तव सामर्थ्यं ततो दुःखतरं नु किम् ॥ ३६ ॥
}} }} }}

Many unseemly words will be spoken by thine enemies, slandering thy strength; what more painful than that? {{float right|{{larger|(36)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
हतो वा प्राप्स्यसि स्वर्गं जित्वा वा भोक्ष्यसे महीम् ।

तस्मादुत्तिष्ठ कौन्तेय युद्धाय कृतनिश्चयः ॥ ३७ ॥
}} }} }}

Slain, thou wilt obtain heaven; victorious, thou wilt enjoy the earth; therefore stand up, O son of Kuntî, resolute to fight. {{float right|{{larger|(37)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
सुखदुःखे समे कृत्वा लाभालाभौ जयाजयौ ।

ततो युद्धाय युज्यस्व नैवं पापमवाप्स्यसि ॥ ३८ ॥
}} }} }}

Taking as equal pleasure and pain, gain and loss, victory and defeat, gird thee for the battle; thus thou shalt not incur sin. {{float right|{{larger|(38)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}<noinclude></noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader|32|THE BHAGAVAD-GITA.|}}</noinclude>{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
एषा तेऽभिहिता साङ्ख्ये बुद्धिर्योगे त्विमां शृणु ।

बुद्ध्या युक्तो यया पार्थ कर्मबन्धं प्रहास्यसि ॥ ३९ ॥
}} }} }}

This teaching set forth to thee is in accordance with the [[w:Samkhya|Sâñkhya]]<ref>One of the six systems of Indian philosophy dealing with evolution.</ref>; hear it now according to the Yoga<ref>Another of the same systems, dealing with meditation.</ref>, imbued with which teaching, O Pârtha, thou shalt cast away the bonds of action. {{float right|{{larger|(39)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
नेहाभिक्रमनाशोऽस्ति प्रत्यवायो न विद्यते ।

स्वल्पमप्यस्य धर्मस्य त्रायते महतो भयात् ॥ ४० ॥
}} }} }}

In this there is no loss of effort, nor is there transgression. Even a little of this knowledge<ref>Dharma.</ref> protects from great fear. {{float right|{{larger|(40)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
{{SIC|व्ययसायात्मिका|व्यवसायात्मिका}} बुद्धिरेकेह कुरुनन्दन ।

बहुशाखा ह्यनन्ताश्च बुद्धयोऽव्यवसायिनाम् ॥ ४१ ॥
}} }} }}

The determinate Reason<ref>Buddhi.</ref> is but one-pointed,<noinclude>{{rule}}
{{smallrefs}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader||SECOND DISCOURSE.|33}}</noinclude>O joy of the Kurus; many-branched and endless are the thoughts of the irresolute. {{float right|{{larger|(41)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
यामिमां पुष्पितां वाचं प्रवदन्त्यविपश्चितः ।

वेदवादरताः पार्थ नान्यदस्तीति वादिनः ॥ ४२ ॥
}} }} }}

Flowery speech is uttered by the foolish, rejoicing in the letter of the Vedas,<ref>The Hindu Scriptures.</ref> O Pârtha, saying: "There is naught but this"; {{float right|{{larger|(42)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
कामात्मानः स्वर्गपरा जन्मकर्मफलप्रदाम् ।

क्रियाविशेषबहुलां भोगैश्वर्यगतिं प्रति ॥ ४३ ॥
}} }} }}

With desire for self<ref>Those whose very self is desire, Kâma, and who therefore act with a view to win heaven and also rebirth to wealth and rank.</ref>, with heaven for goal, they offer birth as the fruit of action, and prescribe many and various ceremonies for the attainment of pleasure and lordship. {{float right|{{larger|(43)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
भोगैश्वर्यप्रसक्तानां तयाऽपहृतचेतसाम् ।

व्यवसायात्मिका बुद्धिः समाधौ न विधीयते ॥ ४४ ॥
}} }} }}
{{nop}}<noinclude>{{rule}}
{{smallrefs}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader|34|THE BHAGAVAD-GITA.|}}</noinclude>For them who cling to pleasure and lordship, whose minds are captivated by such teaching, is not designed this determinate Reason,<ref>Buddhi.</ref> on contemplation<ref>Samadhi, the third state of consciousness in meditation.</ref> steadily bent.<ref>The following alternative translation of Slokas 42, 43, and 44 is offered: "The flowery speech that the unwise utter, O Pârtha, clinging to the word of the Veda, saying there is nothing else, ensouled by desire and longing after heaven, (the speech) that offereth only rebirth as the (ultimate) fruit of action, that is full of (recommendations to) various rites for the sake of (gaining) enjoyments and sovereignty—the thought of those misled by that (speech), cleaving to pleasures and lordship, not being inspired with resolution, is not engaged in contemplation." This is closer to the original, which is all in one sentence.</ref> {{float right|{{larger|(44)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
त्रैगुण्यविषया वेदा निस्त्रैगुण्यो भवार्जुन ।

निर्द्वन्द्वो नित्यसत्त्वस्थो निर्योगक्षेम आत्मवान् ॥ ४५ ॥
}} }} }}

The Vedas deal with the three attributes<ref>Gunas = attributes, or forms of energy. They are sattva, rhythm, harmony, or purity; rajas, motion, activity, or passion; tamas, inertia, darkness, or stupidity.</ref>; be<noinclude>{{rule}}
{{smallrefs}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader||SECOND DISCOURSE.|35}}</noinclude>thou above these three attributes, O Arjuna; beyond the pairs of opposites, ever steadfast in purity,<ref>Sattva.</ref> careless of possessions, full of the {{sc|Self}}. {{float right|{{larger|(45)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
यावानर्थ उदपाने सर्वतः सम्प्लुतोदके ।

तावान्सर्वेषु वेदेषु ब्राह्मणस्य विजानतः ॥ ४६ ॥
}} }} }}

All the Vedas are as useful to an enlightened Brâhmana<ref>A person of the highest, the priestly and teaching caste.</ref> as is a tank in a place covered all over with water. {{float right|{{larger|(46)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
कर्मण्येवाधिकारस्ते मा फलेषु कदाचन ।

मा कर्मफलहेतुर्भूर्मा ते सङ्गोऽस्त्वकर्मणि ॥ ४७ ॥
}} }} }}

Thy business is with the action only, never with its fruits; so let not the fruit of action be thy motive, nor be thou to inaction attached. {{float right|{{larger|(47)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
योगस्थः कुरु कर्माणि सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा धनञ्जय ।

सिद्ध्यसिद्ध्योः समो भूत्वा समत्वं योग उच्यते ॥ ४८ ॥
}} }} }}
{{nop}}<noinclude>{{rule}}
{{smallrefs}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader|36|THE BHAGAVAD-GITA.|}}</noinclude>Perform action, O Dhananjaya, dwelling in union with the divine,<ref>Dwelling in yoga, union.</ref> renouncing attachments and balanced evenly in success and failure: equilibrium is called yoga. {{float right|{{larger|(48)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
दूरेण ह्यवरं कर्म बुद्धियोगाद्धनञ्जय ।

बुद्धौ शरणमन्विच्छ कृपणाः फलहेतवः ॥ ४९ ॥
}} }} }}

Far lower than the Yoga of Discrimination<ref>Union with Buddhi, the innermost sheath (or vehicle) of Atma.</ref> is action, O Dhananjaya. Take thou refuge in the Pure Reason<ref name="p36Buddhi">Buddhi.</ref>; pitiable are they who work for fruit. {{float right|{{larger|(49)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
बुद्धियुक्तो जहातीह उभे सुकृतदुष्कृते ।

तस्माद्योगाय युज्यस्व योगः कर्मसु कौशलम् ॥ ५० ॥
}} }} }}

United to the Pure Reason<ref name="p36Buddhi" /> one abandoneth here both good and evil deeds; therefore cleave thou to yoga; yoga is skill in action. {{float right|{{larger|(50)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
कर्मजं बुद्धियुक्ता हि फलं त्यक्त्वा मनीषिणः ।

जन्मबन्धविनिर्मुक्ताः पदं गच्छन्त्यनामयम् ॥ ५१ ॥
}} }} }}

The Sages, united to the Pure Reason<ref name="p36Buddhi" />,<noinclude>{{rule}}
{{smallrefs}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader||SECOND DISCOURSE.|37}}</noinclude>renounce the fruit which action yieldeth, and, liberated from the bonds of birth, they go to the blissful seat. {{float right|{{larger|(51)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
यदा ते मोहकलिलं बुद्धिर्व्यतितरिष्यति ।

तदा गन्तासि निर्वेदं श्रोतव्यस्य श्रुतस्य च ॥ ५२ ॥
}} }} }}

When thy mind<ref name="p37Buddhi">Buddhi.</ref> shall escape from this tangle of delusion, then thou shalt rise to indifference as to what has been heard and shall be heard. {{float right|{{larger|(52)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
श्रुतिविप्रतिपन्ना ते यदा स्थास्यति निश्चला ।

समाधावचला बुद्धिस्तदा योगमवाप्स्यसि ॥ ५३ ॥
}} }} }}

When thy mind<ref name="p37Buddhi" />, bewildered by the Scriptures<ref>Sruti.</ref>, shall stand immovable, fixed in contemplation, then shalt thou attain unto yoga<ref>To union with Atma, the {{small-caps|Self}}; yoga implies harmony with the divine will. The word translated contemplation is, as before, Samâdhi.</ref>. {{float right|{{larger|(53)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center/s}}{{larger block/s}}{{lang block|sa|
{{c|अर्जुन उवाच ।}}

स्थितप्रज्ञस्य का भाषा समाधिस्थस्य केशव ।

{{smallrefs}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader|38|THE BHAGAVAD-GITA.|}}
{{block center/s}}{{larger block/s}}</noinclude>{{lang block|sa|

}} {{larger block/e}} {{block center/e}}

{{c|Arjuna said:}}

What the mark, of him who is stable of mind,<ref name="p38Prajna">Prajnâ.</ref> steadfast in contemplation, O Keshava? How doth the stable-minded<ref>Dhî.</ref> talk, how doth he sit, how walk? {{float right|{{larger|(54)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
{{c|श्रीभगवानुवाच ।}}

प्रजहाति यदा कामान्सर्वान्पार्थ मनोगतान् ।

आत्मन्येवात्मना तुष्टः स्थितप्रज्ञस्तदोच्यते ॥ ५५ ॥
}} }} }}

{{c|The Blessed Lord said:}}

When a man abandoneth, O Pârtha, all the desires of the heart<ref>Manah.</ref>, and is satisfied in the {{sc|Self}} by the {{sc|Self}}, then is he called stable in mind<ref>Prajnâ.</ref>. {{float right|{{larger|(55)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
दुःखेष्वनुद्विग्नमनाः सुखेषु विगतस्पृहः ।

वीतरागभयक्रोधः स्थितधीर्मुनिरुच्यते ॥ ५६ ॥
}} }} }}

He whose mind<ref name="p38Prajna" /> is free from anxiety amid pains, indifferent amid pleasures, loosed from<noinclude>{{rule}}
{{smallrefs}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader||SECOND DISCOURSE.|39}}</noinclude>passion, fear and anger, is called a sage<ref>A Muni, ''i.e.'', a saint or ascetic: in its original meaning, one who observed the vow of silence.</ref> of stable mind.<ref>Dhî.</ref> {{float right|{{larger|(56)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
यः सर्वत्रानभिस्नेहस्तत्तत्प्राप्य शुभाशुभम् ।

नाभिनन्दति न द्वेष्टि तस्य प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठिता ॥ ५७ ॥
}} }} }}

He who on every side is without attachments, whatever hap of fair and foul, who neither likes nor dislikes, of such a one the understanding<ref name="p39Prajna">Prajnâ.</ref> is well poised. {{float right|{{larger|(57)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
यदा संहरते चायं कूर्मोऽङ्गानीव सर्वशः ।

इन्द्रियाणीन्द्रियार्थेभ्यस्तस्य प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठिता ॥ ५८ ॥
}} }} }}

When, again, as a tortoise draws in on all sides its limbs, he withdraws his senses from the objects of sense, then is his understanding<ref name="p39Prajna" /> well poised. {{float right|{{larger|(58)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
विषया विनिवर्तन्ते निराहारस्य देहिनः ।

रसवर्जं रसोऽप्यस्य परं दृष्ट्वा निवर्तते ॥ ५९ ॥
}} }} }}
{{nop}}<noinclude>{{rule}}
{{smallrefs}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader|40|THE BHAGAVAD-GITA.|}}</noinclude>The objects of sense, but not the relish for them,<ref>The objects turn away when rejected, but still desire for them remains; even desire is lost when the Supreme is seen.</ref> turn away from an abstemious dweller in the body; and even relish turneth away from him after the Supreme is seen. {{float right|{{larger|(59)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
यततो ह्यपि कौन्तेय पुरुषस्य विपश्चितः ।

इन्द्रियाणि प्रमाथीनि हरन्ति प्रसभं मनः ॥ ६० ॥
}} }} }}

O son of Kuntî, the excited senses of even a wise man, though he be striving, impetuously carry away his mind<ref>Manah.</ref>. {{float right|{{larger|(60)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
तानि सर्वाणि संयम्य युक्त आसीत मत्परः ।

वशे हि यस्येन्द्रियाणि तस्य प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठिता ॥ ६१ ॥
}} }} }}

Having restrained them all, he should sit harmonised, I his supreme goal; for, whose senses are mastered, of him the understanding<ref>Prajnâ.</ref> is well poised. {{float right|{{larger|(61)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}<noinclude>{{rule}}
{{smallrefs}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader||SECOND DISCOURSE.|41}}</noinclude>{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
ध्यायतो विषयान्पुंसः सङ्गस्तेषूपजायते ।

सङ्गात्सञ्जायते कामः कामात्क्रोधोऽभिजायते ॥ ६२ ॥
}} }} }}

Man, musing on the objects of sense, conceiveth an attachment to these; from attachment ariseth desire; from desire anger<ref>Krodha.</ref> cometh forth; {{float right|{{larger|(62)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
क्रोधाद्भवति सम्मोहः सम्मोहात्स्मृतिविभ्रमः ।

स्मृतिभ्रंशाद्बुद्धिनाशो बुद्धिनाशात्प्रणश्यति ॥ ६३ ॥
}} }} }}

From anger proceedeth delusion; from delusion confused memory; from confused memory the destruction of Reason<ref>Buddhi here implying specially Discrimination.</ref>; from destruction of Reason he perishes. {{float right|{{larger|(63)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
{{SIC|रागद्वेषवियुक्तैस्तुं|रागद्वेषवियुक्तैस्तु}} विषयानिन्द्रियैश्चरन् ।

आत्मवश्यैर्विधेयात्मा प्रसादमधिगच्छति ॥ ६४ ॥
}} }} }}

But the disciplined self, moving among sense-objects with senses free from attraction and repulsion, mastered by the Self, goeth to peace. {{float right|{{larger|(64)}}}}

{{dhr}}<noinclude>{{rule}}
{{smallrefs}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader|42|THE BHAGAVAD-GITA.|}}</noinclude>{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
प्रसादे सर्वदुःखानां हानिरस्योपजायते ।

प्रसन्नचेतसो ह्याशु बुद्धिः पर्यवतिष्ठते ॥ ६५ ॥
}} }} }}

In that Peace the extinction of all pains ariseth for him, for of him whose heart<ref>Chetah.</ref> is peaceful the Reason<ref>Buddhi.</ref> soon attaineth equilibrium. {{float right|{{larger|(65)}}}}

{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
नास्ति बुद्धिरयुक्तस्य न चायुक्तस्य भावना ।

न चाभावयतः शान्तिरशान्तस्य कुतः सुखम् ॥ ६६ ॥
}} }} }}

There is no Pure Reason for the non-harmonised, nor for the non-harmonised is there concentration<ref>Bhâvanâ.</ref>; for him without concentration there is no peace, and for the unpeaceful how can there be happiness? {{float right|{{larger|(66)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
इन्द्रियाणां हि चरतां यन्मनोऽनु विधीयते ।

तदस्य हरति प्रज्ञां वायुर्नावमिवाम्भसि ॥ ६७ ॥
}} }} }}

Such of the roving senses as the mind<ref>Manah.</ref> yieldeth to, that hurries away the understanding<ref>Prajnâ.</ref>, just<noinclude>{{rule}}
{{smallrefs}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader||SECOND DISCOURSE.|43}}</noinclude>as the gale hurries away a ship upon the waters. {{float right|{{larger|(67)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
तस्माद्यस्य महाबाहो निगृहीतानि सर्वशः ।

इन्द्रियाणीन्द्रियार्थेभ्यस्तस्य प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठिता ॥ ६८ ॥
}} }} }}

Therefore, O mighty-armed, whose senses are all completely restrained from the objects of sense, of him the understanding is well poised. {{float right|{{larger|(68)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
या निशा सर्वभूतानां तस्यां जागर्ति संयमी ।

यस्यां जाग्रति भूतानि सा निशा पश्यतो मुनेः ॥ ६९ ॥
}} }} }}
 
That which is the night of all beings, for the disciplined man is the time of waking; when other beings are waking, then is it night for the sage who seeth<ref>The sage is awake to things over which the ordinary man sleeps and the eyes of the sage are open to truths shut out from the common vision, while ''vice versa'' that which is real for the masses is illusion for the sage.</ref>. {{float right|{{larger|(69)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center/s}}{{larger block/s}}{{lang block|sa|
आपूर्यमाणमचलप्रतिष्ठं समुद्रमापः प्रविशन्ति यद्वत् ।
}}<noinclude>{{larger block/e}} {{block center/e}}
{{rule}}
{{smallrefs}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader|44|THE BHAGAVAD-GITA.|}}
{{block center/s}}{{larger block/s}}</noinclude>{{lang block|sa|
तद्वत्कामा यं प्रविशन्ति सर्वे स शान्तिमाप्नोति न कामकामी ॥ ७० ॥
}} {{larger block/e}} {{block center/e}}

He attaineth Peace, into whom all desires flow as rivers flow into the ocean, which is filled with water, but remaineth unmoved—not he who desireth desires. {{float right|{{larger|(70)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
विहाय कामान्यः सर्वान्पुमांश्चरति निःस्पृहः ।

निर्ममो निरहङ्कारः स शान्तिमधिगच्छति ॥ ७१ ॥
}} }} }}

Whoso forsaketh all desires and goeth onwards free from yearnings, selfless and without egoism—he goeth to Peace. {{float right|{{larger|(71)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
एषा ब्राह्मी स्थितिः पार्थ नैनां प्राप्य विमुह्यति ।

स्थित्वाऽस्यामन्तकालेऽपि ब्रह्म निर्वाणमृच्छति ॥ ७२ ॥
}} }} }}

This is the {{sc|Eternal}} state, O son of Prithâ. Having attained thereto, none is bewildered. Who, even at the death-hour, is established therein, he goeth to the Nirvâna of the {{sc|Eternal}}. {{float right|{{larger|(72)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}<noinclude></noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader||SECOND DISCOURSE.|45}}</noinclude>{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
इति श्रीमद्भगवद्गीता॰ साङ्ख्ययोगो नाम द्वितीयोऽध्यायः ॥
}} }} }}

{{fine block|Thus in the glorious Upanishads of the {{sc|Bhagavad-Gita}}, the science of the {{small-caps|Eternal}}, the scripture of Yoga, the dialogue between Sri Krishna and Arjuna, the second discourse, entitled:}}

{{c|YOGA BY THE SANKHYA.}}

{{nop}}<noinclude></noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" /></noinclude>{{dhr}}
{{c|{{larger|THIRD DISCOURSE.}}}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
{{c|अर्जुन उवाच ।}}

ज्यायसी चेत्कर्मणस्ते मता बुद्धिर्जनार्दन ।

तत्किं कर्मणि घोरे मां नियोजयसि केशव ॥ १ ॥
}} }} }}

{{c|Arjuna said:}}

If it be thought by Thee that knowledge is superior to action, O Janârdana, why dost Thou, O Keshava, enjoin on me this terrible action? {{float right|{{larger|(1)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
व्यामिश्रेणेव वाक्येन बुद्धिं मोहयसीव मे ।

तदेकं वद निश्चित्य येन श्रेयोऽहमाप्नुयाम् ॥ २ ॥
}} }} }}

With these perplexing words Thou only confusest my understanding<ref>Buddhi.</ref>; therefore tell me with certainty the one way by which I may reach bliss. {{float right|{{larger|(2)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
{{c|श्रीभगवानुवाच ।}}

लोकेऽस्मिन्द्विविधा निष्ठा पुरा प्रोक्ता मयाऽनघ ।

ज्ञानयोगेन साङ्ख्यानां कर्मयोगेन योगिनाम् ॥ ३ ॥
}} }} }}
{{nop}}<noinclude>{{rule}}
{{smallrefs}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader||THIRD DISCOURSE.|47}}</noinclude>{{c|The Blessed Lord said:}}

In this world there is a twofold path, as I before said, O sinless one: that of yoga by knowledge, of the Sâñkhyas; and that of yoga by action, of the Yogis. {{float right|{{larger|(3)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
न कर्मणामनारम्भान्नैष्कर्म्यं पुरुषोऽश्नुते ।

न च संन्यसनादेव सिद्धिं समधिगच्छति ॥ ४ ॥
}} }} }}

Man winneth not freedom from action by abstaining from activity, nor by mere renunciation doth he rise to perfection. {{float right|{{larger|(4)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
न हि कश्चित्क्षणमपि जातु तिष्ठत्यकर्मकृत् ।

कार्यते ह्यवशः कर्म सर्वः प्रकृतिजैर्गुणैः ॥ ५ ॥
}} }} }}

Nor can anyone, even for an instant, remain really actionless; for helplessly is everyone driven to action by the qualities<ref>Gunas.</ref> born of nature<ref>Prakriti.</ref>. {{float right|{{larger|(5)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
कर्मेन्द्रियाणि संयम्य य आस्ते मनसा स्मरन् ।

इन्द्रियार्थान्विमूढात्मा मिथ्याचारः स उच्यते ॥ ६ ॥
}} }} }}
{{nop}}<noinclude>{{rule}}
{{smallrefs}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader|48|THE BHAGAVAD-GITA.|}}</noinclude>Who sitteth, controlling the organs of action, but dwelling in his mind<ref name="p48Manah">Manah.</ref> on the objects of the senses, that bewildered man is called a hypocrite. {{float right|{{larger|(6)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
यस्त्विन्द्रियाणि मनसा नियम्यारभतेऽर्जुन ।

कर्मेन्द्रियैः कर्मयोगमसक्तः स विशिष्यते ॥ ७ ॥
}} }} }}

But who, controlling the senses by the mind<ref name="p48Manah" />, O Arjuna, with the organs of action without attachment, performeth yoga by action<ref>Karma-Yoga is the consecration of physical energy on the divine Altar; ''i.e.'', the using of one's organs of action simply in service, in obedience to Law and Duty.</ref>, he is worthy. {{float right|{{larger|(7)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
नियतं कुरु कर्म त्वं कर्म ज्यायो ह्यकर्मणः ।

शरीरयात्राऽपि च ते न {{SIC|प्रसिध्येदकर्मणः|प्रसिद्ध्येदकर्मणः}} ॥ ८ ॥
}} }} }}

Perform thou right<ref>Regulated, prescribed as a duty; or, regularly.</ref> action, for, action is superior to inaction, and, inactive, even the maintenance of thy body would not be possible. {{float right|{{larger|(8)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}<noinclude>{{rule}}
{{smallrefs}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader||THIRD DISCOURSE.|49}}</noinclude>{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
यज्ञार्थात्कर्मणोऽन्यत्र लोकोऽयं कर्मबन्धनः ।

तदर्थं कर्म कौन्तेय मुक्तसङ्गः समाचर ॥ ९ ॥
}} }} }}

The world is bound by action, unless performed for the sake of sacrifice; for that sake, free from attachment, O son of Kuntî, perform thou action. {{float right|{{larger|(9)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
सहयज्ञाः प्रजाः सृष्ट्वा पुरोवाच प्रजापतिः ।

अनेन प्रसविष्यध्वमेष वोऽस्त्विष्टकामधुक् ॥ १० ॥
}} }} }}

Having in ancient times emanated mankind together with sacrifice, the Lord of emanation<ref>Prajâpati.</ref> said: "By this shall ye propagate; be this to you the giver of desire<ref>Kâmadhuk, the cow of Indra, from which each could milk what he wished for; hence the giver of desired objects.</ref>; {{float right|{{larger|(10)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
देवान्भावयतानेन ते देवा भावयन्तु वः ।

परस्परं भावयन्तः श्रेयः परमवाप्स्यथ ॥ ११ ॥
}} }} }}

"With this nourish ye the Shining Ones, and<noinclude>{{rule}}
{{smallrefs}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader|50|THE BHAGAVAD-GITA.|}}</noinclude>may the Shining Ones nourish you; thus nourishing one another ye shall reap the supremest good. {{float right|{{larger|(11)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
इष्टान्भोगान्हि वो देवा दास्यन्ते यज्ञभाविताः ।

तैर्दत्तानप्रदायैभ्यो यो भुङ्क्ते स्तेन एव सः ॥ १२ ॥
}} }} }}

"For, nourished by sacrifice, the Shining Ones shall bestow on you the enjoyments you desire." A thief verily is he who enjoyeth what is given by Them without returning Them aught. {{float right|{{larger|(12)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
यज्ञशिष्टाशिनः सन्तो मुच्यन्ते सर्वकिल्बिषैः ।

भुञ्जते ते त्वघं पापा ये पचन्त्यात्मकारणात् ॥ १३ ॥
}} }} }}

The righteous, who eat the remains of the sacrifice, are freed from all sins; but the impious, who dress food for their own sakes, they verily eat sin. {{float right|{{larger|(13)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
अन्नाद्भवन्ति भूतानि पर्जन्यादन्नसंभवः ।

यज्ञाद्भवति पर्जन्यो यज्ञः कर्मसमुद्भवः ॥ १४ ॥
}} }} }}

From food creatures become; from rain is the<noinclude></noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader||THIRD DISCOURSE.|51}}</noinclude>production of food; rain proceedeth from sacrifice; sacrifice ariseth out of action. {{float right|{{larger|(14)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
कर्म ब्रह्मोद्भवं विद्धि ब्रह्माऽक्षरसमुद्भवम् ।

तस्मात्सर्वगतं ब्रह्म नित्यं यज्ञे प्रतिष्ठितम् ॥ १५ ॥
}} }} }}

Know thou that from Brahma<ref>An Indian of much knowledge translates Brahma here as "the Vedas."</ref> action groweth, and Brahma from the Imperishable cometh. Therefore the {{sc|Eternal}}, the all-permeating, is ever present in sacrifice. {{float right|{{larger|(15)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
एवं प्रवर्तितं चक्रं नानुवर्तयतीह यः ।

अघायुरिन्द्रियारामो मोघं पार्थ स जीवति ॥ १६ ॥
}} }} }}

He who on earth doth not follow the wheel thus revolving, sinful of life and rejoicing in the senses, he, O son of Pritha, liveth in vain. {{float right|{{larger|(16)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
यस्त्वात्मरतिरेव स्यादात्मतृप्तश्च मानवः ।

आत्मन्येव च सन्तुष्टस्तस्य कार्यं न विद्यते ॥ १७ ॥
}} }} }}

But the man who rejoiceth in the {{sc|Self}}, with<noinclude>{{rule}}
{{smallrefs}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader|52|THE BHAGAVAD-GITA.|}}</noinclude>the {{sc|Self}} is satisfied, and is content in the {{sc|Self}}, for him verily there is nothing to do; {{float right|{{larger|(17)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
नैव तस्य कृतेनार्थो नाकृतेनेह कश्चन ।

न चास्य सर्वभूतेषु कश्चिदर्थव्यपाश्रयः ॥ १८ ॥
}} }} }}

For him there is no interest in things done, in this world, nor any in things not done, nor doth any object of his depend on any being. {{float right|{{larger|(18)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
तस्मादसक्तः सततं कार्यं कर्म समाचर ।

असक्तो ह्याचरन्कर्म परमाप्नोति पूरुषः ॥ १९ ॥
}} }} }}

Therefore, without attachment, constantly perform action which is duty, for, by performing action without attachment, man verily reacheth the Supreme. {{float right|{{larger|(19)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
कर्मणैव हि संसिद्धिमास्थिता जनकादयः ।

लोकसङ्ग्रहमेवापि सम्पश्यन्कर्तुमर्हसि ॥ २० ॥
}} }} }}

Janaka and others indeed attained to perfection by action: then having an eye to the welfare of {{SIC|he|the}} world also, thou shouldst perform action. {{float right|{{larger|(20)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}<noinclude></noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader||THIRD DISCOURSE|{{SIC||53}}}}</noinclude>{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
यद्यदाचरति श्रेष्ठस्तत्तदेवेतरो जनः ।

स यत्प्रमाणं कुरुते लोकस्तदनुवर्तते ॥ २१ ॥
}} }} }}

Whatsoever a great man doeth, that other men also do; the standard he setteth up, by that the people go. {{float right|{{larger|(21)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
न मे पार्थास्ति कर्तव्यं त्रिषु लोकेषु किञ्चन ।

नानवाप्तमवाप्तव्यं वर्त एव च कर्मणि ॥ २२ ॥
}} }} }}

There is nothing in the three worlds, O Pârtha, that should be done by Me, nor anything unattained that might be attained; yet I mingle in action. {{float right|{{larger|(22)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
यदि ह्यहं न वर्तेयं जातु कर्मण्यतन्द्रितः ।

मम वर्त्मानुवर्तन्ते मनुष्याः पार्थ सर्वशः ॥ २३ ॥
}} }} }}

For if I mingled not ever in action unwearied, men all around would follow My path, O son of Prithâ. {{float right|{{larger|(23)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
उत्सीदेयुरिमे लोका न कुर्यां कर्म चेदहम् ।

सङ्करस्य च कर्ता स्यामुपहन्यामिमाः प्रजाः ॥ २४ ॥
}} }} }}
{{nop}}<noinclude></noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader|54|THE BHAGAVAD-GITA.|}}</noinclude>These worlds would fall into ruin, if I did not perform action; I should be the author of confusion of castes, and should destroy these creatures. {{float right|{{larger|(24)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
सक्ताः कर्मण्यविद्वांसो यथा कुर्वन्ति भारत ।

कुर्याद्विद्वांस्तथाऽसक्तश्चिकीर्षुर्लोकसङ्ग्रहम् ॥ २५ ॥
}} }} }}
 
As the ignorant act from attachment to action, O Bhârata, so should the wise act without attachment, desiring the welfare of the world. {{float right|{{larger|(25)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
न बुद्धिभेदं जनयेदज्ञानां कर्मसङ्गिनाम् ।

जोषयेत्सर्वकर्माणि विद्वान्युक्तः समाचरन् ॥ २६ ॥
}} }} }}

Let no wise man unsettle the mind of ignorant people attached to action; but acting in harmony with Me let him render all action attractive. {{float right|{{larger|(26)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
प्रकृतेः क्रियमाणानि गुणैः कर्माणि सर्वशः ।

अहङ्कारविमूढात्मा कर्ताऽहमिति मन्यते ॥ २७ ॥
}} }} }}

All actions are wrought by the quali-<noinclude></noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader||THIRD DISCOURSE.|55}}</noinclude>ties<ref>Gunas.</ref> of nature only. The self, deluded by egoism<ref>Ahamkâra, the separate "I am."</ref>, thinketh: "I am the doer." {{float right|{{larger|(27)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
तत्त्ववित्तु महाबाहो गुणकर्मविभागयोः ।

गुणा गुणेषु वर्तन्त इति मत्वा न सज्जते ॥ २८ ॥
}} }} }}

But he, O mighty-armed, who knoweth the essence of the divisions of the qualities and functions, holding that "the qualities move amid the qualities,"<ref>The Gunas, qualities, as sense-organs move amid the Gunas, qualities, as sense-objects. A suggested reading is "The functions dwell in the propensities." [[Author:Adi Shankara|Sankarâchârya]] says, "of the class of qualities and the class of actions;" or the arrangement, or relations of qualities and actions.</ref> is not attached. {{float right|{{larger|(28)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
प्रकृतेर्गुणसम्मूढाः सज्जन्ते गुणकर्मसु ।

तानकृत्स्नविदो मन्दान्कृत्स्नविन्न विचालयेत् ॥ २९ ॥
}} }} }}

Those deluded by the qualities of nature are attached to the functions of the qualities. The man of perfect knowledge should not unsettle the foolish whose knowledge is imperfect. {{float right|{{larger|(29)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}<noinclude>{{rule}}
{{smallrefs}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader|56|THE BHAGAVAD-GITA.|}}</noinclude>{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
मयि सर्वाणि कर्माणि संन्यस्याऽध्यात्मचेतसा ।

निराशीर्निर्ममो भूत्वा युध्यस्व विगतज्वरः ॥ ३० ॥
}} }} }}

Surrendering all actions to Me, with thy thoughts resting on the supreme {{sc|Self}}, from hope and egoism freed, and of mental fever cured, engage in battle. {{float right|{{larger|(30)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
ये मे मतमिदं नित्यमनुतिष्ठन्ति मानवाः ।

श्रद्धावन्तोऽनसूयन्तो मुच्यन्ते तेऽपि कर्मभिः ॥ ३१ ॥
}} }} }}

Who abide ever in this teaching of Mine full of faith and free from caviling, they too are released from actions. {{float right|{{larger|(31)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
ये त्वेतदभ्यसूयन्तो नानुतिष्ठन्ति मे मतम् ।

सर्वज्ञानविमूढांस्तान्विद्धि नष्टानचेतसः ॥ ३२ ॥
}} }} }}

Who carp at My teaching and act not thereon, senseless, deluded in all knowledge, know thou these mindless ones as fated to be destroyed. {{float right|{{larger|(32)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
सदृशं चेष्टते स्वस्याः प्रकृतेर्ज्ञानवानपि ।

प्रकृतिं यान्ति भूतानि निग्रहः किं करिष्यति ॥ ३३ ॥
}} }} }}
{{nop}}<noinclude></noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader||THIRD DISCOURSE.|57}}</noinclude>Even the man of knowledge behaves in conformity with his own nature; beings follow nature; what shall restraint avail? {{float right|{{larger|(33)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
इन्द्रियस्येन्द्रियस्यार्थे रागद्वेषौ व्यवस्थितौ ।

तयोर्न वशमागच्छेत्तौ ह्यस्य परिपन्थिनौ ॥ ३४ ॥
}} }} }}

Affection and aversion for the objects of sense abide in the senses; let none come under the dominion of these two; they are obstructors of the path. {{float right|{{larger|(34)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
श्रेयान्स्वधर्मो विगुणः परधर्मात्स्वनुष्ठितात् ।

स्वधर्मे निधनं श्रेयः परधर्मो भयावहः ॥ ३५ ॥
}} }} }}

Better one's own duty,<ref name="p57Dharma">Dharma.</ref> though destitute of merit, than the duty<ref name="p57Dharma" /> of another, well discharged. Better death in the discharge of one's own duty;<ref name="p57Dharma" /> the duty<ref name="p57Dharma" /> of another is full of danger. {{float right|{{larger|(35)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
{{c|अर्जुन उवाच ।}}

अथ केन प्रयुक्तोऽयं पापं चरति पूरुषः ।

अनिच्छन्नपि वार्ष्णेय बलादिव नियोजितः ॥ ३६ ॥
}} }} }}

{{c|Arjuna said:}}

But dragged on by what does a man commit<noinclude>{{rule}}
{{smallrefs}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader|58|THE BHAGAVAD-GITA.|}}</noinclude>sin, reluctantly indeed, O Varshneya, as it were by force constrained? {{float right|{{larger|(36)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
{{c|श्रीभगवानुवाच ।}}

काम एष क्रोध एष रजोगुणसमुद्भवः ।

महाशनो महापाप्मा विद्ध्येनमिह वैरिणम् ॥ ३७ ॥
}} }} }}

{{c|The Blessed Lord said:}}

It is desire, it is wrath, begotten by the quality of motion<ref>Rajah.</ref>; all-consuming, all-polluting, know thou this as our foe here on earth. {{float right|{{larger|(37)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
धूमेनाऽव्रियते वह्निर्यथाऽऽदर्शो मलेन च ।

यथोल्बेनावृतो गर्भस्तथा तेनेदमावृतम् ॥ ३८ ॥
}} }} }}

As a flame is enveloped by smoke, as a mirror by dust, as an embryo is wrapped by the amnion, so This<ref>The universe: "{{sc|This}}" as opposed to "{{sc|That}}" the {{sc|Eternal}}. Some say "{{sc|This}}" stands for knowledge.</ref> is enveloped by it. {{float right|{{larger|(38)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
आवृतं ज्ञानमेतेन ज्ञानिनो नित्यवैरिणा ।

कामरूपेण कौन्तेय दुष्पूरेणानलेन च ॥ ३९ ॥
}} }} }}
{{nop}}<noinclude>{{rule}}
{{smallrefs}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader||THIRD DISCOURSE.|59}}</noinclude>Enveloped is wisdom by this constant enemy of the wise in the form of desire, which is insatiable as a flame. {{float right|{{larger|(39)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
इन्द्रियाणि मनो बुद्धिरस्याधिष्ठानमुच्यते ।

एतैर्विमोहयत्येष ज्ञानमावृत्य देहिनम् ॥ ४० ॥
}} }} }}

The senses, the mind<ref name="p59Manah">Manah.</ref> and the Reason<ref name="p59Buddhi">Buddhi.</ref> are said to be its seat; by these enveloping wisdom, it bewilders the dweller in the body. {{float right|{{larger|(40)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
तस्मात्त्वमिन्द्रियाण्यादौ नियम्य भरतर्षभ ।

पाप्मानं प्रजहि ह्येनं ज्ञानविज्ञाननाशनम् ॥ ४१ ॥
}} }} }}

Therefore, O best of the Bhâratas, mastering first the senses, do thou slay this thing of sin, destructive of wisdom and knowledge. {{float right|{{larger|(41)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
इन्द्रियाणि पराण्याहुरिन्द्रियेभ्यः परं मनः ।

मनसस्तु परा बुद्धिर्यो बुद्धेः परतस्तु सः ॥ ४२ ॥
}} }} }}

It is said that the senses are great; greater than the senses is the mind:<ref name="p59Manah" /> greater than the mind<ref name="p59Manah" /> is the Reason;<ref name="p59Buddhi" /> but what is greater than the Reason,<ref name="p59Buddhi" /> is He<ref>The Supreme.</ref>. {{float right|{{larger|{{SIC|(42|(42)}}}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}<noinclude>{{rule}}
{{smallrefs}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader|60|THE BHAGAVAD-GITA.|}}</noinclude>{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
एवं बुद्धेः परं {{SIC|बुध्वा|बुद्ध्वा}} संस्तभ्यात्मानमात्मना ।

जहि शत्रुं महाबाहो कामरूपं दुरासदम् ॥ ४३ ॥
}} }} }}

Thus understanding Him as greater than the Reason,<ref>Buddhi.</ref> restraining the self by the {{sc|Self}}, slay thou, O mighty-armed, the enemy in the form of desire, difficult to overcome. {{float right|{{larger|(43)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
इति श्रीमद्भगवद्गीतासूप॰ कर्मयोगो नाम तृतीयोऽध्यायः ।
}} }} }}

{{fine block|Thus in the glorious Upanishads of the {{sc|Bhagavad-Gita}}, the science of the {{small-caps|Eternal}}, the scripture of Yoga, the dialogue between Sri Krishna and Arjuna, the third discourse, entitled:}}

{{c|THE YOGA OF ACTION.}}
{{dhr|5em}}
{{rule|3em}}
{{nop}}<noinclude>{{dhr}}
{{rule}}
{{smallrefs}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" /></noinclude>{{dhr}}
{{c|{{larger|FOURTH DISCOURSE.}}}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
{{c|श्रीभगवानुवाच ।}}

इमं विवस्वते योगं प्रोक्तवानहमव्ययम् ।

विवस्वान्मनवे प्राह मनुरिक्ष्वाकवेऽब्रवीत् ॥ १ ॥
}} }} }}

{{c|The Blessed Lord said:}}

This imperishable yoga I declared to Vivasvân; Vivasvân taught it to Manu; Manu to Ikshvâku told it. {{float right|{{larger|(1)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
एवं परम्पराप्राप्तमिमं राजर्षयो विदुः ।

स कालेनेह महता योगो नष्टः परन्तप ॥ २ ॥
}} }} }}

This, handed on down the line, the King-Sages knew. This yoga by great efflux of time decayed in the world, O Parantapa. {{float right|{{larger|(2)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
स एवाऽयं मया तेऽद्य योगः प्रोक्तः पुरातनः ।

भक्तोऽसि मे सखा चेति रहस्यं ह्येतदुत्तमम् ॥ ३ ॥
}} }} }}

This same ancient yoga hath been to-day declared to thee by Me, for thou art My devotee and My friend; it is the supreme Secret. {{float right|{{larger|(3)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}<noinclude></noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader|62|THE BHAGAVAD-GITA.|}}</noinclude>{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
{{c|अर्जुन उवाच ।}}

कथमेतद्विजानीयां त्वमादौ प्रोक्तवानिति ॥ ४ ॥
}} }} }}

Later was Thy birth, earlier the birth of Vivasvân; how then am I to understand that Thou declaredst it in the beginning? {{float right|{{larger|(4)}}}}

तान्यहं वेद सर्वाणि न त्वं वेत्थ परन्तप ॥ ५ ॥
}} }} }}

{{c|The Blessed Lord said:}}

Many births have been left behind by Me and by thee, O Arjuna. I know them all, but thou knowest not thine, O Parantapa. {{float right|{{larger|(5)}}}}

{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|

प्रकृतिं {{SIC|स्वामधिष्टाय|स्वामधिष्ठाय}} सम्भवाम्यात्ममायया ॥ ६ ॥
}} }} }}

Though unborn, the imperishable {{sc|Self}}, and also the Lord of all beings, brooding over nature<noinclude></noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader||FOURTH DISCOURSE.|63}}</noinclude>which is Mine own, yet I am born through My own Power.<ref>Mâyâ, the power of thought that produces form, which is transient and therefore unreal compared with the eternal Reality; hence Mâyâ comes to be taken as the power of producing illusion.</ref> {{float right|{{larger|(6)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|

}} }} }}

Whenever there is decay of righteousness,<ref name="p63Dharma">Dharma.</ref> O Bhârata, and there is exaltation of unrighteousness,<ref>Adharma, the opposite of dharma, all that is disorderly, against the nature of things.</ref> then I Myself come forth; {{float right|{{larger|(7)}}}}

{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|

}} }} }}

For the protection of the good, for the destruction of evil-doers, for the sake of firmly establishing righteousness,<ref name="p63Dharma" /> I am born from age to age. {{float right|{{larger|(8)}}}}

{{dhr}}

{{block center/s}}{{larger block/s}}{{lang block|sa|

He who thus knoweth My divine birth and action, in its essence, having abandoned the body, cometh not to birth again, but cometh unto Me, O Arjuna. {{float right|{{larger|(9)}}}}

Freed from passion, fear and anger, filled with Me, taking refuge in Me, purified in the fire<ref>Tapas, from tap, blazing like fire.</ref> of wisdom, many have entered into My Being. {{float right|{{larger|(10)}}}}

{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|

However men approach Me, even so do I welcome them, for the path men take from every side is Mine, O Pârtha. {{float right|{{larger|(11)}}}}

The four castes were emanated by Me, by the different distribution of qualities<ref>Gunas.</ref> and actions; know Me to be the author of them, though the actionless and inexhaustible. {{float right|{{larger|(13)}}}}

{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|

}} }} }}

Nor do actions affect Me, nor is the fruit of action desired by Me. He who thus knoweth Me is not bound by actions. {{float right|{{larger|(14)}}}}

}} }} }}

"What is action, what inaction"? Even the wise are herein perplexed. Therefore I will declare to thee the action by knowing which thou shalt be loosed from evil. {{float right|{{larger|(16)}}}}

}} }} }}

It is needful to discriminate action, to discriminate unlawful action, and to discriminate inaction; mysterious is the path of action. {{float right|{{larger|(17)}}}}

Having abandoned attachment to the fruit of action, always content, nowhere seeking refuge, he is not doing anything, although doing actions. {{float right|{{larger|(20)}}}}

Content with whatsoever he obtaineth without effort, free from the pairs of opposites, without envy, balanced in success and failure, though 
acting he is not bound. {{float right|{{larger|(22)}}}}

{{smallrefs}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader||FOURTH DISCOURSE.|71}}</noinclude>incoming breaths, solely absorbed in the control of breathing.<ref>Prânâyâma, restraint of breath, a technical name for this practice.</ref> {{float right|{{larger|(29)}}}}

{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|

{{dhr}}

}} }} }}

Learn thou this by discipleship,<ref>Literally, falling at the feet, ''i.e.'', the feet of the teacher.</ref> by investiga-<noinclude>{{rule}}
{{smallrefs}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader||FOURTH DISCOURSE.|73}}</noinclude>tion, and by service. The wise, the seers of the essence of things, will instruct thee in wisdom. {{float right|{{larger|(34)}}}}
