आत्मवन्तं न कर्माणि निबध्नन्ति धनञ्जय ॥ ४१ ॥
}} }} }}

He who hath renounced actions by yoga, who hath cloven asunder doubt by wisdom, who is ruled by the {{sc|Self}},<ref>Madhusûdana explains ''âtmavantam'' as "always watchful."</ref> actions do not bind him, O Dhananjaya. {{float right|{{larger|(41)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
तस्मादज्ञानसम्भूतं हृत्स्थं ज्ञानासिनाऽऽत्मनः ।

छित्त्वैनं संशयं योगमातिष्ठोत्तिष्ठ भारत ॥ ४२ ॥
}} }} }}

Therefore, with the sword of the wisdom of the {{sc|Self}} cleaving asunder this ignorance-born doubt dwelling in thy heart, be established in yoga. Stand up, O Bhârata. {{float right|{{larger|(42)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
इति श्रीमद्भगवद्गीतासूप॰ ज्ञानविभागयोगो नाम चतुर्थोऽध्यायः ।
}} }} }}

{{fine block|Thus in the glorious Upanishads of the {{sc|Bhagavad-Gita}}, the science of the {{sc|Eternal}}, the scripture of {{SIC|Yoga|Yoga,}} the dialogue between Shri Krishna and Arjuna, the fourth discourse, entitled:}}

{{c|THE YOGA OF WISDOM.}}
{{dhr|5em}}
{{rule|3em}}
{{nop}}<noinclude>{{dhr}}
{{rule}}
{{smallrefs}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" /></noinclude>{{dhr}}
{{c|{{larger|FIFTH DISCOURSE.}}}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
{{c|अर्जुन उवाच ।}}

संन्यासं कर्मणां कृष्ण पुनर्योगं च शंससि ।

यच्छ्रेय एतयोरेकं तन्मे ब्रूहि सुनिश्चितम् ॥ १ ॥
}} }} }}

{{c|Arjuna said:}}

Renunciation of actions Thou praisest, O Krishna, and then also yoga. Of the two which one is the better? That tell me conclusively. {{float right|{{larger|(1)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
{{c|श्रीभगवानुवाच ।}}

संन्यासः कर्मयोगश्च निःश्रेयसकरावुभौ ।

तयोस्तु कर्मसंन्यासात्कर्मयोगो विशिष्यते ॥ २ ॥
}} }} }}

{{c|The Blessed Lord said:}}

Renunciation and yoga by action both lead to the highest bliss; of the two, yoga by action is verily better than renunciation of action. {{float right|{{larger|(2)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
ज्ञेयः स नित्यसंन्यासी यो न द्वेष्टि न काङ्क्षति ।

निर्द्वन्द्वो हि महाबाहो सुखं बन्धात्प्रमुच्यते ॥ ३ ॥
}} }} }}
{{nop}}<noinclude></noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader||FIFTH DISCOURSE.|77}}</noinclude>He should be known as a perpetual ascetic,<ref>Sannyâsi; one who renounces all.</ref> who neither hateth nor desireth; free from the pairs of opposites, O mighty-armed, he is easily set free from bondage. {{float right|{{larger|(3)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
साङ्ख्ययोगौ पृथग्बालाः प्रवदन्ति न पण्डिताः ।

एकमप्यास्थितः सम्यगुभयोर्विन्दते फलम् ॥ ४ ॥
}} }} }}

Children, not sages, speak of the Sânkhya<ref>See footnote, page 32.</ref> and the Yoga<ref>''Ibid''.</ref> as different; he who is duly established in one obtaineth the fruits of both. {{float right|{{larger|(4)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
यत्साङ्ख्यैः प्राप्यते स्थानं तद्योगैरपि गम्यते ।

एकं साङ्ख्यं च योगं च यः पश्यति स पश्यति ॥ ५ ॥
}} }} }}

That place which is gained by the Sânkhyas is reached by the Yogîs also. He seeth, who seeth that the Sânkhya and the Yoga are one. {{float right|{{larger|(5)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
संन्यासस्तु महाबाहो दुःखमाप्तुमयोगतः ।

योगयुक्तो मुनिर्ब्रह्म न चिरेणाधिगच्छति ॥ ६ ॥
}} }} }}
{{nop}}<noinclude>{{rule}}
{{smallrefs}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader|78|THE BHAGAVAD-GITA.|}}</noinclude>But without yoga, O mighty-armed, renunciation is hard to attain to; the yoga-harmonised Muni swiftly goeth to the {{sc|Eternal}}. {{float right|{{larger|(6)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
योगयुक्तो विशुद्धात्मा विजितात्मा जितेन्द्रियः ।

सर्वभूतात्मभूतात्मा कुर्वन्नपि न लिप्यते ॥ ७ ॥
}} }} }}

He who is harmonised by yoga, the self purified, {{sc|Self}}-ruled, the senses subdued, whose {{sc|Self}} is the {{sc|Self}} of all beings, although acting he is not affected. {{float right|{{larger|(7)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
नैव किञ्चित्करोमीति युक्तो मन्येत तत्त्ववित् ।

{{SIC|पश्यन्शृण्वन्स्पृशञ्जिघ्रन्नश्नन्गच्छन्श्वसन्स्वपन्|पश्यन्शृण्वन्स्पृशञ्जिघ्रन्नश्नन्गच्छन्स्वपन्श्वसन्}} ॥ ८ ॥
}} }} }}

"I do not anything," should think the harmonised one, who knoweth the essence of things; seeing, hearing, touching, smelling, eating, moving, sleeping, breathing. {{float right|{{larger|(8)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
प्रलपन्विसृजन्गृह्णन्नुन्मिषन्निमिषन्नपि ।

इन्द्रियाणीन्द्रियार्थेषु वर्तन्त इति धारयन् ॥ ९ ॥
}} }} }}

Speaking, giving, grasping, opening and closing<noinclude></noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader||FIFTH DISCOURSE.|79}}</noinclude>the eyes, he holdeth: "The senses move among the objects of the senses." {{float right|{{larger|(9)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
ब्रह्मण्याधाय कर्माणि सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा करोति यः ।

लिप्यते न स पापेन पद्मपत्रमिवाम्भसा ॥ १० ॥
}} }} }}

He who acteth, placing all actions in the {{sc|Eternal}}, abandoning attachment, is unaffected by sin as a lotus leaf by the waters. {{float right|{{larger|(10)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}} 

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
कायेन मनसा बुद्ध्या केवलैरिन्द्रियैरपि ।

योगिनः कर्म कुर्वन्ति सङ्गं त्यक्त्वाऽऽत्मशुद्धये ॥ ११ ॥
}} }} }}

{{SIC|Yogis}}, having abandoned attachment, perform action only by the body, by the mind<ref>Manah.</ref>, by the Reason<ref>Buddhi.</ref>, and even by the senses, for the purification of the self. {{float right|{{larger|(11)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
युक्तः कर्मफलं त्यक्त्वा शान्तिमाप्नोति नैष्ठिकीम् ।

अयुक्तः कामकारेण फले सक्तो निबध्यते ॥ १२ ॥
}} }} }}

The harmonised man, having abandoned the fruit of action, attaineth to the eternal Peace;<noinclude>{{rule}}
{{smallrefs}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader|80|THE BHAGAVAD-GITA.|}}</noinclude>the non-harmonised, impelled by desire, attached to fruit, are bound. {{float right|{{larger|(12)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
सर्वकर्माणि मनसा संन्यस्यास्ते सुखं वशी ।

नवद्वारे पुरे देही नैव कुर्वन्न कारयन् ॥ १३ ॥
}} }} }}

Mentally renouncing all actions, the sovereign dweller in the body resteth serenely in the nine-gated city,<ref>The body, often called the city of the {{sc|Eternal}}.</ref> neither acting nor causing to act. {{float right|{{larger|(13)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
न कर्तृत्वं न कर्माणि लोकस्य सृजति प्रभुः ।

न कर्मफलसंयोगं स्वभावस्तु प्रवर्तते ॥ १४ ॥
}} }} }}

The Lord of the world produceth not the idea of agency, nor actions, nor the union together of action and its fruit; nature, however, manifesteth. {{float right|{{larger|(14)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
नादत्ते कस्यचित्पापं न चैव सुकृतं विभुः ।

अज्ञानेनावृतं ज्ञानं तेन मुह्यन्ति जन्तवः ॥ १५ ॥
}} }} }}

The Lord accepteth neither the evil-doing nor<noinclude>{{rule}}
{{smallrefs}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader||FIFTH DISCOURSE.|81}}</noinclude>yet the well-doing of any. Wisdom is enveloped by unwisdom; therewith mortals are deluded. {{float right|{{larger|(15)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
ज्ञानेन तु तदज्ञानं येषां नाशितमात्मनः ।

तेषामादित्यवज्ज्ञानं प्रकाशयति तत्परम् ॥ १६ ॥
}} }} }}

Verily, in whom unwisdom is destroyed by the wisdom of the {{sc|Self}}, in them wisdom, shining as the sun, reveals the Supreme. {{float right|{{larger|(16)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
तद्बुद्धयस्तदात्मानस्तन्निष्ठास्तत्परायणाः ।

गच्छन्त्यपुनरावृत्तिं ज्ञाननिर्धूतकल्मषाः ॥ १७ ॥
}} }} }}

Thinking on {{sc|That}}, merged in {{sc|That}}, established in {{sc|That}}, solely devoted to {{sc|That}}, they go whence there is no return, their sins dispelled by wisdom. {{float right|{{larger|(17)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
विद्याविनयसम्पन्ने ब्राह्मणे गवि हस्तिनि ।

शुनि चैव श्वपाके च पण्डिताः समदर्शिनः ॥ १८ ॥
}} }} }}

Sages look equally on a Brâhmana adorned<noinclude></noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader|82|THE BHAGAVAD-GITA.|}}</noinclude>with learning and humility, a cow, an elephant, and even a dog and an outcaste.<ref>Shvapâka, the lowest class of outcastes.</ref> {{float right|{{larger|(18)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
इहैव तैर्जितः सर्गो येषां साम्ये स्थितं मनः ।

निर्दोषं हि समं ब्रह्म तस्माद्ब्रह्मणि ते स्थिताः ॥ १९ ॥
}} }} }}

Even here on earth everything is overcome by those whose mind<ref>Manah.</ref> remains balanced; the {{sc|Eternal}} is incorruptible and balanced; therefore they are established in the {{sc|Eternal}}. {{float right|{{larger|(19)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
न प्रहृष्येत्प्रियं प्राप्य नोद्विजेत्प्राप्य चाप्रियम् ।

स्थिरबुद्धिरसंमूढो ब्रह्मविद्ब्रह्मणि स्थितः ॥ २० ॥
}} }} }}

With Reason<ref>Buddhi.</ref> firm, unperplexed, the knower of the {{sc|Eternal}} established in the {{sc|Eternal}}, neither rejoiceth on obtaining what is pleasant, nor sorroweth on obtaining what is unpleasant. {{float right|{{larger|(20)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
बाह्यस्पर्शेष्वसक्तात्मा विन्दत्यात्मनि यत्सुखम् ।

स ब्रह्मयोगयुक्तात्मा सुखमक्षयमश्नुते ॥ २१ ॥
}} }} }}
{{nop}}<noinclude>{{rule}}
{{smallrefs}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader||FIFTH DISCOURSE.|83}}</noinclude>He, whose self is unattached to external contacts and findeth joy in the {{sc|Self}}, having the self harmonised with the {{sc|Eternal}} by yoga, enjoys imperishable bliss. {{float right|{{larger|(21)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
ये हि संस्पर्शजा भोगा दुःखयोनय एव ते ।

आद्यन्तवन्तः कौन्तेय न तेषु रमते बुधः ॥ २२ ॥
}} }} }}

The delights that are contact-born, they are verily wombs of pain, for they have beginning and ending, O Kaunteya; not in them may rejoice the wise. {{float right|{{larger|(22)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
शक्नोतीहैव यः सोढुं प्राक् शरीरविमोक्षणात् ।

कामक्रोधोद्भवं वेगं स युक्तः स सुखी नरः ॥ २३ ॥
}} }} }}

He who is able to endure here on earth, ere he be liberated from the body, the force born from desire and passion, he is harmonised, he is a happy man. {{float right|{{larger|(23)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
योऽन्तःसुखोऽन्तरारामस्तथान्तर्ज्योतिरेव यः ।

स योगी ब्रह्मनिर्वाणं ब्रह्मभूतोऽधिगच्छति ॥ २४ ॥
}} }} }}
{{nop}}<noinclude></noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader|84|THE BHAGAVAD-GITA.|}}</noinclude>He who is happy within, who rejoiceth within, who is illuminated within, that Yogî, becoming the {{sc|Eternal}}, goeth to the Peace<ref name="p84Peace">Nirvâna.</ref> of the {{sc|Eternal}}. {{float right|{{larger|(24)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
लभन्ते ब्रह्मनिर्वाणमृषयः क्षीणकल्मषाः ।

छिन्नद्वैधा यतात्मानः सर्वभूतहिते रताः ॥ २५ ॥
}} }} }}

Rishis, their sins destroyed, their duality removed, their selves controlled, intent upon the welfare of all beings, obtain the Peace<ref name="p84Peace" /> of the {{sc|Eternal}}. {{float right|{{larger|(25)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
कामक्रोधवियुक्तानां यतीनां यतचेतसाम् ।

अभितो ब्रह्मनिर्वाणं वर्तते विदितात्मनाम् ॥ २६ ॥
}} }} }}

The Peace<ref name="p84Peace" /> of the {{sc|Eternal}} lies near to those who know themselves, who are disjoined from desire and passion, subdued in nature, of subdued thoughts. {{float right|{{larger|(26)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}<noinclude>{{rule}}
{{smallrefs}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader||FIFTH DISCOURSE.|85}}</noinclude>{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
स्पर्शान्कृत्वा बहिर्बाह्यांश्चक्षुश्चैवान्तरे भ्रुवोः ।

प्राणापानौ समौ कृत्वा नासाभ्यन्तरचारिणौ ॥ २७ ॥
}} }} }}

Having external contacts excluded, and with gaze fixed between the eyebrows; having made equal the outgoing and ingoing breaths moving within the nostrils; {{float right|{{larger|(27)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
यतेन्द्रियमनोबुद्धिर्मुनिर्मोक्षपरायणः ।

विगतेच्छाभयक्रोधो यः सदा मुक्त एव सः ॥ २८ ॥
}} }} }}

With senses, mind,<ref>Manah.</ref> and Reason<ref>Buddhi.</ref> ever controlled, solely pursuing liberation, the Sage, having for ever cast away desire, fear and passion, verily is liberated. {{float right|{{larger|(28)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
भोक्तारं यज्ञतपसां सर्वलोकमहेश्वरम् ।

सुहृदं सर्वभूतानां ज्ञात्वा मां शान्तिमृच्छति ॥ २९ ॥
}} }} }}

Having known Me, as the Enjoyer of sacrifice and of austerity, the mighty Ruler of all the<noinclude>{{rule}}
{{smallrefs}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader|86|THE BHAGAVAD-GITA.|}}</noinclude>worlds, and the Lover of all beings, he goeth to Peace. {{float right|{{larger|(29)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
इति श्रीमद्भगवद्गीतासूप॰ संन्यासयोगो नाम पञ्चमोऽध्यायः ।
}} }} }}

{{fine block|Thus in the glorious Upanishads of the {{sc|Bhagavad-Gita}}, the science of the {{small-caps|Eternal}}, the scripture of Yoga, in the dialogue between Shrî Krishna and Arjuna, the fifth discourse, entitled:}}

{{c|THE YOGA OF THE RENUNCIATION OF ACTION.}}
{{dhr|5em}}
{{rule|3em}}
{{nop}}<noinclude></noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" /></noinclude>{{dhr}}
{{c|{{larger|SIXTH DISCOURSE.}}}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
{{c|श्रीभगवानुवाच ।}}

अनाश्रितः कर्मफलं कार्यं कर्म करोति यः ।

स संन्यासी च योगी च न निरग्निर्न चाक्रियः ॥ १ ॥
}} }} }}

{{c|The Blessed Lord said:}}

He that performeth such action as his duty, independently of the fruit of action, he is an ascetic,<ref>The ascetic, the Sannyâsî, lights no sacrificial fire and performs no sacrifices nor ceremonies; but merely to omit these, without true renunciation, is not to be a real ascetic.</ref> he is a Yogî, not he that is without fire, and without rites. {{float right|{{larger|(1)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
यं संन्यासमिति प्राहुर्योगं तं विद्धि पाण्डव ।

न ह्यसंन्यस्तसङ्कल्पो योगी भवति कश्चन ॥ २ ॥
}} }} }}

That which is called renunciation, know thou that as yoga, O Pândava; nor doth any one become a Yogî with the formative will<ref>Sankalpa, the imaginative faculty that makes plans for the future.</ref> unrenounced. {{float right|{{larger|(2)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}<noinclude>{{rule}}
{{smallrefs}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader|88|THE BHAGAVAD-GITA.|}}</noinclude>{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
आरुरुक्षोर्मुनेर्योगं कर्म कारणमुच्यते ।

योगारूढस्य तस्यैव शमः कारणमुच्यते ॥ ३ ॥
}} }} }}

For a Sage who is seeking Yoga, action is called the means; for the same Sage, when he is enthroned in yoga, serenity is called the means. {{float right|{{larger|(3)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
यदा हि नेन्द्रियार्थेषु न कर्मस्वनुषज्जते ।

सर्वसङ्कल्पसंन्यासी योगारूढस्तदोच्यते ॥ ४ ॥
}} }} }}

When a man feeleth no attachment either for the objects of sense or for actions, renouncing the formative will,<ref>Sankalpa.</ref> then, he is said to be enthroned in yoga. {{float right|{{larger|(4)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
उद्धरेदात्मनाऽऽत्मानं नात्मानमवसादयेत् ।

आत्मैव ह्यात्मनो बन्धुरात्मैव रिपुरात्मनः ॥ ५ ॥
}} }} }}

Let him raise the self by the {{sc|Self}} and not let the self become depressed; for verily is the {{sc|Self}} the friend of the self, and also the {{sc|Self}} the self's enemy; {{float right|{{larger|(5)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}<noinclude>{{rule}}
{{smallrefs}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader||SIXTH DISCOURSE.|89}}</noinclude>{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
बन्धुरात्माऽऽत्मनस्तस्य येनात्मैवात्मना जितः ।

अनात्मनस्तु शत्रुत्वे वर्तेतात्मैव शत्रुवत् ॥ ६ ॥
}} }} }}

The {{sc|Self}} is the friend of the self of him in whom the self by the {{sc|Self}} is vanquished; but to the unsubdued self<ref>Literally, the non-self.</ref> the {{sc|Self}} verily becometh hostile as an enemy. {{float right|{{larger|(6)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
जितात्मनः प्रशान्तस्य परमात्मा समाहितः ।

शीतोष्णसुखदुःखेषु तथा मानापमानयोः ॥ ७ ॥
}} }} }}

The higher Self of him who is {{sc|Self}}-controlled and peaceful is uniform in cold and heat, pleasure and pain, as well as in honour and dishonour. {{float right|{{larger|(7)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
ज्ञानविज्ञानतृप्तात्मा कूटस्थो विजितेन्द्रियः ।

युक्त इत्युच्यते योगी समलोष्टाश्मकाञ्चनः ॥ ८ ॥
}} }} }}

The Yogî<ref>The word Yogi is used for any one who is practising yoga, as well as for the man who has attained union.</ref> who is satisfied with wisdom and knowledge, unwavering,<ref>Literally, rock-seated.</ref> whose senses are sub-<noinclude>{{rule}}
{{smallrefs}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader|90|THE BHAGAVAD-GITA.|}}</noinclude>dued, to whom a lump of earth, a stone and gold are the same, is said to be harmonised. {{float right|{{larger|(8)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
सुहृन्मित्रार्युदासीनमध्यस्थद्वेष्यबन्धुषु ।

साधुष्वपि च पापेषु समबुद्धिर्विशिष्यते ॥ ९ ॥
}} }} }}

He who regards impartially lovers, friends, and foes, strangers, neutrals, foreigners and relatives, also the righteous and unrighteous, he excelleth. {{float right|{{larger|(9)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
योगी युञ्जीत सततमात्मानं रहसि स्थितः ।

एकाकी यतचित्तात्मा निराशीरपरिग्रहः ॥ १० ॥
}} }} }}

Let the Yogî constantly engage himself in yoga, remaining in a secret place by himself, with thought and self subdued, free from hope and greed. {{float right|{{larger|(10)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
शुचौ देशे प्रतिष्ठाप्य स्थिरमासनमात्मनः ।

नात्युच्छ्रितं नातिनीचं {{SIC|चेलाजिनकुशोत्तरम्|चैलाजिनकुशोत्तरम्}} ॥ ११ ॥
}} }} }}

In a pure place, established on a fixed seat of his own, neither very much raised nor very low,<noinclude></noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader||SIXTH DISCOURSE.|91}}</noinclude>made of a cloth, a black antelope skin, and kusha grass, one over the other; {{float right|{{larger|(11)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
तत्रैकाग्रं मनः कृत्वा यतचित्तेन्द्रियक्रियः ।

उपविश्यासने युञ्ज्याद्योगमात्मविशुद्धये ॥ १२ ॥
}} }} }}

There, having made the mind<ref>Manah.</ref> one-pointed, with thought and the functions of the senses subdued, steady on his seat, he should practise yoga for the purification of the self. {{float right|{{larger|(12)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
समं कायशिरोग्रीवं धारयन्नचलं स्थिरः ।

संप्रेक्ष्य नासिकाग्रं स्वं दिशश्चानवलोकयन् ॥ १३ ॥
}} }} }}

Holding the body, head and neck erect, immovably steady, looking fixedly at the point of the nose, with unseeing gaze, {{float right|{{larger|(13)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
प्रशान्तात्मा विगतभीर्ब्रह्मचारिव्रते स्थितः ।

मनः संयम्य मच्चित्तो युक्त आसीत मत्परः ॥ १४ ॥
}} }} }}

The self serene, fearless, firm in the vow of the<noinclude>{{rule}}
{{smallrefs}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader|92|THE BHAGAVAD-GITA.|}}</noinclude>Brahmachâri,<ref>A Brahmachârî is a man who is keeping the vow of continence, a celibate.</ref> the mind<ref name="p92Manah">Manah.</ref> controlled, thinking on Me, harmonised, let him sit aspiring after Me. {{float right|{{larger|(14)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
युञ्जन्नेवं सदाऽऽत्मानं योगी नियतमानसः ।

शान्तिं निर्वाणपरमां मत्संस्थामधिगच्छति ॥ १५ ॥
}} }} }}

The Yogî ever united thus with the {{sc|Self}}, with the mind<ref name="p92Manah" /> controlled, goeth to Peace, to the supreme Bliss<ref>Nirvana.</ref> that abideth in Me. {{float right|{{larger|(15)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
नात्यश्नतस्तु योगोऽस्ति न चैकान्तमनश्नतः ।

न चातिस्वप्नशीलस्य जाग्रतो नैव चार्जुन ॥ १६ ॥
}} }} }}

Verily yoga is not for him who eateth too much, nor who abstaineth to excess, nor who is too much addicted to sleep, nor even to wakefulness, O Arjuna. {{float right|{{larger|(16)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
युक्ताहारविहारस्य  युक्तचेष्टस्य कर्मसु ।

युक्तस्वप्नावबोधस्य योगो भवति दुःखहा ॥ १७ ॥
}} }} }}
{{nop}}<noinclude>{{rule}}
{{smallrefs}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader||SIXTH DISCOURSE.|93}}</noinclude>Yoga killeth out all pain for him who is regulated in eating and amusement, regulated in performing actions, regulated in sleeping and waking. {{float right|{{larger|(17)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
यदा विनियतं चित्तमात्मन्येवावतिष्ठते ।

निःस्पृहः सर्वकामेभ्यो युक्त इत्युच्यते तदा ॥ १८ ॥
}} }} }}

When his subdued thought is fixed on the {{sc|Self}}, free from longing after all desirable things, then it is said, "he is harmonised." {{float right|{{larger|(18)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
यथा दीपो निवातस्थो नेङ्गते सोपमा स्मृता ।

योगिनो यतचित्तस्य युञ्जतो योगमात्मनः ॥ १९ ॥
}} }} }}

As a lamp in a windless place flickereth not, to such is likened the Yogî of subdued thought, absorbed in the yoga of the {{sc|Self}}. {{float right|{{larger|(19)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
यत्रोपरमते चित्तं निरुद्धं योगसेवया ।

यत्र चैवात्मनाऽऽत्मानं पश्यन्नात्मनि तुष्यति ॥ २० ॥
}} }} }}

That in which the mind finds rest, quieted by the practice of yoga: that in which he, seeing the {{sc|Self}} by the {{sc|Self}}, in the {{sc|Self}} is satisfied; {{float right|{{larger|(20)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}<noinclude></noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader|94|THE BHAGAVAD-GITA.|}}</noinclude>{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
सुखमात्यन्तिकं यत्तद् बुद्धिग्राह्यमतीन्द्रियम् ।

वेत्ति यत्र न चैवाऽयं स्थितश्चलति तत्त्वतः ॥ २१ ॥
}} }} }}

That in which he findeth the supreme delight which the Reason<ref>Buddhi.</ref> can grasp beyond the senses, wherein established he moveth not from the Reality; {{float right|{{larger|(21)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
यं लब्ध्वा चापरं लाभं मन्यते नाधिकं ततः ।

यस्मिन्स्थितो न दुःखेन गुरुणाऽपि विचाल्यते ॥ २२ ॥
}} }} }}

Which, having obtained, he thinketh there is no greater gain beyond it; wherein, established, he is not shaken even by heavy sorrow; {{float right|{{larger|(22)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
तं विद्याद्‌ दुःखसंयोगवियोगं योगसंज्ञितम् ।

स निश्चयेन योक्तव्यो योगोऽनिर्विण्णचेतसा ॥ २३ ॥
}} }} }}

That should be known by the name of yoga, this disconnection from the union with pain. This yoga must be clung to with a firm conviction and with undesponding mind.<ref>Chetah.</ref>  {{float right|{{larger|{{SIC|(23|(23)}}}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}<noinclude>{{rule}}
{{smallrefs}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader||SIXTH DISCOURSE.|95}}</noinclude>{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
सङ्कल्पप्रभावान्कामांस्त्यक्त्वा सर्वानशेषतः ।

मनसैवेन्द्रियग्रामं विनियम्य समन्ततः ॥ २४ ॥
}} }} }}

Abandoning without reserve all desires born of the imagination,<ref>Sankalpa.</ref> by the mind<ref name="p95Manah">Manah.</ref> curbing in the aggregate of the senses on every side, {{float right|{{larger|(24)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
शनैःशनैरुपरमेद्‌ बुद्ध्या धृतिगृहीतया ।

आत्मसंस्थं मनः कृत्वा न किञ्चिदपि चिन्तयेत् ॥ २५ ॥
}} }} }}

Little by little let him gain tranquillity, by means of Reason<ref>Buddhi.</ref> controlled by steadiness; having made the mind<ref name="p95Manah" /> abide in the {{sc|Self}}, let him not think of anything. {{float right|{{larger|(25)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
यतो यतो निश्चरति मनश्चञ्चलमस्थिरम् ।

ततस्ततो नियम्यैतदात्मन्येव वशं नयेत् ॥ २६ ॥
}} }} }}

As often as the wavering and unsteady mind<ref name="p95Manah" /> goeth forth, so often reining it in, let him bring it under the control of the {{sc|Self}}. {{float right|{{larger|(26)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
प्रशान्तमनसं ह्येनं योगिनं सुखमुत्तमम् ।

उपैति शान्तरजसं ब्रह्मभूतमकल्मषम् ॥ २७ ॥
}} }} }}

Supreme joy is for this Yogi whose mind<ref name="p95Manah" /> is<noinclude>{{rule}}
{{smallrefs}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader|96|THE BHAGAVAD-GITA.|}}</noinclude>peaceful, whose passion-nature is calmed, who is sinless and of the nature of the {{sc|Eternal}}. {{float right|{{larger|(27)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
युञ्जन्नेवं सदाऽऽत्मानं योगी विगतकल्मषः ।

सुखेन ब्रह्मसंस्पर्शमत्यन्तं सुखमश्नुते ॥ २८ ॥
}} }} }}

The Yogî who thus, ever harmonising the self, hath put away sin, he easily enjoyeth the infinite bliss of contact with the {{sc|Eternal}}. {{float right|{{larger|(28)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
सर्वभूतस्थमात्मानं सर्वभूतानि चात्मनि ।

ईक्षते योगयुक्तात्मा सर्वत्र समदर्शनः ॥ २९ ॥
}} }} }}

The self, harmonised by yoga, seeth the {{sc|Self}} abiding in all beings, all beings in the {{sc|Self}}; everywhere he seeth the same. {{float right|{{larger|(29)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
यो मां पश्यति सर्वत्र सर्वं च मयि पश्यति ।

तस्याहं न प्रणश्यामि स च मे न प्रणश्यति ॥ ३० ॥
}} }} }}

He who seeth Me everywhere, and seeth everything in Me, of him will I never lose hold, and he shall never lose hold of Me. {{float right|{{larger|(30)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}<noinclude></noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader||SIXTH DISCOURSE|97}}</noinclude>{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
सर्वभूतस्थितं यो मां भजत्येकत्वमास्थितः ।

सर्वथा वर्त्तमानोऽपि स योगी मयि वर्तते ॥ ३१ ॥
}} }} }}

He who, established in unity, worshippeth Me abiding in all beings, that Yogi liveth in Me, whatever his mode of living. {{float right|{{larger|(31)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
आत्मौपम्येन सर्वत्र समं पश्यति योऽर्जुन ।

सुखं वा यदि वा दुःखं स योगी परमो मतः ॥ ३२ ॥
}} }} }}

He who, through the likeness of the {{sc|Self}}<ref>The same {{sc|Self}} shining in the heart of each.</ref>, O Arjuna, seeth equality in everything, whether pleasant or painful, he is considered a perfect Yogî. {{float right|{{larger|(32)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
{{c|अर्जुन उवाच ।}}

योऽयं योगस्त्वया प्रोक्तः साम्येन मधुसूदन ।

एतस्याहं न पश्यामि चञ्चलत्वात्स्थितिं स्थिराम् ॥ ३३ ॥
}} }} }}

{{SIC|This yoga|Arjuna said: This yoga}} which Thou hast declared to be by equanimity, O Madhusûdana, I see not a stable foundation for it, owing to restlessness; {{float right|{{larger|(33)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}<noinclude>{{rule}}
{{smallrefs}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader|98|THE BHAGAVAD-GITA.|}}</noinclude>{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
चञ्चलं हि मनः कृष्ण प्रमाथि बलवद्‌ दृढम् ।

तस्याऽहं निग्रहं मन्ये वायोरिव सुदुष्करम् ॥ ३४ ॥
}} }} }}

For the mind<ref name="p98Manah">Manah.</ref> is verily restless, O Krishna; it is impetuous, strong and difficult to bend. I deem it as hard to curb as the wind. {{float right|{{larger|(34)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
{{c|श्रीभगवानुवाच ।}}

असंशयं महाबाहो मनो दुर्निग्रहं चलम् ।

अभ्यासेन तु कौन्तेय वैराग्येण च गृह्यते ॥ ३५ ॥
}} }} }}

{{c|The Blessed Lord said:}}

Without doubt, O mighty-armed, the mind<ref name="p98Manah" /> is hard to curb and restless; but it may be curbed by constant practice and by dispassion. {{float right|{{larger|(35)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
असंयतात्मना योगो दुष्प्राप इति मे मतिः ।

वश्यात्मना तु यतता शक्योऽवाप्तुमुपायतः ॥ ३६ ॥
}} }} }}

Yoga is hard to attain, methinks, by a self that is uncontrolled; but by the {{sc|Self}}-controlled it is attainable by properly directed energy. {{float right|{{larger|(36)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}<noinclude>{{rule}}
{{smallrefs}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader||SIXTH DISCOURSE.|99}}</noinclude>{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
{{c|अर्जुन उवाच ।}}

अयतिः श्रद्धयोपेतो योगाच्चलितमानसः ।

अप्राप्य योगसंसिद्धिं कां गतिं कृष्ण गच्छति ॥ ३७ ॥
}} }} }}

{{c|Arjuna said:}}

He who is unsubdued but who possesseth faith, with the mind<ref>Manah.</ref> wandering away from yoga, failing to attain perfection in yoga, what path doth he tread, O Krishna?  {{float right|{{larger|(37)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
कच्चिन्नोभयविभ्रष्टश्छिन्नाभ्रमिव नश्यति ।

अप्रतिष्ठो महाबाहो विमूढो ब्रह्मणः पथि ॥ ३८ ॥
}} }} }}

Fallen from both, is he destroyed like a rent cloud, unsteadfast, O mighty-armed, deluded in the path of the {{sc|Eternal}}? {{float right|{{larger|(38)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
एतं मे संशयं कृष्ण छेत्तुमर्हस्यशेषतः ।

त्वदन्यः संशयस्यास्य छेत्ता नह्युपपद्यते ॥ ३९ ॥
}} }} }}

Deign, O Krishna, to completely dispel this<noinclude>{{rule}}
{{smallrefs}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader|100|THE BHAGAVAD-GITA.|}}</noinclude>doubt of mine; for there is none to be found save Thyself able to destroy this doubt. {{float right|{{larger|(39)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
{{c|श्रीभगवानुवाच ।}}

पार्थ नैवेह नामुत्र विनाशस्तस्य विद्यते ।

न हि कल्याणकृत्कश्चिद्‌दुर्गतिं तात गच्छति ॥ ४० ॥
}} }} }}

{{c|The Blessed Lord said:}}

O son of Prithâ, neither in this world nor in the life to come is there destruction for him; never doth any who worketh righteousness, O beloved, tread the path of woe. {{float right|{{larger|(40)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
प्राप्य पुण्यकृतां लोकानुषित्वा शाश्वतीः समाः ।

शुचीनां श्रीमतां गेहे योगभ्रष्टोऽभिजायते ॥ ४१ ॥
}} }} }}

Having attained to the worlds of the pure-doing, and having dwelt there for immemorial years, he who fell from yoga is reborn in a pure and blessed house; {{float right|{{larger|(41)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
अथवा योगिनामेव कुले भवति धीमताम् ।

एतद्धि दुर्लभतरं लोके जन्म यदीदृशम् ॥ ४२ ॥
}} }} }}
{{nop}}<noinclude></noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader||SIXTH DISCOURSE.|101}}</noinclude>Or he may even be born into a family of wise Yogîs; but such a birth as that is most difficult to obtain in this world. {{float right|{{larger|(42)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
तत्र तं बुद्धिसंयोगं लभते पौर्वदेहिकम् ।

यतते च ततो भूयः संसिद्धौ कुरुनन्दन ॥ ४३ ॥
}} }} }}

There he recovereth the characteristics belonging to this former body, and with these he again laboureth for perfection, O joy of the Kurus. {{float right|{{larger|(43)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
पूर्वाभ्यासेन तेनैव ह्रियते ह्यवशोऽपि सः ।

जिज्ञासुरपि योगस्य शब्दब्रह्मातिवर्तते ॥ ४४ ॥
}} }} }}

By that former practice he is irresistibly swept away. Only wishing to know yoga, even the seeker after yoga goeth beyond the Brâhmic world;<ref>The Vedas.</ref>{{float right|{{larger|(44)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
प्रयत्नाद्यतमानस्तु योगी संशुद्धकिल्बिषः ।

अनेकजन्मसंसिद्धस्ततो याति परां गतिम् ॥ ४५ ॥
}} }} }}

But the Yogî, labouring with assiduity, purified<noinclude>{{rule}}
{{smallrefs}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader|102|THE BHAGAVAD-GITA.|}}</noinclude>from sin, fully perfected through manifold births, he reacheth the supreme goal. {{float right|{{larger|(45)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
तपस्विभ्योऽधिको योगी ज्ञानिभ्योऽपि मतोऽधिकः ।

कर्मिभ्यश्चाधिको योगी तस्माद्योगी भवार्जुन ॥ ४६ ॥
}} }} }}

The Yogî is greater than the ascetics; he is thought to be greater than even the wise; the Yogî is greater than the men of action; therefore become thou a Yogî, O Arjuna! {{float right|{{larger|(46)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
योगिनामपि सर्वेषां मद्गतेनान्तरात्मना ।

श्रद्धावान्भजते यो मां स मे युक्ततमो मतः ॥ ४७ ॥
}} }} }}

And among all Yogîs, he who, full of faith, with the inner {{sc|Self}} abiding in Me, adoreth Me, he is considered by Me to be the most completely harmonised. {{float right|{{larger|(47)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
इति श्रीमद्भगवद्गीता॰ अध्यात्मयोगो नाम षष्ठोऽध्यायः ।
}} }} }}

{{fine block|Thus in the glorious Upanishads of the {{sc|Bhagavad-Gita}}, the science of the {{small-caps|Eternal}}, the scripture of Yoga, in the dialogue between Shrî Krishna and Arjuna, the sixth discourse, entitled:}}

{{c|THE YOGA OF SELF-SUBDUAL.}}

{{rule|3em}}
{{nop}}<noinclude></noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" /></noinclude>{{dhr}}
{{c|{{larger|SEVENTH DISCOURSE.}}}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
{{c|श्रीभगवानुवाच ।}}

मय्यासक्तमनाः पार्थ योगं युञ्जन्मदाश्रयः ।

असंशयं समग्रं मां यथा ज्ञास्यसि तच्छृणु ॥ १ ॥
}} }} }}

{{c|The Blessed Lord said:}}
With the mind<ref>Manah.</ref> clinging to me, O Pârtha, performing yoga, refuged in Me, how thou shalt without doubt know Me to the uttermost, that hear thou. {{float right|{{larger|(1)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
ज्ञानं तेऽहं सविज्ञानमिदं वक्ष्याम्यशेषतः ।

यज्ज्ञात्वा नेह भूयोऽन्यज्ज्ञातव्यमवशिष्यते ॥ २ ॥
}} }} }}

I will declare to thee this knowledge and wisdom in its completeness, which, having known, there is nothing more here needeth to be known. {{float right|{{larger|(2)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
मनुष्याणां सहस्रेषु कश्चिद्यतति सिद्धये ।

यततामपि सिद्धानां कश्चिन्मां वेत्ति तत्त्वतः ॥ ३ ॥
}} }} }}
{{nop}}<noinclude>{{rule}}
{{smallrefs}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader|104|THE BHAGAVAD-GITA.|}}</noinclude>Among thousands of men scarce one striveth for perfection; of the successful strivers scarce one knoweth Me in essence. {{float right|{{larger|(3)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
भूमिरापोऽनलो वायुः खं मनो बुद्धिरेव च ।

अहङ्कार इतीयं मे भिन्ना प्रकृतिरष्टधा ॥ ४ ॥
}} }} }}

Earth, water, fire, air, ether, Mind,<ref>Manah.</ref> and Reason<ref>Buddhi.</ref> also and Egoism<ref>Ahañkâra.</ref>—these are the eightfold division of My nature.<ref name="p104Nature">Prakriti, matter in the widest sense of the term, including all that has extension. The "Higher Prakriti," of the next verse, is sometimes called Daivîprakriti, the Light of the Logos.</ref> {{float right|{{larger|(4)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
अपरेयमितस्त्वन्यां प्रकृतिं विद्धि मे पराम् ।

जीवभूतां महाबाहो ययेदं धार्यते जगत् ॥ ५ ॥
}} }} }}


This the inferior. Know My other nature,<ref name="p104Nature" /> the higher, the life-element, O mighty-armed, by which the universe is upheld. {{float right|{{larger|(5)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
एतद्योनीनि भूतानि सर्वाणीत्युपधारय ।

अहं कृत्स्नस्य जगतः प्रभवः प्रलयस्तथा ॥ ६ ॥
}} }} }}
{{nop}}<noinclude>{{rule}}
{{smallrefs}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader||SEVENTH DISCOURSE.|105}}</noinclude>Know this to be the womb of all beings. I am the source of the forthgoing of the whole universe and likewise the place of its dissolving. {{float right|{{larger|(6)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
मत्तः परतरं नान्यत्किञ्चिदस्ति धनञ्जय ।

मयि सर्वमिदं प्रोतं सूत्रे मणिगणा इव ॥ ७ ॥
}} }} }}

There is naught whatsoever higher than I, O Dhananjaya. All this is threaded on Me, as rows of pearls on a string. {{float right|{{larger|(7)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
रसोऽहमप्सु कौन्तेय प्रभाऽस्मि शशिसूर्ययोः ।

प्रणवः सर्ववेदेषु शब्दः खे पौरुषं नृषु ॥ ८ ॥
}} }} }}

I the sapidity in waters, O son of Kuntî, I the radiance in moon and sun; the Word of Power<ref>The Prañava, the [[w:Om|Aum]].</ref> in all the Vedas, sound in ether, and virility in men; {{float right|{{larger|(8)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
पुण्यो गन्धः पृथिव्यां च तेजश्चास्मि विभावसौ ।

जीवनं सर्वभूतेषु तपश्चास्मि तपस्विषु ॥ ९ ॥
}} }} }}

The pure fragrance of earths and the bril-<noinclude>{{rule}}
{{smallrefs}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader|106|THE BHAGAVAD-GITA.|}}</noinclude>liance in fire am I; the life in all beings am I, and the austerity in ascetics. {{float right|{{larger|(9)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
बीजं मां सर्वभूतानां विद्धि पार्थ सनातनम् ।

बुद्धिर्बुद्धिमतामस्मि तेजस्तेजस्विनामहम् ॥ १० ॥
}} }} }}

Know Me, O Pârtha! as the eternal seed of all beings. I am the Reason<ref name="p106Buddhi">Buddhi.</ref> of the Reason<ref name="p106Buddhi" />-endowed, the splendour of splendid things am I. {{float right|{{larger|(10)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
बलं बलवतामस्मि कामरागविवर्जितम् ।

धर्माविरुद्धो भूतेषु कामोऽस्मि भरतर्षभ ॥ ११ ॥
}} }} }}

And I the strength of the strong, devoid of desire and passion. In beings I am desire not contrary to duty,<ref>Dharma.</ref> O Lord of the Bharatas. {{float right|{{larger|(11)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}} 

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
ये चैव सात्त्विका भावा राजसास्तामसाश्च ये ।

मत्त एवेति तान्विद्धि न त्वहं तेषु ते मयि ॥ १२ ॥
}} }} }}

The natures that are harmonious, active, slothful,<ref>Sattvic, rajasic, tamasic, that is, those in whom one of the three qualities, Sattva, Rajah, Tamah, predominates.</ref> these know as from Me; not I in them, but they in me. {{float right|{{larger|(12)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}<noinclude>{{rule}}
{{smallrefs}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader||SEVENTH DISCOURSE.|107}}</noinclude>{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
त्रिभिर्गुणमयैर्भावैरेभिः सर्वमिदं जगत् ।

मोहितं नाभिजानाति मामेभ्यः परमव्ययम् ॥ १३ ॥
}} }} }}

All this world, deluded by these natures made by the three qualities,<ref name="p107Gunas">Gunas.</ref> knoweth not Me, above these, imperishable. {{float right|{{larger|(13)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
दैवी ह्येषा गुणमयी मम माया दुरत्यया ।

मामेव ये प्रपद्यन्ते मायामेतां तरन्ति ते ॥ १४ ॥
}} }} }}

This divine illusion<ref name="p107Maya">Mâyâ.</ref> of Mine, caused by the qualities,<ref name="p107Gunas" /> is hard to pierce; they who come to Me, they cross over this illusion.<ref name="p107Maya" />{{float right|{{larger|(14)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
न मां दुष्कृतिनो मूढाः प्रपद्यन्ते नराधमाः ।

माययाऽपहृतज्ञाना आसुरं भावमाश्रिताः ॥ १५॥
}} }} }}

The evil-doing, the deluded, the vilest men, they come not to Me, they whose wisdom is destroyed by illusion,<ref name="p107Maya" /> who have embraced the nature of demons.<ref>Asuras, the opponents of the Suras or gods.</ref>{{float right|{{larger|(15)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}<noinclude>{{rule}}
{{smallrefs}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader|108|THE BHAGAVAD-GITA.|}}</noinclude>{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
चतुर्विधा भजन्ते मां जनाः सुकृतिनोऽर्जुन ।

आर्तो जिज्ञासुरर्थार्थी ज्ञानी च भरतर्षभ ॥ १६ ॥
}} }} }}

Fourfold in division are the righteous ones who worship me, O Arjuna; the suffering, the seeker for knowledge, the self-interested and the wise, O Lord of the Bhâratas. {{float right|{{larger|(16)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
तेषां ज्ञानी नित्ययुक्त एकभक्तिर्विशिष्यते ।

प्रियो हि ज्ञानिनोऽत्यर्थमहं स च मम प्रियः ॥ १७ ॥
}} }} }}

Of these the wise, constantly harmonised, worshipping the One, is the best; I am supremely dear to the wise, and he is dear to Me. {{float right|{{larger|(17)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
उदाराः सर्व एवैते ज्ञानी त्वात्मैव मे मतम् ।

आस्थितः स हि युक्तात्मा मामेवानुत्तमां गतिम् ॥ १८ ॥
}} }} }}

Noble are all these, but I hold the wise as verily Myself; he, {{sc|Self}} united, is fixed on Me, the highest Path. {{float right|{{larger|(18)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center/s}}{{larger block/s}}{{lang block|sa|
बहूनां जन्मनामन्ते ज्ञानवान्मां प्रपद्यते ।
}}<noinclude>{{larger block/e}} {{block center/e}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader||SEVENTH DISCOURSE.|109}}
{{block center/s}}{{larger block/s}}</noinclude>{{lang block|sa|
वासुदेवः सर्वमिति स महात्मा सुदुर्लभः ॥ १९ ॥
}}
{{larger block/e}} {{block center/e}}

At the close of many births the man full of wisdom cometh unto Me; "Vâsudeva<ref>A name of Shrî Krishna, as the son of Vasudeva.</ref> is all." saith he, the Mahâtmâ, very difficult to find. {{float right|{{larger|(19)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
कामैस्तैस्तैर्हृतज्ञानाः प्रपद्यन्तेऽन्यदेवताः ।

तं तं नियममास्थाय प्रकृत्या नियताः स्वया ॥ २० ॥
}} }} }}

They whose wisdom hath been rent away by desires go forth to other Shining Ones, resorting to various external observances, according to their own natures. {{float right|{{larger|(20)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
यो यो यां यां तनुं भक्तः श्रद्धयाऽर्चितुमिच्छति ।

तस्य तस्याचलां श्रद्धां तामेव विदधाम्यहम् ॥ २१ ॥
}} }} }}

Any devotee who seeketh to worship with faith any such aspect, I verily bestow the unswerving faith of that man. {{float right|{{larger|(21)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
स तया श्रद्धया युक्तस्तस्याराधनमीहते ।

लभते च ततः कामान्मयैव विहितान्हि तान् ॥ २२ ॥
}} }} }}
{{nop}}<noinclude>{{rule}}
{{smallrefs}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader|110|THE BHAGAVAD-GITA.|}}</noinclude>He endowed with that faith, seeketh the worship of such a one, and from him he obtaineth his desires, I verily decreeing the benefits; {{float right|{{larger|(22)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
अन्तवत्तु फलं तेषां तद्भवत्यल्पमेधसाम् ।

देवान्देवयजो यान्ति मद्भक्ता यान्ति मामपि ॥ २३ ॥
}} }} }}

Finite indeed the fruit that belongeth to those who are of small intelligence. To the Shining Ones go the worshippers of the Shining Ones, but my devotees come unto Me. {{float right|{{larger|(23)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}} 

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
अव्यक्तं व्यक्तिमापन्नं मन्यन्ते मामबुद्धयः ।

परं भावमजानन्तो ममाव्ययमनुत्तमम् ॥ २४ ॥
}} }} }}

Those devoid of Reason<ref>Buddhi.</ref> think of Me, the unmanifest, as having manifestation, knowing not My supreme nature, imperishable, most excellent. {{float right|{{larger|(24)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}} 

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
नाहं प्रकाशः सर्वस्य योगमायासमावृतः ।

मूढोऽयं नाभिजानाति लोको मामजमव्ययम् ॥ २५ ॥
}} }} }}
{{nop}}<noinclude>{{rule}}
{{smallrefs}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader||SEVENTH DISCOURSE.|111}}</noinclude>Nor am I of all discovered, enveloped in My creation-illusion.<ref>Yoga-Maya, the creative power of Yoga, all things being the thought-forms of the One.</ref> This deluded world knoweth Me not, the unborn, the imperishable. {{float right|{{larger|(25)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
वेदाहं समतीतानि वर्तमानानि चार्जुन ।

भविष्याणि च भूतानि मां तु वेद न कश्चन ॥ २६ ॥
}} }} }}

I know the beings that are past, that are present, that are to come, O Arjuna, but no one knoweth Me. {{float right|{{larger|(26)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
इच्छाद्वेषसमुत्थेन द्वन्द्वमोहेन भारत ।

सर्वभूतानि सम्मोहं सर्गे यान्ति परन्तप ॥ २७ ॥
}} }} }}

By the delusion of the pairs of opposites, sprung from attraction and repulsion, O Bhârata, all beings walk this universe wholly deluded, O Parantapa. {{float right|{{larger|(27)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
येषां त्वन्तगतं पापं जनानां पुण्यकर्मणाम् ।

ते द्वन्द्वमोहनिर्मुक्ता भजन्ते मां दृढव्रताः ॥ २८ ॥
}} }} }}
{{nop}}<noinclude>{{rule}}
{{smallrefs}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader|112|THE BHAGAVAD-GITA.|}}</noinclude>But those men of pure deeds, in whom sin is come to an end, they, freed from the delusive pairs of opposites, worship Me, steadfast in vows. {{float right|{{larger|(28)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
जरामरणमोक्षाय मामाश्रित्य यतन्ति ये ।

ते ब्रह्म तद्विदुः कृत्स्नमध्यात्मं कर्म चाखिलम् ॥ २९ ॥
}} }} }}

They who, refuged in Me, strive for liberation from birth and death, they know the {{sc|Eternal}}, the whole {{sc|Self}}-knowledge, and all action. {{float right|{{larger|(29)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
साधिभूताधिदैवं मां साधियज्ञं च ये विदुः ।

प्रयाणकालेऽपि च मां ते विदुर्युक्तचेतसः ॥ ३० ॥
}} }} }}

They who know Me as the knowledge of the elements, as that of the Shining Ones, and as that of the Sacrifice,<ref>These six terms are: Brahman, Adhyâtma, Karma, Adhibhûta, Adhidaiva, Adhiyajña.</ref> they harmonised in mind, know Me verily even in the time of forthgoing.<ref>Death—going forth from the body.</ref> {{float right|{{larger|(30)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}<noinclude>{{rule}}
{{smallrefs}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader||SEVENTH DISCOURSE.|113}}</noinclude>{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
इति श्रीमद्भगवद्गीता॰ ज्ञानयोगो नाम सप्तमोऽध्यायः ।
}} }} }}

{{fine block|Thus in the glorious Upanishads of the {{sc|Bhagavad-Gita}}, the science of the {{small-caps|Eternal}}, the scripture of Yoga, the dialogue between Shrî Krishna and Arjuna, the seventh discourse, entitled:}}

{{c|THE YOGA OF DISCRIMINATIVE KNOWLEDGE.}}
{{dhr|3em}}
{{rule|3em}}
{{nop}}<noinclude></noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" /></noinclude>{{dhr}}
{{c|{{larger|EIGHTH DISCOURSE.}}}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
{{c|अर्जुन उवाच ।}}

किं तद्ब्रह्म किमध्यात्मं किं कर्म पुरुषोत्तम ।

अधिभूतं च किं प्रोक्तमधिदैवं किमुच्यते ॥ १ ॥
}} }} }}

{{c|Arjuna said:}}

What is that {{sc|Eternal}},<ref>Brahman.</ref> what {{sc|Self}}-knowledge,<ref>Adhyâtma.</ref> what Action,<ref>Karma.</ref> O Purushottama? And what is declared to be the knowledge of the Elements,<ref>Adhibhûta.</ref> what is called the knowledge of the Shining Ones?<ref>Adhidaiva.</ref> {{float right|{{larger|(1)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
अधियज्ञः कथं कोऽत्र देहेऽस्मिन्मधुसूदन ।

प्रयाणकाले च कथं ज्ञेयोऽसि नियतात्मभिः ॥ २ ॥
}} }} }}

What is the knowledge of Sacrifice<ref>Adhiyajña.</ref> in this body, and how, O, Madhusûdana? And how, at the time of forthgoing art Thou known by the {{sc|Self}}-controlled? {{float right|{{larger|(2)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}<noinclude>{{rule}}
{{smallrefs}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader||EIGHTH DISCOURSE.|115}}</noinclude>{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
{{c|श्रीभगवानुवाच ।}}

अक्षरं ब्रह्म परमं स्वभावोऽध्यात्ममुच्यते ।

भूतभावोद्भवकरो विसर्गः कर्मसंज्ञितः ॥ ३ ॥
}} }} }}

{{c|The Blessed Lord said:}}

The indestructible, the supreme is the {{sc|Eternal}};<ref>Brahman.</ref> His essential nature is called {{sc|Self}}-knowledge;<ref>Adhyâtma.</ref> the emanation that causes the birth of beings is named Action;<ref>Karma.</ref> {{float right|{{larger|(3)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
अधिभूतं क्षरो भावः पुरुषश्चाधिदैवतम् ।

अधियज्ञोऽहमेवात्र देहे देहभृतां वर ॥ ४ ॥
}} }} }}

Knowledge of the Elements<ref>Adhibhûta.</ref> concerns My perishable nature, and knowledge of the Shining Ones<ref>Adhidaiva.</ref> concerns the life-giving energy<ref>Purusha, the male creative energy. The supreme {{SIC|Pursha|Purusha}} is the Divine Man, the manifested God.</ref>; the knowledge of Sacrifice<ref>Adhiyajña.</ref> tells of Me, as wearing the body, O best of living beings. {{float right|{{larger|(4)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}<noinclude>{{rule}}
{{smallrefs}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader|116|THE BHAGAVAD-GITA.|}}</noinclude>{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
अन्तकाले च मामेव स्मरन्मुक्त्वा कलेवरम् ।

यः प्रयाति स मद्भावं याति नास्त्यत्र संशयः ॥ ५ ॥
}} }} }}

And he who, casting off the body, goeth forth thinking upon Me only at the time of the end, he entereth into My being: there is no doubt of that. {{float right|{{larger|(5)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
यं यं वापि स्मरन्भावं त्यजत्यन्ते कलेवरम् ।

तं तमेवैति कौन्तेय सदा तद्भावभावितः ॥ ६ ॥
}} }} }}

Whosoever at the end abandoneth the body, thinking upon any being, to that being only he goeth, O Kaunteya, ever to that conformed in nature. {{float right|{{larger|(6)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
तस्मात्सर्वेषु कालेषु मामनुस्मर युध्य च ।

मय्यर्पितमनोबुद्धिर्मामेवैष्यस्यसंशयम् ॥ ७ ॥
}} }} }}

Therefore at all times think upon Me only and fight. With mind<ref>Manah.</ref> and Reason<ref>Buddhi.</ref> set on Me, without doubt thou shalt come to Me. {{float right|{{larger|(7)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}<noinclude>{{rule}}
{{smallrefs}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader||EIGHTH DISCOURSE.|117}}</noinclude>{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
अभ्यासयोगयुक्तेन चेतसा नान्यगामिना ।

परमं पुरुषं दिव्यं याति पार्थानुचिन्तयन् ॥ ८ ॥
}} }} }}

With the mind<ref>Chetah.</ref> not wandering after aught else, harmonised by continual practice, constantly meditating, O Pârtha, one goeth to the Spirit supreme, divine. {{float right|{{larger|(8)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
कविं पुराणमनुशासितारमणोरणीयांसमनुस्मरेद्यः ।

सर्वस्य धातारमचिन्त्यरूपमादित्यवर्णं तमसः परस्तात् ॥ ९ ॥
}} }} }}

He who thinketh upon the Ancient, the Omniscient, the All-Ruler, minuter than the minute, the supporter of all, of form unimaginable, refulgent as the sun beyond the darkness, {{float right|{{larger|(9)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center/s}}{{larger block/s}}{{lang block|sa|
प्रयाणकाले मनसाऽचलेन भक्त्या युक्तो योगबलेन चैव ।
}}<noinclude>{{larger block/e}}{{block center/e}}
{{rule}}
{{smallrefs}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader|118|THE BHAGAVAD-GITA.|}}
{{block center/s}}{{larger block/s}}</noinclude>{{lang block|sa|
भ्रुवोर्मध्ये प्राणमावेश्य सम्यक् स तं परं पुरुषमुपैति दिव्यम् ॥ १० ॥
}} {{larger block/e}} {{block center/e}}

In the time of forthgoing, with unshaken mind,<ref>Manah.</ref> fixed in devotion, by the power of yoga drawing together his life-breath in the centre of the two eyebrows, he goeth to this Spirit, supreme, divine. {{float right|{{larger|(10)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
यदक्षरं वेदविदो वदन्ति विशन्ति यद्यतयो वीतरागाः ।

यदिच्छन्तो ब्रह्मचर्यं चरन्ति तत्ते पदं सङ्ग्रहेण प्रवक्ष्ये ॥ ११ ॥
}} }} }}

That which is declared indestructible by the Veda-knowers, that which the controlled and passion-free enter, that desiring which Brahmacharya<ref>The vow of continence.</ref> is performed, that path I will declare to thee with brevity. {{float right|{{larger|(11)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}<noinclude>{{rule}}
{{smallrefs}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader||EIGHTH DISCOURSE.|119}}</noinclude>{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
सर्वद्वाराणि संयम्य मनो हृदि निरुध्य च ।

मूर्ध्न्याधायात्मनः प्राणमास्थितो योगधारणाम् ॥ १२ ॥
}} }} }}

All the gates<ref>The gates of the body, ''i.e.'', the sense-organs.</ref> closed, the mind confined in the heart, the life-breath fixed in his own head, concentrated by yoga, {{float right|{{larger|(12)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
ओमित्येकाक्षरं ब्रह्म व्याहरन्मामनुस्मरन् ।

यः प्रयाति त्यजन्देहं स याति परमां गतिम् ॥ १३ ॥
}} }} }}

"Aum!" the one syllabled {{sc|Eternal}}, reciting, thinking upon Me, he who goeth forth, abandoning the body, he goeth on the highest path. {{float right|{{larger|(13)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
अनन्यचेताः सततं यो मां स्मरति नित्यशः ।

तस्याहं सुलभः पार्थ नित्ययुक्तस्य योगिनः ॥ १४ ॥
}} }} }}

He who constantly thinketh upon Me, not thinking ever of another, of him I am easily reached, O Pârtha, of this ever-harmonised Yogî. {{float right|{{larger|(14)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}<noinclude>{{rule}}
{{smallrefs}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader|120|THE BHAGAVAD-GITA.|}}</noinclude>{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
मामुपेत्य पुनर्जन्म दुःखालयमशाश्वतम् ।

नाप्नुवन्ति महात्मानः संसिद्धिं परमां गताः ॥ १५ ॥
}} }} }}

Having come to Me, these Mahâtmâs come not again to birth, the place of pain, non-eternal; they have gone to the highest bliss. {{float right|{{larger|(15)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
आब्रह्मभुवनाल्लोकाः पुनरावर्तिनोऽर्जुन ।

मामुपेत्य तु कौन्तेय पुनर्जन्म न विद्यते ॥ १६ ॥
}} }} }}

The worlds, beginning with the world of Brahmâ, they come and go, O Arjuna; but he who cometh unto Me, O Kaunteya, he knoweth birth no more. {{float right|{{larger|(16)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
सहस्रयुगपर्यन्तमहर्यद्ब्रह्मणो विदुः ।

रात्रिं युगसहस्रान्तां तेऽहोरात्रविदो जनाः ॥ १७ ॥
}} }} }}

The people who know the day of Brahmâ, a thousand ages<ref>Yugas.</ref> in duration, and the night a thousand ages in ending, they know day and night. {{float right|{{larger|(17)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}<noinclude>{{rule}}
{{smallrefs}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader||EIGHTH DISCOURSE.|121}}</noinclude>{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
अव्यक्ताद्व्यक्तयः सर्वाः प्रभवन्त्यहरागमे ।

रात्र्यागमे प्रलीयन्ते तत्रैवाव्यक्तसंज्ञके ॥ १८ ॥
}} }} }}

From the unmanifested all the manifested stream forth at the coming of day; at the coming of night they dissolve, even in That called the unmanifested. {{float right|{{larger|(18)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
भूतग्रामः स एवायं भूत्वा भूत्वा प्रलीयते ।

रात्र्यागमेऽवशः पार्थ प्रभवत्यहरागमे ॥ १९ ॥
}} }} }}

This multitude of beings, going forth repeatedly, is dissolved at the coming of night: by ordination, O Pârtha, it streams forth at the coming of day. {{float right|{{larger|(19)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
परस्तस्मात्तु भावोऽन्योऽव्यक्तोऽव्यक्तात्सनातनः ।

यः स सर्वेषु भूतेषु नश्यत्सु न विनश्यति ॥ २० ॥
}} }} }}
 
Therefore verily there existeth, higher than that unmanifested, another unmanifested, eternal, which in the destroying of all beings, is not destroyed. {{float right|{{larger|{{SIC|(20|(20)}}}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}<noinclude></noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader|122|THE BHAGAVAD-GITA.|}}</noinclude>{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
अव्यक्तोऽक्षर इत्युक्तस्तमाहुः परमां गतिम् ।

यं प्राप्य न निवर्तन्ते तद्धाम परमं मम ॥ २१ ॥
}} }} }}

That unmanifested, "the Indestructible," It is called; It is named the highest Path. They who reach It return not. That is My supreme abode. {{float right|{{larger|(21)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
पुरुषः स परः पार्थ भक्त्या लभ्यस्त्वनन्यया ।

यस्यान्तःस्थानि भूतानि येन सर्वमिदं ततम् ॥ २२ ॥
}} }} }}
 
He, the highest Spirit,<ref>Purusha.</ref> O Pârtha, may be reached by unswerving devotion to Him alone, in whom all beings abide, by whom all This<ref>This, the universe, in opposition to {{sc|that}}, the source of all.</ref> is pervaded. {{float right|{{larger|(22)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
यत्र काले त्वनावृत्तिमावृत्तिं चैव योगिनः ।

प्रयाता यान्ति तं कालं वक्ष्यामि भरतर्षभ ॥ २३ ॥
}} }} }}

That time wherein going forth Yogîs return<noinclude>{{rule}}
{{smallrefs}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader||EIGHTH DISCOURSE.|123}}</noinclude>not, and also that wherein going forth they return, that time shall I declare to thee, O prince of the Bhâratas. {{float right|{{larger|(23)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
अग्निर्ज्योतिरहः शुक्लः षण्मासा उत्तरायणम् ।

तत्र प्रयाता गच्छन्ति ब्रह्म ब्रह्मविदो जनाः ॥ २४ ॥
}} }} }}

Fire, light, day-time, the bright fortnight, the six months of the northern path<ref name="p123path">Of the sun.</ref>—then, going forth, the men who know the {{sc|Eternal}} go to the {{sc|Eternal}}. {{float right|{{larger|(24)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
धूमो रात्रिस्तथा कृष्णः षण्मासा दक्षिणायनम् ।

तत्र चान्द्रमसं ज्योतिर्योगी प्राप्य निवर्तते ॥ २५ ॥
}} }} }}

Smoke, night-time, the dark fortnight also, the six months of the southern path<ref name="p123path" />—then the Yogî, obtaining the moonlight,<ref>The Lunar, or astral body. Until this is slain the soul returns to birth.</ref> returneth. {{float right|{{larger|(25)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
शुक्लकृष्णे गती ह्येते जगतः शाश्वते मते ।

एकया यात्यनावृत्तिमन्ययाऽऽवर्तते पुनः ॥ २६ ॥
}} }} }}
{{nop}}<noinclude>{{rule}}
{{smallrefs}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader|124|THE BHAGAVAD-GITA.|}}</noinclude>Light and darkness, these are thought to be the world's everlasting paths; by the one he goeth who returneth not, by the other he who returneth again. {{float right|{{larger|(26)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
नैते सृती पार्थ जानन्योगी मुह्यति कश्चन ।

तस्मात्सर्वेषु कालेषु योगयुक्तो भवार्जुन ॥ २७ ॥
}} }} }}

Knowing these paths, O Pârtha, the Yogi is nowise perplexed. Therefore in all times be firm in yoga, O Arjuna. {{float right|{{larger|(27)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
वेदेषु यज्ञेषु तपःसु चैव दानेषु यत्पुण्यफलं प्रदिष्टम् ।

अत्येति तत्सर्वमिदं विदित्वा योगी परं स्थानमुपैति चाद्यम् ॥ २८ ॥
}} }} }}

The fruit of meritorious deeds, attached in the Vedas to sacrifices, to austerities, and also to almsgiving, the Yogî passeth all these by having known this, and goeth to the supreme and ancient Seat. {{float right|{{larger|(28)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}<noinclude></noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader||EIGHTH DISCOURSE.|125}}</noinclude>{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
इति श्रीमद्भगवद्गीता॰ योगशास्त्रेऽक्षरब्रह्मयोगो नामाष्टमोऽध्यायः ।
}} }} }}

{{fine block|Thus in the glorious Upanishads of the {{sc|Bhagavad-Gita}}, the science of the {{small-caps|Eternal}}, the scripture of Yoga, the dialogue between Shrî Krishna and Arjuna, the eighth discourse, entitled:}}

{{c|THE YOGA OF THE INDESCTRUCTIBLE SUPREME ETERNAL.}}
{{dhr|3em}}
{{rule|3em}}
{{nop}}<noinclude></noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" /></noinclude>{{dhr}}
{{c|{{larger|NINTH DISCOURSE.}}}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
{{c|श्रीभगवानुवाच ।}}

इदं तु ते गुह्यतमं प्रवक्ष्याम्यनसूयवे ।

ज्ञानं विज्ञानसहितं यज्ज्ञात्वा मोक्ष्यसेऽशुभात् ॥ १ ॥
}} }} }}

{{c|The Blessed Lord said:}}

To thee, the uncarping, verily shall I declare this profoundest Secret, wisdom with knowledge combined, which, having known, thou shalt be freed from evil. {{float right|{{larger|(1)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
राजविद्या राजगुह्यं पवित्रमिदमुत्तमम् ।

प्रत्यक्षावगमं धर्म्यं सुसुखं कर्तुमव्ययम् ॥ २ ॥
}} }} }}

Kingly Science, kingly Secret, supreme Purifier, this; intuitional, according to righteousness,<ref name="p126Dharma">Dharma.</ref> very easy to perform, imperishable. {{float right|{{larger|(2)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
अश्रद्दधानाः पुरुषा धर्मस्यास्य परन्तप ।

अप्राप्य मां निवर्तन्ते मृत्युसंसारवर्त्मनि ॥ ३ ॥
}} }} }}
 
Men without faith in this knowledge,<ref name="p126Dharma" /> O<noinclude>{{rule}}
{{smallrefs}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader||NINTH DISCOURSE.|127}}</noinclude>Parantapa, not reaching Me, return to the paths of this world of death. {{float right|{{larger|(3)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
मया ततमिदं सर्वं जगदव्यक्तमूर्तिना ।

मत्स्थानि सर्वभूतानि न चाहं तेष्ववस्थितः ॥ ४ ॥
}} }} }}

By Me all this world is pervaded in My unmanifested aspect; all beings have root in Me, I am not rooted in them. {{float right|{{larger|(4)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
न च मत्स्थानि भूतानि पश्य मे योगमैश्वरम् ।

भूतभृन्न च भूतस्थो ममात्मा भूतभावनः ॥ ५ ॥
}} }} }}

Nor have beings root in Me; behold My sovereign Yoga! The support of beings, yet not rooted in beings, My {{sc|Self}} their efficient cause. {{float right|{{larger|(5)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
यथाऽऽकाशस्थितो नित्यं वायुः सर्वत्रगो महान् ।

तथा सर्वाणि भूतानि मत्स्थानीत्युपधारय ॥ ६ ॥
}} }} }}

As the mighty air everywhere moving is rooted in the Ether,<ref>Akâsha.</ref> so all beings rest rooted in Me—thus know thou. {{float right|{{larger|(6)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}<noinclude>{{rule}}
{{smallrefs}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader|128|THE BHAGAVAD-GITA.|}}</noinclude>{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
सर्वभूतानि कौन्तेय प्रकृतिं यान्ति मामिकाम् ।

कल्पक्षये पुनस्तानि कल्पादौ विसृजाम्यहम् ॥ ७ ॥
}} }} }}

All beings, O Kaunteya, enter my lower nature<ref name="p128Nature">Prakriti.</ref> at the end of a world-age;<ref name="p128WorldAge">Kalpa, a period of activity, of manifestation.</ref> at the beginning of a world-age<ref name="p128WorldAge" /> again I emanate them. {{float right|{{larger|(7)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
प्रकृतिं स्वामवष्टभ्य विसृजामि पुनः पुनः ।

भूतग्राममिमं कृत्स्नमवशं प्रकृतेर्वशात् ॥ ८ ॥
}} }} }}

Hidden in Nature,<ref name="p128Nature" /> which is mine own, I emanate again and again all this multitude of beings, helpless, by the force of Nature<ref name="p128Nature" />. {{float right|{{larger|(8)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|

}} }} }}

The knowers of the three,<ref>The Three Vedas.</ref> the Soma-drinkers, the purified from sin, worshipping Me with sacrifice, pray of Me the way to heaven; they, ascending to the holy world of the Ruler of the Shining Ones, eat in heaven the divine feasts of the Shining Ones. {{float right|{{larger|(20)}}}}

{{c|अर्जुन उवाच ।}}

परं ब्रह्म परं धाम पवित्रं परमं भवान् ।

पुरुषं शाश्वतं दिव्यमादिदेवमजं विभुम् ॥ १२ ॥
}} }} }}
{{nop}}<noinclude>{{rule}}
{{smallrefs}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader|142|THE BHAGAVAD-GITA.|}}</noinclude>{{c|Arjuna said:}}

Thou art the supreme {{sc|Eternal}}, the supreme Abode, the supreme Purity, eternal divine man, primeval Deity, unborn, the Lord! {{float right|{{larger|(12)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
आहुस्त्वामृषयः सर्वे देवर्षिर्नारदस्तथा ।

असितो देवलो व्यासः स्वयं चैव ब्रवीषि मे ॥ १३ ॥
}} }} }}

All the Rishis have thus acclaimed Thee, as also the divine Rishi, Nârada; so Asita, Devala, and Vyâsa; and now Thou Thyself tellest it me. {{float right|{{larger|(13)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
सर्वमेतदृतं मन्ये यन्मां वदसि केशव ।

न हि ते भगवन्व्यक्तिं विदुर्देवा न दानवाः ॥ १४ ॥
}} }} }}

All this I believe true that Thou sayest to me, O Keshava. Thy manifestation, O Blessed Lord, neither Shining Ones nor Dânavas<ref>Demigods, in the Greek sense.</ref> comprehend. {{float right|{{larger|(14)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}<noinclude>{{rule}}
{{smallrefs}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader||TENTH DISCOURSE.|143}}</noinclude>{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
स्वयमेवात्मनाऽऽत्मानं वेत्थ त्वं पुरुषोत्तम ।

भूतभावन भूतेश देवदेव जगत्पते ॥ १५ ॥
}} }} }}

Thyself indeed knowest Thyself by Thyself, O Purushottama; Source of beings, Lord of beings, Shining One of Shining Ones, Ruler of the world! {{float right|{{larger|(15)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
वक्तुमर्हस्यशेषेण दिव्या ह्यात्मविभूतयः ।

याभिर्विभूतिभिर्लोकानिमांस्त्वं व्याप्य तिष्ठसि ॥ १६ ॥
}} }} }}

Deign to tell without reserve of Thine own divine glories, by which glories Thou remainest, pervading these worlds. {{float right|{{larger|(16)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
कथं विद्यामहं योगिंस्त्वां सदा परिचिन्तयन् ।

केषु केषु च भावेषु चिन्त्योऽसि भगवन्मया ॥ १७ ॥
}} }} }}

How may I know thee, O Yogi, by constant meditation? In what, in what aspects art Thou to be thought of by me, O blessed Lord? {{float right|{{larger|(17)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
विस्तरेणात्मनो योगं विभूतिं च जनार्दन ।

भूयः कथय तृप्तिर्हि शृण्वतो नास्ति मेऽमृतम् ॥ १८ ॥
}} }} }}
{{nop}}<noinclude></noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader|144|THE BHAGAVAD-GITA.|}}</noinclude>In detail tell me again of Thy yoga and glory, O Janardana; for me there is never satiety in hearing thy life-giving words. {{float right|{{larger|(18)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
{{c|श्रीभगवानुवाच ।}}

हन्त ते कथयिष्यामि दिव्या ह्यात्मविभूतयः ।

प्राधान्यतः कुरुश्रेष्ठ नास्त्यन्तो विस्तरस्य मे ॥ १९ ॥
}} }} }}

{{c|The Blessed Lord said:}}

Blessed be thou! I will declare to thee My divine glory by its chief characteristics, O best of the Kurus; there is no end to details of Me. {{float right|{{larger|(19)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
अहमात्मा गुडाकेश सर्वभूताशयस्थितः ।

अहमादिश्च मध्यं च भूतानामन्त एव च ॥ २० ॥
}} }} }}

I, O Gudakesha, am the {{sc|Self}}, seated in the heart of all beings; I am the beginning, the middle, and also the end of all beings. {{float right|{{larger|(20)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
आदित्यानामहं विष्णुर्ज्योतिषां रविरंशुमान् ।

मरीचिर्मरुतामस्मि नक्षत्राणामहं शशी ॥ २१ ॥
}} }} }}

Of the Adityas I am Vishnu; of radiances the glorious sun; I am Marîchi of the Maruts; of the asterisms the Moon am I. {{float right|{{larger|(21)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}<noinclude></noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader||TENTH DISCOURSE.|145}}</noinclude>{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
वेदानां सामवेदोऽस्मि देवानामस्मि वासवः ।

इन्द्रियाणां मनश्चास्मि भूतानामस्मि चेतना ॥ २२ ॥
}} }} }}

Of the Vedas I am the Sâma-Veda; I am Vâsava of the Shining Ones; and of the senses I am the mind<ref>Manah.</ref>; I am of living beings the intelligence<ref>{{SIC|Chetana|Chetanâ}}.</ref>. {{float right|{{larger|(22)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
रुद्राणां शङ्करश्चास्मि वित्तेशो यक्षरक्षसाम् ।

वसूनां पावकश्चास्मि मेरुः शिखरिणामहम् ॥ २३ ॥
}} }} }}

And of the Rudras<ref name="p145Celestial">Celestial beings.</ref> Shañkara am I; Vittesha of the Yakshas and Râkshasas<ref>Semi-human beings.</ref>; and of the Vasus<ref name="p145Celestial" /> I am Pâvaka; Meru of high mountains am I. {{float right|{{larger|(23)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
पुरोधसां च मुख्यं मां विद्धि पार्थ बृहस्पतिम् ।

सेनानीनामहं स्कन्दः सरसामस्मि सागरः ॥ २४ ॥
}} }} }}

And know Me, O Pârtha, of household priests the chief, Brihaspati: of generals I am Skanda; of lakes I am the ocean. {{float right|{{larger|(24)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}<noinclude>{{rule}}
{{smallrefs}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader|146|THE BHAGAVAD-GITA.|}}</noinclude>{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
महर्षीणां भृगुरहं गिरामस्म्येकमक्षरम् ।

यज्ञानां जपयज्ञोऽस्मि स्थावराणां हिमालयः ॥ २५ ॥
}} }} }}

Of the great Rishis Bhṛigu; of speech I am the one syllable<ref>Om.</ref>; of sacrifices I am the sacrifice of silent repetitions<ref>Japa.</ref>; of immovable things the Himâlaya. {{float right|{{larger|(25)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
अश्वत्थः सर्ववृक्षाणां देवर्षीणां च नारदः ।

गन्धर्वाणां चित्ररथः सिद्धानां कपिलो मुनिः ॥ २६ ॥
}} }} }}

Asvattha of all tree; and of divine Rishis Nârada; of Gandharvas<ref>Celestial Singers.</ref> Chitraratha; of the perfected the Muni Kapila. {{float right|{{larger|(26)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
उच्चैःश्रवसमश्वानां विद्धि माममृतोद्भवम् ।

ऐरावतं गजेन्द्राणां नराणां च नराधिपम् ॥ २७ ॥
}} }} }}

Uchchaishravas of horses know me, nectar-born<ref>Amrita, the nectar of immortality.</ref>; Airâvata of lordly elephants, and of men the Monarch. {{float right|{{larger|(27)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}<noinclude>{{rule}}
{{smallrefs}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader||TENTH DISCOURSE.|147}}</noinclude>{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
आयुधानामहं वज्रं धेनूनामस्मि कामधुक् ।

प्रजनश्चास्मि कन्दर्पः सर्पाणामस्मि वासुकिः ॥ २८ ॥
}} }} }}

Of weapons I am the thunderbolt; of cows I am Kâmadhuk; I am Kandarpa of the progenitors; of serpents Vâsuki am I. {{float right|{{larger|(28)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
अनन्तश्चास्मि नागानां वरुणो यादसामहम् ।

पितॄणामर्यमा चास्मि यमः संयमतामहम् ॥ २९ ॥
}} }} }}

And I am Ananta of Nâgas<ref>Serpents, who were Teachers of Wisdom.</ref>, Varuna of sea-dwellers I; and of ancestors Aryaman; Yama of governors am I. {{float right|{{larger|(29)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
प्रह्लादश्चास्मि दैत्यानां कालः कलयतामहम् ।

मृगाणां च मृगेन्द्रोऽहं वैनतेयश्च पक्षिणाम् ॥ ३० ॥
}} }} }}

And I am Prahlâda of Daityas;<ref>Semi-human beings.</ref> of calculators Time am I; and of wild beasts I the imperial beast;<ref>Lion.</ref> and Vainateya of birds. {{float right|{{larger|(30)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}<noinclude>{{rule}}
{{smallrefs}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader|148|THE BHAGAVAD-GITA.|}}</noinclude>{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
पवनः पवतामस्मि रामः शस्त्रभृतामहम् ।

झषाणां मकरश्चास्मि स्रोतसामस्मि जाह्नवी ॥ ३१ ॥ 
}} }} }}

Of purifiers I am the wind; Rama of warriors I; and I am Makara of fishes; of streams the Gangâ am I. {{float right|{{larger|{{SIC|{{gap}}|(31)}}}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
सर्गाणामादिरन्तश्च मध्यं चैवाहमर्जुन ।

अध्यात्मविद्या विद्यानां वादः प्रवदतामहम् ॥ ३२ ॥
}} }} }}

Of creations the beginning and the ending, and also the middle am I, O Arjuna. Of sciences the science concerning the {{sc|Self}}; the speech of orators I. {{float right|{{larger|(32)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
अक्षराणामकारोऽस्मि द्वन्द्वः सामासिकस्य च ।

अहमेवाक्षयः कालो धाताऽहं विश्वतोमुखः ॥ ३३ ॥
}} }} }}

Of letters the letter A I am, and the duality of a compound<ref>Dvanda.</ref>; I also everlasting Time; I the Supporter, whose face turns everywhere. {{float right|{{larger|(33)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}<noinclude>{{rule}}
{{smallrefs}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader||TENTH DISCOURSE.|149}}</noinclude>{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
मृत्युः सर्वहरश्चाहमुद्भवश्च भविष्यताम् ।

कीर्तिः श्रीर्वाक्च नारीणां स्मृतिर्मेधा धृतिः क्षमा ॥ ३४ ॥
}} }} }}

And all-devouring Death am I, and the origin of all to come; and of feminine qualities, fame, prosperity, speech, memory, intelligence, constancy, forgiveness. {{float right|{{larger|(34)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
बृहत्साम तथा साम्नां गायत्री छन्दसामहम् ।

मासानां मार्गशीर्षोऽहमृतूनां कुसुमाकरः ॥ ३५ ॥
}} }} }}

Of hymns also Brihatsâman; Gâyatrî of metres am I; of months I am Mârgasîrsha; of seasons the flowery. {{float right|{{larger|(35)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
द्यूतं छलयतामस्मि तेजस्तेजस्विनामहम् ।

जयोऽस्मि व्यवसायोऽस्मि सत्त्वं सत्त्ववतामहम् ॥ ३६ ॥
}} }} }}

I am the gambling of the cheat, and the splendour of splendid things I; I am victory, I am determination, and the truth of the truthful I. {{float right|{{larger|(36)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}<noinclude></noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader|150|THE BHAGAVAD-GITA.|}}</noinclude>{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
वृष्णीनां वासुदेवोऽस्मि पाण्डवानां धनञ्जयः ।

मुनीनामप्यहं व्यासः कवीनामुशना कविः ॥ ३७ ॥
}} }} }}

Of the Vṛishnis<ref name="p150family">A family, or clan, among the Hindus.</ref> Vâsudeva am I; of the Pândavas<ref name="p150family" /> Dhananjaya; of the Sages<ref>Munis.</ref> also I am Vyâsa; of poets Ushanâ the Bard. {{float right|{{larger|(37)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
दण्डो दमयतामस्मि नीतिरस्मि जिगीषताम् ।

मौनं चैवास्मि गुह्यानां ज्ञानं ज्ञानवतामहम् ॥ ३८ ॥
}} }} }}

Of rulers I am the sceptre; of those that seek victory I am statesmanship; and of secrets I am also silence; the knowledge of knowers am I. {{float right|{{larger|(38)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
यच्चापि सर्वभूतानां बीजं तदहमर्जुन ।

न तदस्ति विना यत्स्यान्मया भूतं चराचरम् ॥ ३९ ॥
}} }} }}
 
And whatsoever is the seed of all beings, that am I, O Arjuna; nor is there aught, moving or unmoving, that may exist bereft of Me. {{float right|{{larger|(39)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}<noinclude>{{rule}}
{{smallrefs}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader||TENTH DISCOURSE.|151}}</noinclude>{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
नान्तोऽस्ति मम दिव्यानां विभूतीनां परन्तप ।

एष तूद्देशतः प्रोक्तो विभूतेर्विस्तरो मया ॥ ४० ॥
}} }} }}

There is no end of My divine powers, O Parantapa. What has been declared is illustrative of My infinite glory. {{float right|{{larger|(40)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
यद्यद्विभूतिमत्सत्त्वं श्रीमदूर्जितमेव वा ।

तत्तदेवावगच्छ त्वं मम तेजोंऽशसम्भवम् ॥ ४१ ॥
}} }} }}

Whatsoever is glorious, good, beautiful, and mighty, understand thou that to go forth from a fragment of My splendour. {{float right|{{larger|(41)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
अथवा बहुनैतेन किं ज्ञातेन तवार्जुन ।

विष्टभ्याहमिदं कृत्स्नमेकांशेन स्थितो जगत् ॥ ४२ ॥
}} }} }}

But what is the knowledge of all these details to thee, O Arjuna? Having pervaded this whole universe with one fragment of Myself, I remain. {{float right|{{larger|(42)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
इति श्रीमद्भगवद्गीता॰ विभूतियोगो नाम दशमोऽध्यायः ।
}} }} }}
{{nop}}<noinclude></noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="4" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader|152|THE BHAGAVAD-GITA.|}}</noinclude>{{fine block|Thus in the glorious Upanishads of the {{sc|Bhagavad-Gita}}, the science of the {{sc|Eternal}}, the scripture of Yoga, the dialogue between Shri Krishna and Arjuna, the tenth discourse, entitled:}}

{{c|THE YOGA OF SOVEREIGNTY.}}


{{rule|3em}}<noinclude></noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" /></noinclude>{{dhr}}
{{c|{{larger|ELEVENTH DISCOURSE.}}}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
{{c|अर्जुन उवाच ।}}

मदनुग्रहाय परमं गुह्यमध्यात्मसंज्ञितम् ।

यत्त्वयोक्तं वचस्तेन मोहोऽयं विगतो मम ॥ १ ॥
}} }} }}

{{c|Arjuna said:}}

This word of the supreme Secret concerning the Self, Thou hast spoken out of compassion; by this my delusion is taken away. {{float right|{{larger|(1)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
भवाप्ययौ हि भूतानां श्रुतौ विस्तरशो मया ।

त्वत्तः कमलपत्राक्ष माहात्म्यमपि चाव्ययम् ॥ २ ॥
}} }} }}

The production and destruction of beings have been heard by me in detail from Thee, O Lotus-eyed, and also Thy imperishable greatness. {{float right|{{larger|(2)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
एवमेतद्यथाऽऽत्थ त्वमात्मानं परमेश्वर ।

द्रष्टुमिच्छामि ते रूपमैश्वरं पुरुषोत्तम ॥ ३ ॥
}} }} }}

O supreme Lord,<ref>Ishvara, the Creator and Ruler of a Universe.</ref> even as Thou describest<noinclude>{{rule}}
{{smallrefs}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader|154|THE BHAGAVAD-GITA.|}}</noinclude>Thyself, O best of beings, I desire to see Thy Form omnipotent. {{float right|{{larger|(3)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
मन्यसे यदि तच्छक्यं मया द्रष्टुमिति प्रभो ।

योगेश्वर ततो मे त्वं दर्शयात्मानमव्ययम् ॥ ४ ॥
}} }} }}

If Thou thinkest that by me It can be seen, O Lord, Lord of Yoga, then show me Thine imperishable Self. {{float right|{{larger|(4)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
{{c|श्रीभगवानुवाच ।}}

पश्य मे पार्थ रूपाणि शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः ।

नानाविधानि दिव्यानि नानावर्णाकृतीनि च ॥ ५ ॥
}} }} }}

{{c|The Blessed Lord said:}}

Behold, O Pârtha, a Form of Me, a hundredfold, a thousandfold, various in kind, divine, various in colours and shapes. {{float right|{{larger|(5)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
पश्यादित्यान्वसून्रुद्रानश्विनौ मरुतस्तथा ।

बहून्यदृष्टपूर्वाणि पश्याश्चर्याणि भारत ॥ ६ ॥
}} }} }}

Behold the Âdityas, the Vasus, the Rudras,<noinclude></noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader||ELEVENTH DISCOURSE.|155}}</noinclude>the two Ashvins and also the Maruts<ref>Various classes of Celestial Beings.</ref>; behold many marvels never seen ere this, O Bhârata. {{float right|{{larger|(6)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|

}} }} }}

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader||ELEVENTH DISCOURSE.|169}}</noinclude>{{block center|width=350px|<poem>
How should they otherwise, O loftiest Self!
First Cause! Brahmâ Himself less great than Thou.
Infinite, God of Gods, home of all worlds,
Unperishing, Sat, Asat,<ref>Being, Non-Being.</ref> {{sc|That}} supreme! {{float right|{{larger|(37)}}}}</poem>}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
त्वमादिदेवः पुरुषः पुराणस्त्वमस्य विश्वस्य परं निधानम् ।

वेत्ताऽसि वेद्यं च परं च धाम त्वया ततं विश्वमनन्तरूप ॥ ३८ ॥
}} }} }}

{{block center|width=350px|<poem>
First of the Gods, most ancient Man Thou art.
Supreme receptacle of all that lives;
Knower and known, the dwelling-place on high;
In Thy vast Form the universe is spread. {{float right|{{larger|(38)}}}}</poem>}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
वायुर्यमोऽग्निर्वरुणः शशाङ्कः प्रजापतिस्त्वं प्रपितामहश्च ।

नमो नमस्तेऽस्तु सहस्रकृत्वः पुनश्च भूयोऽपि नमो नमस्ते ॥ ३९ ॥
}} }} }}
{{nop}}<noinclude>{{rule}}
{{smallrefs}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader|170|THE BHAGAVAD-GITA.|}}</noinclude>{{block center|width=350px|<poem>
Thou art Vâyu and Yama, Agni, moon,
Varuna, Father, Grandsire of all;
