Hail, hail to Thee! a thousand times all hail!
Hail unto Thee! again, again all hail! {{float right|{{larger|(39)}}}}</poem>}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
नमः पुरस्तादथ पृष्ठतस्ते

नमोऽस्तु ते सर्वत एव सर्व ।

अनन्तवीर्यामितविक्रमस्त्वम्

सर्वं समाप्नोषि ततोऽसि सर्वः ॥ ४० ॥
}} }} }}

{{block center|width=350px|<poem>
Prostrate in front of Thee, prostrate behind;
Prostrate on every side to Thee, O All.
In power boundless, measureless in strength,
Thou holdest all: then Thou Thyself art All. {{float right|{{larger|(40)}}}}</poem>}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
सखेति मत्वा प्रसभं यदुक्तम्

हे कृष्ण हे यादव हे सखेति ।

अजानता महिमानं तवेदम्

मया प्रमादात्प्रणयेन वापि ॥ ४१ ॥
}} }} }}
{{nop}}<noinclude></noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader||ELEVENTH DISCOURSE.|171}}</noinclude>{{block center|width=350px|<poem>
If, thinking Thee but friend, importunate,
O Krishna! or O Yâdava! O friend!
I cried, unknowing of Thy majesty,
And careless in the fondness of my love; {{float right|{{larger|(41)}}}}</poem>}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
यच्चावहासार्थमसत्कृतोऽसि

विहारशय्यासनभोजनेषु ।

एकोऽथवाऽप्यच्युत तत्समक्षम्

तत्क्षामये त्वामहमप्रमेयम् ॥ ४२ ॥
}} }} }}

{{block center|width=350px|<poem>
If jesting I irreverence showed to Thee,
At play, reposing, sitting or at meals,
Alone, O sinless One, or with my friends,
Forgive my error, O Thou boundless One. {{float right|{{larger|(42)}}}}</poem>}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
पिताऽसि लोकस्य चराचरस्य

त्वमस्य पूज्यश्च गुरुर्गरीयान् ।

न त्वत्समोऽस्त्यभ्यधिकः कुतोऽन्यो

लोकत्रयेऽप्यप्रतिमप्रभावः ॥ ४३ ॥
}} }} }}

{{block center/s|width=350px}}<poem>
Father of worlds, of all that moves and stands,
Worthier of reverence than the Guru's self,
</poem><noinclude>{{block center/e}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader|172|THE BHAGAVAD-GITA.|}}
{{block center/s|width=350px}}</noinclude><poem>
There is none like to Thee. Who passeth Thee?
Pre-eminent Thy power in all the worlds. {{float right|{{larger|(43)}}}}</poem>
{{block center/e}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
तस्मात्प्रणम्य प्रणिधाय कायम्

प्रसादये त्वामहमीशमीड्यम् ।

पितेव पुत्रस्य सखेव सख्युः

प्रियः प्रियायार्हसि देव सोढुम् ॥ ४४ ॥
}} }} }}

{{block center|width=350px|<poem>
Therefore I fall before Thee; with my body
I worship as it fitting; bless Thou me.
As father with the son, as friend with friend,
With the beloved as lover, bear with me. {{float right|{{larger|(44)}}}}</poem>}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
अदृष्टपूर्वं हृषितोऽस्मि दृष्ट्वा

भयेन च प्रव्यथितं मनो मे ।

तदेव मे दर्शय देव रूपम्

प्रसीद देवेश जगन्निवास ॥ ४५ ॥
}} }} }}

{{block center|width=350px|<poem>
I have seen that which none hath seen before,
My heart is glad, yet faileth me for fear;
Show me, O God, Thine other Form again—
Mercy, O God of Gods, home of all worlds— {{float right|{{larger|(45)}}}}</poem>}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}<noinclude></noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader||ELEVENTH DISCOURSE.|173}}</noinclude>{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
किरीटिनं गदिनं चक्रहस्तमिच्छामि त्वां द्रष्टुमहं तथैव ।

तेनैव रूपेण चतुर्भुजेन सहस्रबाहो भव विश्वमूर्ते ॥ ४६ ॥
}} }} }}

{{block center|width=350px|<poem>
Diademed, mace and discus in Thy hand.
Again I fain would see Thee as before;
Put on again Thy four-armed shape, O Lord,
O thousand-armed, of forms innumerate. {{float right|{{larger|(46)}}}}</poem>}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
{{c|श्रीभगवानुवाच ।}}

मया प्रसन्नेन तवार्जुनेदम्

रूपं परं दर्शितमात्मयोगात् ।

तेजोमयं विश्वमनन्तमाद्यम्

यन्मे त्वदन्येन न दृष्टपूर्वम् ॥ ४७ ॥
}} }} }}

{{c|The Blessed Lord said:}}

{{block center/s|width=350px}}<poem>
Arjuna, by My favour thou hast seen,
This loftiest Form by yoga's self revealed!
</poem><noinclude>{{block center/e}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader|174|THE BHAGAVAD-GITA.|}}
{{block center/s|width=350px}}</noinclude><poem>
Radiant, all-penetrating, endless, first,
That none except thyself hath ever seen. {{float right|{{larger|(47)}}}}</poem>
{{block center/e}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
न वेदयज्ञाध्ययनैर्न दानैर्न च क्रियाभिर्न तपोभिरुग्रैः ।

एवंरूपः शक्य अहं नृलोके द्रष्टुं त्वदन्येन कुरुप्रवीर ॥ ४८ ॥
}} }} }}

{{block center|width=350px|<poem>
Nor sacrifice, nor Vedas, alms, nor works,
Nor sharp austerity, nor study deep,
Can win the vision of this Form for man,
Foremost of Kurus, thou alone hast seen. {{float right|{{larger|(48)}}}}</poem>}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
मा ते व्यथा मा च विमूढभावो

दृष्ट्वा रूपं घोरमीदृङ्ममेदम् ।

व्यपेतभीः प्रीतमनाः पुनस्त्वम्

तदेव मे रूपमिदं प्रपश्य ॥ ४९ ॥
}} }} }}

{{block center|width=350px|<poem>
Be not bewildered, be thou not afraid,
Because thou hast beheld this awful Form;
Cast fear away, and let thy heart rejoice;
Behold again Mine own familiar shape. {{float right|{{larger|(49)}}}}</poem>}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}<noinclude></noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader||ELEVENTH DISCOURSE.|175}}</noinclude>{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
{{c|सञ्जय उवाच ।}}

इत्यर्जुनं वासुदेवस्तथोक्त्वा

स्वकं रूपं दर्शयामास भूयः ।

आश्वासयामास च भीतमेनम्

भूत्वा पुनः सौम्यवपुर्महात्मा ॥ ५० ॥
}} }} }}

{{c|Sanjaya said:}}

Vâsudeva, having thus spoken to Arjuna, again manifested His own Form, and consoled the terrified one, the Mahâtman again assuming a gentle form. {{float right|{{larger|(50)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
{{c|अर्जुन उवाच ।}}

दृष्ट्वेदं मानुषं रूपं तव सौम्यं जनार्दन ।

इदानीमस्मि संवृत्तः सचेताः प्रकृतिं गतः ॥ ५१ ॥
}} }} }}

{{c|Arjuna said:}}

Beholding again Thy gentle human Form, O Janârdana, I am now collected, and am restored to my own nature. {{float right|{{larger|(51)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}<noinclude></noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader|176|THE BHAGAVAD-GITA.|}}</noinclude>{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
{{c|श्रीभगवानुवाच ।}}

सुदुर्दर्शमिदं रूपं दृष्टवानसि यन्मम ।

देवा अप्यस्य रूपस्य नित्यं दर्शनकाङ्क्षिणः ॥ ५२ ॥
}} }} }}

{{c|The Blessed Lord said:}}

This Form of Mine beholden by thee is very hard to see. Verily the Shining Ones ever long to behold this form. {{float right|{{larger|(52)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
नाहं वेदैर्न तपसा न दानेन न चेज्यया ।

शक्य एवंविधो द्रष्टुं दृष्टवानसि मां यथा ॥ ५३ ॥
}} }} }}

Nor can I be seen as thou hast seen Me by the Vedas, nor by austerities, nor by alms, or by offerings; {{float right|{{larger|(53)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
भक्त्या त्वनन्यया शक्य अहमेवंविधोऽर्जुन ।

ज्ञातुं द्रष्टुं च तत्त्वेन प्रवेष्टुं च परन्तप ॥ ५४ ॥
}} }} }}

But by devotion to Me alone I may thus be perceived, Arjuna, and known and seen in essence, and entered, O Parantapa. {{float right|{{larger|(54)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}<noinclude></noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader||ELEVENTH DISCOURSE.|177}}</noinclude>{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
मत्कर्मकृन्मत्परमो मद्भक्तः सङ्गवर्जितः ।

निर्वैरः सर्वभूतेषु यः स मामेति पाण्डव ॥ ५५ ॥
}} }} }}

He who doeth actions for Me, whose supreme good I am, My devotee, freed from attachment without hatred of any being, he cometh unto Me, O Pândava. {{float right|{{larger|(55)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
इति श्रीमद्भगवद्गीता॰ विश्वरूपदर्शनयोगो नामैकादशोऽध्यायः ।
}} }} }}
 
{{fine block|Thus in the glorious Upanishads of the Bhagavad-Gita, the science of the Eternal, the scripture of Yoga, the dialogue between Shri Krishna and Arjuna, the eleventh discourse, entitled:}}

{{c|THE YOGA OF THE VISION OF THE UNIVERSAL FORM.}}


{{rule|3em}}<noinclude></noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" /></noinclude>{{dhr}}
{{c|{{larger|TWELFTH DISCOURSE.}}}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
{{c|अर्जुन उवाच ।}}

एवं सततयुक्ता ये भक्तास्त्वां पर्युपासते ।

ये चाप्यक्षरमव्यक्तं तेषां के योगवित्तमाः ॥ १ ॥
}} }} }}

{{c|Arjuna said:}}

Those devotees who ever harmonised worship Thee, and those also who worship the Indestructible, the Unmanifested, {{SIC|whether}} of these is the more learned in yoga? {{float right|{{larger|(1)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
{{c|श्रीभगवानुवाच ।}}

मय्यावेश्य मनो ये मां नित्ययुक्ता उपासते ।

श्रद्धया परयोपेतास्ते मे युक्ततमा मताः ॥ २ ॥
}} }} }}

{{c|The Blessed Lord said:}}

They who with mind<ref>Manah.</ref> fixed on Me ever harmonised worship Me, with faith supreme endowed, these, in My opinion, are best in yoga. {{float right|{{larger|(2)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}<noinclude>{{rule}}
{{smallrefs}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader||TWELFTH DISCOURSE.|179}}</noinclude>{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
ये त्वक्षरमनिर्देश्यमव्यक्तं पर्युपासते ।

सर्वत्रगमचिन्त्यं च कूटस्थमचलं ध्रुवम् ॥ ३ ॥
}} }} }}

They who worship the Indestructible, the Ineffable, the unmanifested, Omnipresent, and Unthinkable, the Unchanging, Immutable, Eternal, {{float right|{{larger|(3)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
संनियम्येन्द्रियग्रामं सर्वत्र समबुद्धयः ।

ते प्राप्नुवन्ति मामेव सर्वभूतहिते रताः ॥ ४ ॥
}} }} }}

Restraining and subduing the senses, regarding everything equally, in the welfare of all rejoicing, these also come unto Me. {{float right|{{larger|(4)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
क्लेशोऽधिकतरस्तेषामव्यक्तासक्तचेतसाम् ।

अव्यक्ता हि गतिर्दुःखं देहवद्भिरवाप्यते ॥ ५ ॥
}} }} }}

The difficulty of those whose minds are set on the Unmanifested is greater; for the path of the Unmanifested is hard for the embodied to reach. {{float right|{{larger|(5)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}<noinclude></noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader|180|THE BHAGAVAD-GITA.|}}</noinclude>{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
ये तु सर्वाणि कर्माणि मयि संन्यस्य मत्पराः ।

अनन्येनैव योगेन मां ध्यायन्त उपासते ॥ ६ ॥
}} }} }}

Those verily who, renouncing all actions in Me and intent on Me, worship meditating on Me, with whole-hearted yoga, {{float right|{{larger|(6)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
तेषामहं समुद्धर्ता मृत्युसंसारसागरात् ।

भवामि न चिरात्पार्थ मय्यावेशितचेतसाम् ॥ ७ ॥
}} }} }}

These I speedily lift up from the ocean of death and existence, O Pârtha, their minds<ref>Chetah.</ref> being fixed on Me. {{float right|{{larger|(7)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
मय्येव मन आधत्स्व मयि बुद्धिं निवेशय ।

निवसिष्यसि मय्येव अत ऊर्ध्वं न संशयः ॥ ८ ॥
}} }} }}

Place thy mind<ref>Manah.</ref> in me, into Me let thy Reason<ref>Buddhi.</ref> enter; then without doubt thou shalt abide in Me hereafter. {{float right|{{larger|(8)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
अथ चित्तं समाधातुं न शक्नोषि मयि स्थिरम् ।

अभ्यासयोगेन ततो मामिच्छाप्तुं धनञ्जय ॥ ९ ॥
}} }} }}

And if thou art not able firmly to fix thy mind<ref>Chitta.</ref><noinclude>{{rule}}
{{smallrefs}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader||TWELFTH DISCOURSE.|181}}</noinclude>on Me, then by the yoga of practice seek to reach Me, O Dhananjaya. {{float right|{{larger|(9)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
अभ्यासेऽप्यसमर्थोऽसि मत्कर्मपरमो भव ।

मदर्थमपि कर्माणि कुर्वन्सिद्धिमवाप्स्यसि ॥ १० ॥
}} }} }}
 
If also thou art not equal to constant practice, be intent on My service; performing actions for My sake, thou shalt attain perfection. {{float right|{{larger|(10)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
अथैतदप्यशक्तोऽसि कर्तुं मद्योगमाश्रितः ।

सर्वकर्मफलत्यागं ततः कुरु यतात्मवान् ॥ ११ ॥
}} }} }}

If even to do this thou hast not strength, then, taking refuge in union with Me, renounce all fruit of action with the self controlled. {{float right|{{larger|(11)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
श्रेयो हि ज्ञानमभ्यासाज्ज्ञानाद्ध्यानं विशिष्यते ।

ध्यानात्कर्मफलत्यागस्त्यागाच्छान्तिरनन्तरम् ॥ १२ ॥
}} }} }}

Better indeed is wisdom than constant-practice; than wisdom, meditation is better;<noinclude></noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader|182|THE BHAGAVAD-GITA.|}}</noinclude>than meditation, renunciation of the fruit of action; on renunciation follows peace. {{float right|{{larger|(12)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
अद्वेष्टा सर्वभूतानां मैत्रः करुण एव च ।

निर्ममो निरहङ्कारः समदुःखसुखः क्षमी ॥ १३ ॥
}} }} }}

He who beareth no ill-will to any being, friendly and compassionate, without attachment and egoism, balanced in pleasure and pain, and forgiving, {{float right|{{larger|(13)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
सन्तुष्टः सततं योगी यतात्मा दृढनिश्चयः ।

मय्यर्पितमनोबुद्धिर्यो मे भक्तः स मे प्रियः ॥ १४ ॥
}} }} }}

Ever content, harmonious, with the self-controlled, resolute, with mind<ref>Manah.</ref> and Reason<ref>Buddhi.</ref> dedicated to Me, he, My devotee, is dear to Me. {{float right|{{larger|(14)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
यस्मान्नोद्विजते लोको लोकान्नोद्विजते च यः ।

हर्षामर्षभयोद्वेगैर्मुक्तो यः स च मे प्रियः ॥ १५ ॥
}} }} }}
{{nop}}<noinclude>{{rule}}
{{smallrefs}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader||TWELFTH DISCOURSE.|183}}</noinclude>He from whom the world doth not shrink away, who doth not shrink away from the world, freed from the anxieties of joy, anger, and fear, he is dear to me. {{float right|{{larger|(15)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
अनपेक्षः शुचिर्दक्ष उदासीनो गतव्यथः ।

सर्वारम्भपरित्यागी यो मद्भक्तः स मे प्रियः ॥ १६ ॥
}} }} }}

He who wants nothing, is pure, expert, passionless, untroubled, renouncing every undertaking, he, My devotee, is dear to Me. {{float right|{{larger|(16)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
यो न हृष्यति न द्वेष्टि न शोचति न काङ्क्षति ।

शुभाशुभपरित्यागी भक्तिमान्यः स मे प्रियः ॥ १७ ॥
}} }} }}

He who neither loveth nor hateth, nor grieveth, nor desireth, renouncing good and evil, full of devotion, he is dear to Me. {{float right|{{larger|(17)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
समः शत्रौ च मित्रे च तथा {{SIC|मानपमानयोः|मानापमानयोः}} ।

शीतोष्णसुखदुःखेषु समः सङ्गविवर्जितः ॥ १८ ॥
}} }} }}
{{nop}}<noinclude></noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader|184|THE BHAGAVAD-GITA.|}}</noinclude>Alike to foe and friend, and also in fame and ignominy, alike in cold and heat, pleasures and pains, destitute of attachment, {{float right|{{larger|(18)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
तुल्यनिन्दास्तुतिर्मौनी सन्तुष्टो येनकेनचित् ।

अनिकेतः स्थिरमतिर्भक्तिमान्मे प्रियो नरः ॥ १९ ॥
}} }} }}
 
Taking equally praise and reproach, silent, wholly content with what cometh, homeless, firm in mind, full of devotion, that man is dear to Me. {{float right|{{larger|(19)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
ये तु धर्म्यामृतमिदं यथोक्तं पर्युपासते ।

श्रद्दधाना मत्परमा भक्तास्तेऽतीव मे प्रियाः ॥ २० ॥
}} }} }}

They verily who partake of this life-giving wisdom<ref>Amrita-Dharma.</ref> as taught herein, endued with faith, I their supreme Object, devotees, they are surpassingly dear to Me. {{float right|{{larger|(20)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}<noinclude>{{rule}}
{{smallrefs}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader||TWELFTH DISCOURSE.|185}}</noinclude>{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
इति श्रीमद्भगवद्गीता॰ भक्तियोगो नाम द्वादशोऽध्यायः ।
}} }} }}

{{fine block|Thus in the glorious Upanishads of the Bhagavad-Gita, the science of the {{sc|Eternal}}, the scripture of Yoga, the dialogue between Shri Krishna and Arjuna, the twelfth discourse, entitled:}}

{{c|THE YOGA OF DEVOTION.}}


{{rule|3em}}<noinclude></noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" /></noinclude>{{dhr}}
{{c|{{larger|THIRTEENTH DISCOURSE.}}}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
{{c|अर्जुन उवाच ।}}

प्रकृतिं पुरुषं चैव क्षेत्रं क्षेत्रज्ञमेव च ।

एतद्वेदितुमिच्छामि ज्ञानं ज्ञेयं च केशव ॥ १ ॥
}} }} }}

{{c|Arjuna said:}}
 
Matter and Spirit,<ref>Prakriti and Purusha.</ref> even the Field and the Knower of the Field, wisdom and that which ought to be known, these I fain would learn, O Keshava. {{float right|{{larger|(1)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
{{c|श्रीभगवानुवाच ।}}

इदं शरीरं कौन्तेय क्षेत्रमित्यभिधीयते ।

एतद्यो वेत्ति तं प्राहुः क्षेत्रज्ञ इति तद्विदः ॥ २ ॥
}} }} }}

{{c|The Blessed Lord said:}}

This body, son of Kuntî, is called the Field; that which knoweth it is called the Knower of the Field by the Sages. {{float right|{{larger|(2)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}<noinclude>{{rule}}
{{smallrefs}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader||THIRTEENTH DISCOURSE.|187}}</noinclude>{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
क्षेत्रज्ञं चापि मां विद्धि सर्वक्षेत्रेषु भारत ।{{parabr}}
क्षेत्रक्षेत्रज्ञयोर्ज्ञानं यत्तज्ज्ञानं मतं मम ॥ ३ ॥
}} }} }}

Understand Me as the Knower of the Field in all Fields, O Bhârata. Wisdom as to the Field and the Knower of the Field, that in My opinion is the wisdom. {{float right|{{larger|(3)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
तत्क्षेत्रं यच्च यादृक् च यद्विकारि यतश्च यत् ।{{parabr}}
स च यो यत्प्रभावश्च तत्समासेन मे शृणु ॥ ४ ॥
}} }} }}

What that Field is and of what nature, how modified, and whence it is, and what He<ref>Kshetrajña, the Knower of the Field.</ref> is and what His powers, hear that now briefly from Me. {{float right|{{larger|(4)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
ऋषिभिर्बहुधा गीतं छन्दोभिर्विविधैः पृथक् ।{{parabr}}
ब्रह्मसूत्रपदैश्चैव हेतुमद्भिर्विनिश्चितैः ॥ ५ ॥
}} }} }}

Rishis have sung in manifold ways, in many various chants, and in decisive Brahma-sûtra verses<ref>Short terse sayings, concerning the {{sc|Eternal}}.</ref> full of reasonings. {{float right|{{larger|(5)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}<noinclude>{{rule}}
{{smallrefs}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader|188|THE BHAGAVAD-GITA.|}}</noinclude>{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
महाभूतान्यहङ्कारो बुद्धिरव्यक्तमेव च ।{{parabr}}
इन्द्रियाणि दशैकं च पञ्च चेन्द्रियगोचराः ॥ ६ ॥
}} }} }}

The great Elements, Individuality<ref>Ahañkara</ref>, Reason<ref>Buddhi.</ref>, and also the unmanifested, the ten senses and the one, and the five pastures of the senses<ref>The five organs of knowledge, or senses, the five organs of action, the mind, and the object cognised by each of the five senses.</ref>; {{float right|{{larger|(6)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
इच्छा द्वेषः सुखं दुःखं सङ्घातश्चेतना धृतिः ।{{parabr}}
एतत्क्षेत्रं समासेन सविकारमुदाहृतम् ॥ ७ ॥
}} }} }}

Desire, aversion, pleasure, pain, combination<ref>The body.</ref>, intelligence, firmness; these, briefly described, constitute the Field and its modifications. {{float right|{{larger|(7)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
अमानित्वमदम्भित्वमहिंसा क्षान्तिरार्जवम् ।{{parabr}}
आचार्योपासनं शौचं स्थैर्यमात्मविनिग्रहः ॥ ८ ॥
}} }} }}

Humility, unpretentiousness, harmlessness,<noinclude>{{rule}}
{{smallrefs}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader||THIRTEENTH DISCOURSE.|189}}</noinclude>forgiveness, rectitude, service of the teacher, purity, steadfastness, self-control. {{float right|{{larger|(8)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
इन्द्रियार्थेषु वैराग्यमनहङ्कार एव च ।{{parabr}}
जन्ममृत्युजराव्याधिदुःखदोषानुदर्शनम् ॥ ९ ॥
}} }} }}

Dispassion towards the objects of the senses, and also absence of egoism, insight into the pain and evil of birth, death, old age and sickness, {{float right|{{larger|(9)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
असक्तिरनभिष्वङ्गः पुत्रदारगृहादिषु ।{{parabr}}
नित्यं च समचित्तत्वमिष्टानिष्टोपपत्तिषु ॥ १० ॥
}} }} }}
 
Unattachment, absence of self-identification with son, wife or home, and constant balance of mind in wished-for and unwished-for events, {{float right|{{larger|(10)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
मयि चानन्ययोगेन भक्तिरव्यभिचारिणी ।{{parabr}}
विविक्तदेशसेवित्वमरतिर्जनसंसदि ॥ ११ ॥
}} }} }}

Unflinching devotion to Me by yoga, without<noinclude></noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader|190|THE BHAGAVAD-GITA.|}}</noinclude>other objects, resort to sequestered places, absence of enjoyment in the company of men, {{float right|{{larger|(11)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
अध्यात्मज्ञाननित्यत्वं तत्त्वज्ञानार्थदर्शनम् ।{{parabr}}
एतज्ज्ञानमिति प्रोक्तमज्ञानं यदतोऽन्यथा ॥ १२ ॥
}} }} }}

Constancy in the wisdom of the Self,<ref>Adhyâtma; see vii, 29.</ref> understanding of the object of essential wisdom; that is declared to be the Wisdom; all against it is ignorance. {{float right|{{larger|(12)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
ज्ञेयं यत्तत्प्रवक्ष्यामि यज्ज्ञात्वाऽमृतमश्नुते ।{{parabr}}
अनादिमत्परं ब्रह्म न सत्तन्नासदुच्यते ॥ १३ ॥
}} }} }}

I will declare that which ought to be known, that which being known immortality is enjoyed—the beginningless supreme {{sc|Eternal}}, called neither being nor non-being. {{float right|{{larger|(13)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
सर्वतः पाणिपादं तत्सर्वतोऽक्षिशिरोमुखम् ।{{parabr}}
सर्वतः श्रुतिमल्लोके सर्वमावृत्य तिष्ठति ॥ १४ ॥
}} }} }}

Everywhere {{sc|That}} hath hands and feet,<noinclude>{{rule}}
{{smallrefs}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader||THIRTEENTH DISCOURSE.|191}}</noinclude>everywhere eyes, heads, and mouths; all-hearing, He dwelleth in the world, enveloping all, {{float right|{{larger|(14)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
सर्वेन्द्रियगुणाभासं सर्वेन्द्रियविवर्जितम् ।{{parabr}}
असक्तं सर्वभृच्चैव निर्गुणं गुणभोक्तृ च ॥ १५ ॥
}} }} }}
 
Shining with all sense-faculties without any senses; unattached supporting everything and free from qualities<ref name="p191Gunas">Gunas.</ref> enjoying qualities;<ref name="p191Gunas" /> {{float right|{{larger|(15)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
बहिरन्तश्च भूतानामचरं चरमेव च ।{{parabr}}
सूक्ष्मत्वात्तदविज्ञेयं दूरस्थं चान्तिके च तत् ॥ १६ ॥
}} }} }}

Without and within all beings, immovable and also movable; by reason of His subtlety imperceptible; at hand and far away is {{sc|That}}. {{float right|{{larger|(16)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
अविभक्तं च भूतेषु विभक्तमिव च स्थितम् ।{{parabr}}
भूतभर्तृ च तज्ज्ञेयं ग्रसिष्णु प्रभविष्णु च ॥ १७ ॥
}} }} }}

Not divided amid beings, and yet seated<noinclude>{{rule}}
{{smallrefs}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader|192|THE BHAGAVAD-GITA.|}}</noinclude>distributively; {{sc|that}} is to be known as the supporter of beings; He devours and He generates. {{float right|{{larger|(17)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
ज्योतिषामपि तज्ज्योतिस्तमसः परमुच्यते ।{{parabr}}
ज्ञानं ज्ञेयं ज्ञानगम्यं हृदि सर्वस्य धिष्ठितम् ॥ १८ ॥
}} }} }}

{{sc|That}}, the Light of all lights, is said to be beyond darkness; Wisdom, the Object of Wisdom, by Wisdom to be reached, seated in the hearts of all. {{float right|{{larger|(18)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
इति क्षेत्रं तथा ज्ञानं ज्ञेयं चोक्तं समासतः ।{{parabr}}
मद्भक्त एतद्विज्ञाय मद्भावायोपपद्यते ॥ १९ ॥
}} }} }}

Thus the Field, Wisdom and the Object of Wisdom, have been briefly told. My devotee, thus knowing, enters into My Being. {{float right|{{larger|(19)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
प्रकृतिं पुरुषं चैव विद्ध्यनादी उभावपि ।{{parabr}}
विकारांश्च गुणांश्चैव विद्धि प्रकृतिसंभवान् ॥ २० ॥
}} }} }}
{{nop}}<noinclude></noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader||THIRTEENTH DISCOURSE.|193}}</noinclude>Know thou that Matter<ref name="p193Prakriti">Prakriti.</ref> and Spirit<ref name="p193Purusha">Purusha.</ref> are both without beginning; and know thou also that modifications and qualities<ref name="p193Gunas">Gunas.</ref> are all Matter<ref name="p193Prakriti" />-born. {{float right|{{larger|(20)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
कार्यकारणकर्तृत्वे हेतुः प्रकृतिरुच्यते ।{{parabr}}
पुरुषः सुखदुःखानां भोक्तृत्वे हेतुरुच्यते ॥ २१ ॥
}} }} }}


Matter<ref name="p193Prakriti" /> is called the cause of the generation of causes and effects; Spirit<ref name="p193Purusha" /> is called the cause of the enjoyment of pleasure and pain. {{float right|{{larger|(21)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
पुरुषः प्रकृतिस्थो हि भुङ्‌क्ते प्रकृतिजान्गुणान् ।{{parabr}}
कारणं गुणसङ्गोऽस्य सदसद्योनिजन्मसु ॥ २२ ॥
}} }} }}


Spirit<ref name="p193Purusha" /> seated in Matter<ref name="p193Prakriti" /> useth the qualities born of Matter<ref name="p193Prakriti" />; attachment to the qualities<ref name="p193Gunas" /> is the cause of his births in good and evil wombs. {{float right|{{larger|(22)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
उपद्रष्टाऽनुमन्ता च भर्ता भोक्ता महेश्वरः ।{{parabr}}
परमात्मेति चाप्युक्तो देहेऽस्मिन्पुरुषः परः ॥ २३ ॥
}} }} }}
{{nop}}<noinclude>{{rule}}
{{smallrefs}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader|194|THE BHAGAVAD-GITA.|}}</noinclude>Supervisor and permitter, supporter, enjoyer, the great Lord, and also the supreme {{sc|Self}}; thus is styled in this body the supreme Spirit.{{SIC|<ref name="p193Prakriti" />|<ref name="p193Purusha" />}} {{float right|{{larger|(23)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
य एवं वेत्ति पुरुषं प्रकृतिं च गुणैः सह ।{{parabr}}
सर्वथा वर्तमानोऽपि न स भूयोऽभिजायते ॥ २४ ॥
}} }} }}

He who thus knoweth Spirit<ref name="p193Purusha" /> and Matter<ref name="p193Prakriti" /> with its qualities,<ref name="p193Gunas" /> in whatsoever condition he may be, he shall not be born again. {{float right|{{larger|(24)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
ध्यानेनात्मनि पश्यन्ति केचिदात्मानमात्मना ।{{parabr}}
अन्ये साङ्ख्येन योगेन कर्मयोगेन चापरे ॥ २५ ॥
}} }} }}

Some by meditation behold the {{sc|Self}} in the self by the {{sc|Self}}; others by the Sânkhya Yoga, and others by the Yoga of Action; {{float right|{{larger|(25)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
अन्ये त्वेवमजानन्तः श्रुत्वाऽन्येभ्य उपासते ।{{parabr}}
तेऽपि चातितरन्त्येव मृत्युं श्रुतिपरायणाः ॥ २६ ॥
}} }} }}

Others also, ignorant of this, having heard of it<noinclude>{{rule}}
{{smallrefs|refx=<ref name="p193Prakriti">Prakriti.</ref><ref name="p193Purusha">Purusha.</ref><ref name="p193Gunas">Gunas.</ref>}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader||THIRTEENTH DISCOURSE.|195}}</noinclude>from others, worship; and these also cross beyond death, adhering to what they had heard. {{float right|{{larger|(26)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
यावत्सञ्जायते किञ्चित्सत्त्वं स्थावरजङ्गमम् ।{{parabr}}
क्षेत्रक्षेत्रज्ञसंयोगात्तद्विद्धि भरतर्षभ ॥ २७ ॥
}} }} }}

Whatsoever creature is born immobile or mobile, know thou, O best of the Bhâratas, that it is from the union between the Field and the Knower of the Field. {{float right|{{larger|(27)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
समं सर्वेषु भूतेषु तिष्ठन्तं परमेश्वरम् ।{{parabr}}
विनश्यत्स्वविनश्यन्तं यः पश्यति स पश्यति ॥ २८ ॥
}} }} }}

Seated equally in all beings, the supreme Lord, unperishing within the perishing—he who thus seeth, he seeth. {{float right|{{larger|(28)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
समं पश्यन्हि सर्वत्र समवस्थितमीश्वरम् ।{{parabr}}
न हिनस्त्यात्मनाऽऽत्मानं ततो याति परां गतिम् ॥ २९ ॥
}} }} }}

Seeing indeed everywhere the same Lord equally dwelling, he doth not destroy the {{sc|Self}}, and thus treads the highest Path. {{float right|{{larger|(29)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}<noinclude></noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader|196|THE BHAGAVAD-GITA.|}}</noinclude>{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
प्रकृत्यैव च कर्माणि क्रियमाणानि सर्वशः ।{{parabr}}
यः पश्यति तथाऽऽत्मानमकर्तारं स पश्यति ॥ ३० ॥
}} }} }}

He who seeth that Matter<ref name="p193Prakriti" /> verily performeth all actions, and that the {{sc|Self}} is actionless, he seeth. {{float right|{{larger|(30)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
यदा भूतपृथग्भावमेकस्थमनुपश्यति ।{{parabr}}
तत एव च विस्तारं ब्रह्म संपद्यते तदा ॥ ३१ ॥
}} }} }}

When he perceiveth the diversified existence of beings as rooted in One, and spreading forth from it, then he reacheth the {{sc|Eternal}} {{float right|{{larger|(31)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
अनादित्वान्निर्गुणत्वात्परमात्माऽयमव्ययः ।{{parabr}}
शरीरस्थोऽपि कौन्तेय न करोति न लिप्यते ॥ ३२ ॥
}} }} }}

Being beginningless and without qualities<ref name="p193Gunas" />, the imperishable supreme {{sc|Self}}, though seated in the body, O Kaunteya, worketh not nor is affected. {{float right|{{larger|(32)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}<noinclude>{{rule}}
{{smallrefs|refx=<ref name="p193Prakriti">Prakriti.</ref><ref name="p193Gunas">Gunas.</ref>}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader||THIRTEENTH DISCOURSE.|197}}</noinclude>{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
यथा सर्वगतं सौक्ष्म्यादाकाशं नोपलिप्यते ।{{parabr}}
सर्वत्रावस्थितो देहे {{SIC|तथाऽऽमा|तथाऽऽत्मा}} नोपलिप्यते ॥ ३३ ॥
}} }} }}

As the omnipresent ether is not affected, by reason of its subtlety, so seated everywhere in the body the {{sc|Self}} is not affected. {{float right|{{larger|(33)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
यथा प्रकाशयत्येकः कृत्स्नं लोकमिमं रविः ।{{parabr}}
क्षेत्रं क्षेत्री तथा कृत्स्नं प्रकाशयति भारत ॥ ३४ ॥
}} }} }}

As the one sun illumineth the whole earth, so the Lord of the Field illumineth the whole Field, O Bhârata. {{float right|{{larger|(34)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
क्षेत्रक्षेत्रज्ञयोरेवमन्तरं ज्ञानचक्षुषा ।{{parabr}}
भूतप्रकृतिमोक्षं च ये विदुर्यान्ति ते परम् ॥ ३५ ॥
}} }} }}

They who by the eyes of Wisdom perceive this difference between the Field and the Knower of the Field, and the liberation of beings from Matter<ref>Prakriti</ref> they go to the Supreme. {{float right|{{larger|(35)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}<noinclude>{{rule}}
{{smallrefs}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader|198|THE BHAGAVAD-GITA.|}}</noinclude>{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
इति श्रीमद्भगवद्गीता॰ क्षेत्रक्षेत्रज्ञविभागयोगो नाम त्रयोदशोऽध्यायः ।
}} }} }}

{{fine block|Thus in the glorious Upanishads of the Bhagavad-Gita, the science of the {{sc|Eternal}}, the scripture of Yoga, the dialogue between Shrî Krishna and Arjuna, the thirteenth discourse entitled:}}

{{c|THE YOGA OF THE DISTINCTION BETWEEN THE FIELD AND THE KNOWER OF THE FIELD.}}


{{rule|3em}}<noinclude></noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" /></noinclude>{{dhr}}
{{c|{{larger|FOURTEENTH DISCOURSE.}}}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
{{c|श्रीभगवानुवाच ।}}

परं भूयः प्रवक्ष्यामि ज्ञानानां ज्ञानमुत्तमम् ।

यज्ज्ञात्वा मुनयः सर्वे परां सिद्धिमितो गताः ॥ १ ॥
}} }} }}

{{c|The Blessed Lord said:}}

I will again proclaim that supreme Wisdom, of all wisdom the best, which having known, all the Sages<ref>Munis.</ref> have gone hence to the supreme Perfection. {{float right|{{larger|(1)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
इदं ज्ञानमुपाश्रित्य मम साधर्म्यमागताः ।

सर्गेऽपि नोपजायन्ते प्रलये न व्यथन्ति च ॥ २ ॥
}} }} }}

Having taken refuge in this Wisdom and being assimilated to My own nature, they are not re-born even in the emanation of a universe, nor are disquieted in the dissolution. {{float right|{{larger|(2)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
मम योनिर्महद्ब्रह्म तस्मिन् गर्भं दधाम्यहम् ।

सम्भवः सर्वभूतानां ततो भवति भारत ॥ ३ ॥
}} }} }}
{{nop}}<noinclude>{{rule}}
{{smallrefs}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader|200|THE BHAGAVAD-GITA.|}}</noinclude>My womb is the great {{sc|Eternal}}; in that I place the germ; thence cometh the birth of all beings, O Bhârata. {{float right|{{larger|(3)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
सर्वयोनिषु कौन्तेय मूर्तयः संभवन्ति याः ।

तासां ब्रह्म महद्योनिरहं बीजप्रदः पिता ॥ ४ ॥
}} }} }}

In whatsoever wombs mortals are produced, O Kaunteya, the great {{sc|Eternal}} is their womb, I their generating father. {{float right|{{larger|(4)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
सत्त्वं रजस्तम इति गुणाः प्रकृतिसंभवाः ।

निबध्नन्ति महाबाहो देहे देहिनमव्ययम् ॥ ५ ॥
}} }} }}

Harmony,<ref>More strictly Rhythm.</ref> Motion, Inertia, such are the qualities<ref>Gunas.</ref>, Matter<ref>Prakriti.</ref>-born; they bind fast in the body, O great-armed one, the indestructible dweller in the body. {{float right|{{larger|(5)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
तत्र सत्त्वं निर्मलत्वात्प्रकाशकमनामयम् ।

सुखसङ्गेन बध्नाति ज्ञानसङ्गेन चानघ ॥ ६ ॥
}} }} }}

Of these Harmony from its stainlessness,<noinclude>{{rule}}
{{smallrefs}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader||FOURTEENTH DISCOURSE.|201}}</noinclude>luminous and healthy, bindeth by the attachment to bliss and the attachment to wisdom, O sinless one. {{float right|{{larger|(6)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
रजो रागात्मकं विद्धि तृष्णासङ्गसमुद्भवम् ।

तन्निबध्नाति कौन्तेय कर्मसङ्गेन देहिनम् ॥ ७ ॥
}} }} }}

Motion, the passion nature, know thou, is the source of attachment and thirst for life, O Kaunteya, that bindeth the dweller in the body by the attachment to action. {{float right|{{larger|(7)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
तमस्त्वज्ञानजं विद्धि मोहनं सर्वदेहिनाम् ।

प्रमादालस्यनिद्राभिस्तन्निबध्नाति भारत ॥ ८ ॥
}} }} }}

But Inertia, know thou, born of unwisdom, is the deluder of all dwellers in the body; that bindeth by heedlessness, indolence and sloth, O {{SIC|Bharata|Bhârata}}. {{float right|{{larger|(8)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
सत्त्वं सुखे सञ्जयति रजः कर्मणि भारत ।

ज्ञानमावृत्य तु तमः प्रमादे सञ्जयत्युत ॥ ९ ॥
}} }} }}

Harmony attacheth to bliss, Motion to action<noinclude></noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader|202|THE BHAGAVAD-GITA.|}}</noinclude>O {{SIC|Bharata|Bhârata}}. Inertia, verily, having shrouded wisdom, attacheth on the contrary to heedlessness. {{float right|{{larger|(9)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
रजस्तमश्चाभिभूय सत्त्वं भवति भारत ।

रजः सत्त्वं तमश्चैव तमः सत्त्वं रजस्तथा ॥ १० ॥
}} }} }}

Now Harmony prevaileth, having overpowered Motion and Inertia, O Bhârata; now Motion, having overpowered Harmony and Inertia; and now Inertia, having overpowered Harmony and Motion. {{float right|{{larger|(10)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
सर्वद्वारेषु देहेऽस्मिन्प्रकाश उपजायते ।

ज्ञानं यदा तदा विद्याद्विवृद्धं सत्त्वमित्युत ॥ ११ ॥
}} }} }}

When the wisdom-light streameth forth from all the gates of the body, then it may be known that Harmony is increasing. {{float right|{{larger|(11)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
लोभः प्रवृत्तिरारंभः कर्मणामशमः स्पृहा ।

रजस्येतानि जायन्ते विवृद्धे भरतर्षभ ॥ १२ ॥
}} }} }}

Greed, outgoing energy, undertaking of actions,<noinclude></noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader||FOURTEENTH DISCOURSE.|203}}</noinclude>restlessness, desire—these are born of the increase of Motion, O best of the Bhâratas. {{float right|{{larger|(12)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
अप्रकाशोऽप्रवृत्तिश्च प्रमादो मोह एव च ।

तमस्येतानि जायन्ते विवृद्धे कुरुनन्दन ॥ १३ ॥
}} }} }}

Darkness, stagnation and heedlessness and also delusion—these are born of the increase of Inertia, O joy of the Kurus. {{float right|{{larger|(13)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
यदा सत्त्वे प्रवृद्धे तु प्रलयं याति देहभृत् ।

तदोत्तमविदां लोकानमलान्प्रतिपद्यते ॥ १४ ॥
}} }} }}

If Harmony verily prevaileth when the embodied goeth to dissolution, then he goeth forth to the spotless worlds of the great Sages. {{float right|{{larger|(14)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
रजसि प्रलयं गत्वा कर्मसङ्गिषु जायते ।

तथा प्रलीनस्तमसि मूढयोनिषु जायते ॥ १५ ॥
}} }} }}
 
Having gone to dissolution in Motion, he is born among those attached to action; if dissolved in Inertia, he is born in the wombs of the senseless. {{float right|{{larger|(15)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}<noinclude></noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader|204|THE BHAGAVAD-GITA.|}}</noinclude>{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
कर्मणः सुकृतस्याहुः सात्त्विकं निर्मलं फलम् ।

रजसस्तु फलं दुःखमज्ञानं तमसः फलम् ॥ १६ ॥
}} }} }}

It is said the fruit of a good action is harmonious and spotless; verily the fruit of Motion is pain, and the fruit of Inertia {{SIC|unwisdom|unwisdom.}} {{float right|{{larger|(16)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
सत्त्वात्सञ्जायते ज्ञानं रजसो लोभ एव च ।

प्रमादमोहौ तमसो भवतोऽज्ञानमेव च ॥ १७ ॥
}} }} }}

From Harmony wisdom is born, and also greed from Motion; heedlessness and delusion are of Inertia and also unwisdom. {{float right|{{larger|(17)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
ऊर्ध्वं गच्छन्ति सत्त्वस्था मध्ये तिष्ठन्ति राजसाः ।

जघन्यगुणवृत्तिस्था अधो गच्छन्ति तामसाः ॥ १८ ॥
}} }} }}

They rise upwards who are settled in Harmony; the Active dwell in the mid-most place: the Inert go downwards, enveloped in the {{SIC|vilest|vilest qualities.}} {{float right|{{larger|(18)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}<noinclude>{{red|proofread with input from https://archive.org/details/bhagavadgitawith00londiala/page/256/mode/2up}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader||FOURTEENTH DISCOURSE.|205}}</noinclude>{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
नान्यं गुणेभ्यः कर्तारं यदा द्रष्टाऽनुपश्यति ।

गुणेभ्यश्च परं वेत्ति मद्भावं सोऽधिगच्छति ॥ १९ ॥
}} }} }}

When the Seer perceiveth no agent other than the qualities<ref name="p205Gunas">Gunas.</ref>, and knoweth {{small-caps|That}} which is higher than the qualities,<ref name="p205Gunas" /> he entereth into My Nature. {{float right|{{larger|(19)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
गुणानेतानतीत्य त्रीन्देही देहसमुद्भवान् ।

जन्ममृत्युजरादुःखैर्विमुक्तोऽमृतमश्नुते ॥ २० ॥
}} }} }}

When the dweller in the body hath crossed over these three qualities,<ref name="p205Gunas" /> whence all bodies have been produced, liberated from birth, death, old age and sorrow, he drinketh the nectar of immortality<ref>The Amrita.</ref>. {{float right|{{larger|(20)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
{{c|अर्जुन उवाच ।}}

कैर्लिङ्गैस्त्रीन्गुणानेतानतीतो भवति प्रभो ।

किमाचारः कथं चैतांस्त्रीन्गुणानतिवर्तते ॥ २१ ॥
}} }} }}
{{nop}}<noinclude>{{rule}}
{{smallrefs}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader|206|THE BHAGAVAD-GITA.|}}</noinclude>{{c|Arjuna said:}}

What are the marks of him who hath crossed over the three qualities<ref name="p205Gunas" />, O Lord? How acteth he, and how doth he go beyond these three qualities<ref name="p205Gunas" />? {{float right|{{larger|(21)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
{{c|श्रीभगवानुवाच ।}}

प्रकाशं च प्रवृत्तिं च मोहमेव च पाण्डव ।

न द्वेष्टि संप्रवृत्तानि न निवृत्तानि काङ्क्षति ॥ २२ ॥
}} }} }}
 
{{c|The Blessed Lord said:}}

He, O Pândava, who hateth not radiance, nor outgoing energy, nor even delusion, when present, nor longeth after them, absent; {{float right|{{larger|(22)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
उदासीनवदासीनो गुणैर्यो न विचाल्यते ।

गुणा वर्तन्त इत्येव योऽवतिष्ठति नेङ्गते ॥ २३ ॥
}} }} }}

He who, seated as a neutral, is unshaken by the qualities<ref name="p205Gunas" />; who, saying, "The qualities<ref name="p205Gunas" /> revolve," standeth apart immovable. {{float right|{{larger|(23)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}<noinclude>{{rule}}
{{smallrefs|refx=<ref name="p205Gunas">Gunas.</ref>}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader||FOURTEENTH DISCOURSE.|207}}</noinclude>{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
समदुःखसुखः स्वस्थः समलोष्टाश्मकाञ्चनः ।

तुल्यप्रियाप्रियो धीरस्तुल्यनिन्दात्मसंस्तुतिः ॥ २४ ॥
}} }} }}

Balanced in pleasure and pain, self-reliant, to whom a lump of earth, a rock and gold are alike, the same to loved and unloved, firm, the same in censure and in praise, {{float right|{{larger|(24)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
मानापमानयोस्तुल्यस्तुल्यो मित्रारिपक्षयोः ।

सर्वारंभपरित्यागी गुणातीतः स उच्यते ॥ २५ ॥
}} }} }}

The same in honour and ignominy, the same to friend and foe, abandoning all undertakings—he is said to have crossed over the qualities.<ref name="p205Gunas" /> {{float right|{{larger|(25)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
मां च योऽव्यभिचारेण भक्तियोगेन सेवते ।

स गुणान्समतीत्यैतान् ब्रह्मभूयाय कल्पते ॥ २६ ॥
}} }} }}

And he who serveth Me exclusively by the Yoga of devotion, he, crossing beyond the qualities,<ref name="p205Gunas" /> he is fit to become the {{small-caps|Eternal}}. {{float right|{{larger|(26)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}<noinclude>{{rule}}
{{smallrefs|refx=<ref name="p205Gunas">Gunas.</ref>}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader|208|THE BHAGAVAD-GITA.|}}</noinclude>{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
ब्रह्मणो हि प्रतिष्ठाऽहममृतस्याव्ययस्य च ।

शाश्वतस्य च धर्मस्य सुखस्यैकान्तिकस्य च ॥ २७ ॥
}} }} }}

For I am the abode of the {{small-caps|Eternal}}, and of the indestructible nectar of immortality, of immemorial righteousness,<ref>Dharma.</ref> and of unending bliss. {{float right|{{larger|(27)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
इति श्रीमद्भगवद्गीता॰ गुणत्रयविभागयोगो नाम चतुर्दशोऽध्यायः ।
}} }} }}

{{fine block|Thus in the glorious Upanishads of the {{sc|Bhagavad-Gita}}, the science of the {{sc|Eternal}}, the scripture of Yoga, the dialogue between Shri Krishna and Arjuna, the fourteenth discourse entitled:}}

{{c|THE YOGA OF SEPARATION FROM THE THREE QUALITIES.}}

{{custom rule|sp|40|d|10|sp|40}}<noinclude>{{rule}}
{{smallrefs}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" /></noinclude>{{dhr}}
{{c|{{larger|FIFTEENTH DISCOURSE.}}}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
{{c|श्रीभगवानुवाच ।}}

ऊर्ध्वमूलमधःशाखमश्वत्थं प्राहुरव्ययम् ।

छन्दांसि यस्य पर्णानि यस्तं वेद स वेदवित् ॥ १ ॥
}} }} }}

{{c|The Blessed Lord said:}}

With roots above, branches below, the [[w:Ashvattha|Asvattha]] is said to be indestructible; the leaves of it are hymns; he who knoweth it is a Veda-knower. {{float right|{{larger|(1)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
अधश्चोर्ध्वं प्रसृतास्तस्य शाखाः गुणप्रवृद्धा विषयप्रवालाः ।

अधश्च मूलान्यनुसन्ततानि कर्मानुबन्धीनि मनुष्यलोके ॥ २ ॥
}} }} }}

Downwards and upwards spread the branches of it, nourished by the qualities<ref>Gunas.</ref>; the objects of the senses its buds; and its roots grow<noinclude>{{rule}}
{{smallrefs}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader|210|THE BHAGAVAD-GITA.|}}</noinclude>downwards, the bonds of action in the world of men. {{float right|{{larger|(2)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
न रूपमस्येह तथोपलभ्यते नान्तो न चादिर्न च संप्रतिष्ठा ।

अश्वत्थमेनं सुविरूढमूलमसङ्गशस्त्रेण दृढेन छित्त्वा ॥ ३ ॥
}} }} }}

Nor here may be acquired knowledge of its form, nor its end, nor its origin, nor its rooting-place; this strongly rooted Asvattha having been cut down by the unswerving weapon of non-attachment, {{float right|{{larger|(3)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
ततः पदं तत्परिमार्गितव्यम्

यस्मिन्गता न निवर्तन्ति भूयः ।

तमेव चाद्यं पुरुषं प्रपद्ये

यतः प्रवृत्तिः प्रसृता पुराणी ॥ ४ ॥
}} }} }}

That path beyond may be sought, treading which there is no return. I go indeed to that<noinclude></noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader||FIFTEENTH DISCOURSE.|211}}</noinclude>Primal Man<ref>Purusha.</ref>, whence the ancient energy forth-streamed. {{float right|{{larger|(4)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
निर्मानमोहा जितसङ्गदोषाः

अध्यात्मनित्या विनिवृत्तकामाः ।

द्वन्द्वैर्विमुक्ताः सुखदुःखसंज्ञै-

र्गच्छन्त्यमूढाः पदमव्ययं तत् ॥ ५ ॥
}} }} }}

Without pride and delusion, victorious over the vice of attachment, dwelling constantly in the {{sc|Self}}, desire pacified, liberated from the pairs of opposites known as pleasure and pain, they tread, undeluded, that indestructible path. {{float right|{{larger|(5)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
न तद्भासयते सूर्यो न शशाङ्को न पावकः ।

यद्गत्वा न निवर्तन्ते तद्धाम परमं मम ॥ ६ ॥
}} }} }}

Nor doth the sun lighten there, nor moon, nor fire; having gone thither they return not; that is My supreme abode. {{float right|{{larger|(6)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}<noinclude>{{rule}}
{{smallrefs}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader|212|THE BHAGAVAD-GITA.|}}</noinclude>{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
ममैवांशो जीवलोके जीवभूतः सनातनः ।

मनःषष्ठानीन्द्रियाणि प्रकृतिस्थानि कर्षति ॥ ७ ॥
}} }} }}

A portion of Mine own Self, transformed in the world of life into an immortal Spirit,<ref>Jîva, a life, individualised from the Universal Spirit.</ref> draweth round itself the senses of which the mind<ref name="p212Manah">Manah.</ref> is the sixth, veiled in matter<ref>Prakriti.</ref>. {{float right|{{larger|(7)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
शरीरं यदवाप्नोति यच्चाप्युत्क्रामतीश्वरः ।

गृहित्वैतानि संयाति वायुर्गन्धानिवाशयात् ॥ ८ ॥
}} }} }}

When the Lord acquireth a body and when He abandoneth it, He seizeth these<ref>The senses and the mind.</ref> and goeth with them, as the wind takes fragrances from their {{SIC|retreats|retreats.}} {{float right|{{larger|(8)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
श्रोत्रं चक्षुः स्पर्शनं च रसनं घ्राणमेव च ।

अधिष्ठाय मनश्चायं विषयानुपसेवते ॥ ९ ॥
}} }} }}

Enshrined in the ear, the eye, the touch, the taste and the smell, and in the mind<ref name="p212Manah" /> also, He enjoyeth the objects of the {{SIC|senses|senses.}} {{float right|{{larger|(9)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}<noinclude>{{rule}}
{{smallrefs}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader||FIFTEENTH DISCOURSE.|213}}</noinclude>{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
उत्क्रामन्तं स्थितं वापि भुञ्जानं वा गुणान्वितम् ।

विमूढा नानुपश्यन्ति पश्यन्ति ज्ञानचक्षुषः ॥ १० ॥
}} }} }}

The deluded do not perceive (Him) when He departeth or stayeth or enjoyeth, swayed by the qualities<ref>Gunas.</ref>; the wisdom-eyed perceive. {{float right|{{larger|(10)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
यतन्तो योगिनश्चैनं पश्यन्त्यात्मन्यवस्थितम् ।

यतन्तोऽप्यकृतात्मानो नैनं पश्यन्त्यचेतसः ॥ ११ ॥
}} }} }}

Yogîs also, struggling, perceive Him, established in the {{sc|Self}}; but though struggling, the unintelligent perceive Him not, their selves untrained. {{float right|{{larger|(11)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
यदादित्यगतं तेजो जगद्भासयतेऽखिलम् ।

यच्चन्द्रमसि यच्चाग्नौ तत्तेजो विद्धि मामकम् ॥ १२ ॥
}} }} }}

That splendour issuing from the sun that enlighteneth the whole world, that which is in the moon and in fire, that splendour know as from Me. {{float right|{{larger|(12)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}<noinclude>{{rule}}
{{smallrefs}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader|214|THE BHAGAVAD-GITA.|}}</noinclude>{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
गामाविश्य च भूतानि धारयाम्यहमोजसा ।

पुष्णामि चौषधीः सर्वाः सोमो भूत्वा रसात्मकः ॥ १३ ॥
}} }} }}

Permeating the soil, I support beings by my vital energy, and having become the delicious Soma<ref>"Having become the watery moon" is the accepted translation. Soma is a liquid, drawn from the Soma-plant. "Having become sap" is a probable translation.</ref> I nourish all plants. {{float right|{{larger|(13)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
अहं वैश्वानरो भूत्वा प्राणिनां देहमाश्रितः ।

प्राणापानसमायुक्तः पचाम्यन्नं चतुर्विधम् ॥ १४ ॥
}} }} }}

I, having become the Fire of Life<ref>Vaisvânara.</ref>, take possession of the bodies of breathing things, and united with the life-breaths<ref>Prâna and Apâna.</ref>, I digest the four kinds of food. {{float right|{{larger|(14)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
सर्वस्य चाहं हृदि सन्निविष्टो मत्तः स्मृतिर्ज्ञानमपोहनं च ।

वेदैश्च सर्वैरहमेव वेद्यो वेदान्तकृद्वेदविदेव चाहम् ॥ १५ ॥
}} }} }}
{{nop}}<noinclude>{{rule}}
{{smallrefs}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader||FIFTEENTH DISCOURSE.|215}}</noinclude>And I am seated in the hearts of all, and from Me memory and wisdom and their absence. And that which is to be known in all the Vedas am I; and I indeed the Veda-knower and the author of the Vedanta. {{float right|{{larger|(15)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
द्वाविमौ पुरुषौ लोके क्षरश्चाक्षर एव च ।

क्षरः सर्वाणि भूतानि कूटस्थोऽक्षर उच्यते ॥ १६ ॥
}} }} }}

There are two Energies<ref name="p215Purusha">Purusha.</ref> in this world, the destructible and the indestructible; the destructible is all beings, the unchanging is called the indestructible. {{float right|{{larger|(16)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
उत्तमः पुरुषस्त्वन्यः परमात्मेत्युदाहृतः ।

यो लोकत्रयमाविश्य बिभर्त्यव्यय ईश्वरः ॥ १७ ॥
}} }} }}

The highest Energy<ref name="p215Purusha" /> is verily Another, declared as the Supreme {{sc|Self}}, He who, pervading all, sustaineth the three worlds, the indestructible Lord. {{float right|{{larger|(17)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}<noinclude>{{rule}}
{{smallrefs}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader|216|THE BHAGAVAD-GITA.|}}</noinclude>{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
यस्मात्क्षरमतीतोऽहमक्षरादपि चोत्तमः ।

अतोऽस्मि लोके वेदे च प्रथितः पुरुषोत्तमः ॥ १८ ॥
}} }} }}

Since I excel the destructible, and am more excellent also than the indestructible, in the world and in the Veda I am proclaimed the Supreme Spirit.<ref name="p216Purushottama">Purushottama, the highest Purusha.</ref> {{float right|{{larger|(18)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
यो मामेवमसंमूढो जानाति पुरुषोत्तमम् ।

स सर्वविद्भजति मां सर्वभावेन भारत ॥ १९ ॥
}} }} }}

He who undeluded knoweth Me thus as the Supreme Spirit<ref name="p216Purushottama" />, he, all-knowing, worshippeth Me with his whole being, O Bhârata. {{float right|{{larger|(19)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
इति गुह्यतमं शास्त्रमिदमुक्तं मयाऽनघ ।

एतद्‌बुध्वा बुद्धिमान् स्यात्कृतकृत्यश्च भारत ॥ २० ॥
}} }} }}


Thus by Me this most secret teaching hath been told O sinless one. This known, he hath become illuminated and hath finished his work, O Bhârata. {{float right|{{larger|(20)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}<noinclude>{{rule}}
{{smallrefs}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader||FIFTEENTH DISCOURSE.|217}}</noinclude>{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
इति श्रीमद्भगवद्गीता॰ पुरुषोत्तमयोगो नाम पञ्चदशोऽध्यायः ।
}} }} }}

{{fine block|Thus in the glorious Upanishads of the {{sc|Bhagavad-Gita}}, the science of the {{sc|Eternal}}, the scripture of Yoga, the dialogue between Shrî Krishna and Arjuna, the fifteenth discourse, entitled:}}

{{c|THE YOGA OF ATTAINING THE SUPREME SPIRIT.}}


{{rule|3em}}<noinclude></noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" /></noinclude>{{dhr}}
{{center|{{larger|SIXTEENTH DISCOURSE.}}}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
{{c|श्रीभगवानुवाच ।}}

अभयं सत्त्वसंशुद्धिर्ज्ञानयोगव्यवस्थितिः ।

दानं दमश्च यज्ञश्च स्वाध्यायस्तप आर्जवम् ॥ १ ॥
}} }} }}

{{c|The Blessed Lord said:}}

Fearlessness, cleanness of life, steadfastness in the Yoga of wisdom, almsgiving, self-restraint and sacrifice and study of the Scriptures, austerity and straightforwardness, {{float right|{{larger|(1)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
अहिंसा सत्यमक्रोधस्त्यागः शान्तिरपैशुनम् ।

दया भूतेष्वलोलुप्त्वं मार्दवं ह्रीरचापलम् ॥ २ ॥
}} }} }}

Harmlessness, truth, absence of wrath, renunciation, peacefulness, absence of crookedness, compassion to living beings, uncovetousness, mildness, modesty, absence of fickleness, {{float right|{{larger|(2)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
तेजः क्षमा धृतिः शौचमद्रोहो नातिमानिता ।

भवन्ति सम्पदं दैवीमभिजातस्य भारत ॥ ३ ॥
}} }} }}
{{nop}}<noinclude></noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader||SIXTEENTH DISCOURSE.|219}}</noinclude>Vigour, forgiveness, fortitude, purity, absence of envy and pride—these are his who is born with the divine properties, O Bhârata. {{float right|{{larger|(3)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
दम्भो दर्पोऽभिमानश्च क्रोधः पारुष्यमेव च ।

अज्ञानं चाभिजातस्य पार्थ सम्पदमासुरीम् ॥ ४ ॥
}} }} }}

Hypocrisy, arrogance and conceit, wrath and also harshness and unwisdom are his who is born, O Pârtha, with demoniacal<ref>Asuric; the Asuras were the enemies of the Suras or Gods.</ref> properties. {{float right|{{larger|(4)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
दैवी सम्पद्विमोक्षाय निबन्धायासुरी मता ।

मा शुचः सम्पदं दैवीमभिजातोऽसि पाण्डव ॥ ५ ॥
}} }} }}

The divine properties are deemed to be for liberation, the demoniacal for bondage. Grieve not, thou art born with divine properties, O Pândava. {{float right|{{larger|(5)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
द्वौ भूतसर्गौ लोकेऽस्मिन्दैव आसुर एव च ।

दैवो विस्तरशः प्रोक्त आसुरं पार्थ मे शृणु ॥ ६ ॥
}} }} }}
{{nop}}<noinclude>{{rule}}
{{smallrefs}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader|220|THE BHAGAVAD-GITA.|}}</noinclude>Twofold is the animal creation in this world, the divine and the demoniacal: the divine hath been described at length: hear from Me, O Pârtha, the demoniacal. {{float right|{{larger|(6)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
प्रवृत्तिं च निवृत्तिं च जना न विदुरासुराः ।

न शौचं नापि चाचारो न सत्यं तेषु विद्यते ॥ ७ ॥
}} }} }}
 
Demoniacal men know neither right energy nor right abstinence; nor purity, nor even propriety, nor truth is in them. {{float right|{{larger|(7)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
असत्यमप्रतिष्ठं ते जगदाहुरनीश्वरम् ।

अपरस्परसंभूतं किमन्यत्कामहैतुकम् ॥ ८ ॥
}} }} }}
 
"The universe is without truth, without basis," they say, "without a God<ref>Isvara; the ruler of a universe.</ref>; brought about by mutual union, and caused by lust and nothing else." {{float right|{{larger|(8)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
एतव दृष्टिमवष्टभ्य नष्टात्मानोऽल्पबुद्धयः ।

प्रभवन्त्युग्रकर्माणः क्षयाय जगतोऽहिताः ॥ ९ ॥
}} }} }}
{{nop}}<noinclude>{{rule}}
{{smallrefs}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader||SIXTEENTH DISCOURSE.|221}}</noinclude>Holding this view, these ruined selves of small understanding<ref>Buddhi.</ref>, of fierce deeds, come forth as enemies for the destruction of the world. {{float right|{{larger|(9)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
काममाश्रित्य दुष्पूरं दम्भमानमदान्विताः ।

मोहाद्‌गृहीत्वाऽसद्ग्राहान्प्रवर्तन्तेऽशुचिव्रताः ॥ १० ॥
}} }} }}

Surrendering themselves to insatiable desires, possessed with vanity, conceit and arrogance, holding evil ideas through delusion, they engage in action with impure resolves. {{float right|{{larger|(10)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
चिन्तामपरिमेयां च प्रलयान्तामुपाश्रिताः ।

कामोपभोगपरमा एतावदिति निश्चिताः ॥ ११ ॥
}} }} }}

Giving themselves over to unmeasured thought whose end is death, regarding the gratification of desires as the highest, feeling sure that this is all, {{float right|{{larger|(11)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}<noinclude>{{rule}}
{{smallrefs}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader|222|THE BHAGAVAD-GITA.|}}</noinclude>{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
आशापाशशतैर्बद्धाः कामक्रोधपरायणाः ।

ईहन्ते कामभोगार्थमन्यायेनार्थसञ्चयान् ॥ १२ ॥
}} }} }}

Held in bondage by a hundred ties of expectation, given over to lust and anger, they strive to obtain by unlawful means hoards of wealth for sensual enjoyments. {{float right|{{larger|(12)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
इदमद्य मया लब्धमिमं प्राप्स्ये मनोरथम् ।

इदमस्तीदमपि मे भविष्यति पुनर्धनम् ॥ १३ ॥
}} }} }}

"This to-day by me hath been won, that purpose I shall gain; this wealth is mine already, and also this shall be mine in future. {{float right|{{larger|(13)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
असौ मया हतः शत्रुर्हनिष्ये चापरानपि ।

ईश्वरोऽहमहं भोगी सिद्धोऽहं बलवान्सुखी ॥ १४ ॥
}} }} }}

"I have slain this enemy, and others also I shall slay. I am the Lord, I am the enjoyer, I am perfect, powerful, happy; {{float right|{{larger|(14)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
आढ्योऽभिजनवानस्मि कोऽन्योऽस्ति सदृशो मया ।

यक्ष्ये दास्यामि मोदिष्य इत्यज्ञानविमोहिताः ॥ १५ ॥
}} }} }}
{{nop}}<noinclude></noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader||SIXTEENTH DISCOURSE.|223}}</noinclude>"I am wealthy, well-born; what other is there that is like unto me? I will sacrifice, I will give alms, I will rejoice." Thus deluded by unwisdom, {{float right|{{larger|(15)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
अनेकचित्तविभ्रान्ता मोहजालसमावृताः ।

प्रसक्ताः कामभोगेषु पतन्ति नरकेऽशुचौ ॥ १६ ॥
}} }} }}

Bewildered by numerous thoughts, enmeshed in the web of delusion, addicted to the gratification of desire, they fall downwards into a foul hell. {{float right|{{larger|(16)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
आत्मसंभाविताः स्तब्धा धनमानमदान्विताः ।

यजन्ते नामयज्ञैस्ते दम्भेनाविधिपूर्वकम् ॥ १७ ॥
}} }} }}

Self-glorifying, stubborn, filled with the pride and intoxication of wealth, they perform lip-sacrifices for ostentation, contrary to scriptural ordinance. {{float right|{{larger|(17)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
अहङ्कारं बलं दर्पं कामं क्रोधं च संश्रिताः ।

मामात्मपरदेहेषु प्रद्विषन्तोऽभ्यसूयकाः ॥ १८ ॥
}} }} }}
{{nop}}<noinclude></noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader|224|THE BHAGAVAD-GITA.|}}</noinclude>Given over to egoism, power, insolence, lust and wrath, these malicious ones hate Me in the bodies of others and in their own. {{float right|{{larger|(18)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
तानहं द्विषतः क्रूरान्संसारेषु नराधमान् ।

क्षिपाम्यजस्रमशुभानासुरीष्वेव योनिषु ॥ १९ ॥
}} }} }}

These haters, evil, pitiless, vilest among men in the world, I ever throw down into demoniacal wombs. {{float right|{{larger|(19)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
आसुरीं योनिमापन्ना मूढा जन्मनि जन्मनि ।

मामप्राप्यैव कौन्तेय ततो यान्त्यधमां गतिम् ॥ २० ॥
}} }} }}

Cast into demoniacal wombs, deluded birth after birth, attaining not to Me, O Kaunteya, they sink into the lowest depths. {{float right|{{larger|(20)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
त्रिविधं नरकस्येदं द्वारं नाशनमात्मनः ।

कामः क्रोधस्तथा लोभस्तस्मादेतत्त्रयं त्यजेत् ॥ २१ ॥
}} }} }}
 
Triple is the gate of this hell, destructive of the self—lust, wrath, and greed; therefore let man renounce these three. {{float right|{{larger|(21)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}<noinclude></noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader||SIXTEENTH DISCOURSE.|225}}</noinclude>{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
एतैर्विमुक्तः कौन्तेय तमोद्वारैस्त्रिभिर्नरः ।

आचरत्यात्मनः श्रेयस्ततो याति परां गतिम् ॥ २२ ॥
}} }} }}

A man liberated from these three gates of darkness, O son of Kunti, accomplisheth his own welfare, and thus reacheth the highest goal. {{float right|{{larger|(22)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
यः शास्त्रविधिमुत्सृज्य वर्तते कामकारतः ।

न स सिद्धिमवाप्नोति न सुखं न परां गतिम् ॥ २३ ॥
}} }} }}
 
He who, having cast aside the ordinances of the Scriptures, followeth the promptings of desire, attaineth not to perfection, nor happiness, nor the highest goal. {{float right|{{larger|(23)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
तस्माच्छास्त्रं प्रमाणं ते कार्याकार्यव्यवस्थितौ ।

ज्ञात्वा शास्त्रविधानोक्तं कर्म कर्तुमिहार्हसि ॥ २४ ॥
}} }} }}

Therefore let the Scriptures be thy authority, in determining what ought to be done, or what ought not to be done. Knowing what hath been<noinclude></noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader|226|THE BHAGAVAD-GITA.|}}</noinclude>declared by the ordinances of the Scriptures, thou oughtest to work in this world. {{float right|{{larger|(24)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
इति श्रीमद्भगवद्गीता॰ दैवासुरसम्पद्विभागयोगो नाम षोडशोऽध्यायः ।
}} }} }}

{{fine block|Thus in the glorious Upanishads of the {{small-caps|Bhagavad-Gita}}, the science of the {{small-caps|Eternal}}, the scripture of Yoga, the dialogue between Shri Krishna and Arjuna, the sixteenth discourse, entitled:}}

{{c|THE YOGA OF DIVISION BETWEEN THE DIVINE AND THE DEMONIACAL.}}


{{nop}}<noinclude>{{rule|3em}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" /></noinclude>{{dhr}}
{{c|{{larger|SEVENTEENTH DISCOURSE.}}}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
{{c|अर्जुन उवाच ।}}

ये शास्त्रविधिमुत्सृज्य यजन्ते श्रद्धयाऽन्विताः ।

तेषां निष्ठा तु का कृष्ण सत्त्वमाहो रजस्तमः ॥ १ ॥
}} }} }}

{{c|Arjuna said:}}

Those that sacrifice full of faith,<ref>Shraddhâ.</ref> but casting aside the ordinances of the Scriptures, what is verily their condition, O Krishna? Is it one of Purity, Passion, or Darkness<ref>The three qualities, Sattva, Rajah, Tamah, are here used in their moral correspondences, and are therefore translated as Purity, Passion, and Darkness</ref>? {{float right|{{larger|(1)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
{{c|श्रीभगवानुवाच ।}}

त्रिविधा भवति श्रद्धा देहिनां सा स्वभावजा ।

सात्त्विकी राजसी चैव तामसी चेति तां शृणु ॥ २ ॥
}} }} }}

{{c|The Blessed Lord said:}}

Threefold is by nature the inborn faith of the<noinclude>{{rule}}
{{smallrefs}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader|228|THE BHAGAVAD-GITA.|}}</noinclude>embodied—pure, passionate, and dark. Hear thou of these. {{float right|{{larger|(2)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
सत्त्वानुरूपा सर्वस्य श्रद्धा भवति भारत ।

श्रद्धामयोऽयं पुरुषो यो यच्छ्रद्धः स एव सः ॥ ३ ॥
}} }} }}

The faith of each is shaped to his own nature, O Bhârata. The man consists of his faith<ref>That is, the man's faith shows what is the man's character.</ref>; that which his faith is, he is even that. {{float right|{{larger|(3)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
यजन्ते सात्त्विका देवान्यक्षरक्षांसि राजसाः ।

प्रेतान्भूतगणांश्चान्ये यजन्ते तामसा जनाः ॥ ४ ॥
}} }} }}

Pure men worship the Gods; the passionate the gnomes and giants<ref>Yakshas, gnomes, are the servants of the Lord of Wealth, ''i. e.'', are connected with metals; Râkshasas, giants, or Titans, are the gigantic inhabitants of Atlantis versed in magic and sorcery.</ref>; the others, the dark folk, worship ghosts and troops of nature-spirits<ref>Pretas, ghosts, are departed men; while Bhûtas, nature-spirits, are of a somewhat goblin-like type.</ref>. {{float right|{{larger|(4)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}<noinclude>{{rule}}
{{smallrefs}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader||SEVENTEENTH DISCOURSE.|229}}</noinclude>{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
अशास्त्रविहितं घोरं तप्यन्ते ये तपो जनाः ।

दम्भाहङ्कारसंयुक्ताः कामरागबलान्विताः ॥ ५ ॥
}} }} }}

The men who perform severe austerities, unenjoined by the Scriptures, wedded to vanity and egoism, impelled by the force of their desires and passions, {{float right|{{larger|(5)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
कर्शयन्तः शरीरस्थं भूतग्राममचेतसः ।

मां चैवान्तःशरीरस्थं तान्विद्ध्यासुरनिश्चयान् ॥ ६ ॥
}} }} }}
  
Unintelligent, tormenting the aggregated elements forming the body, and Me also, seated in the inner body, know these demoniacal in their resolves. {{float right|{{larger|(6)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
आहारस्त्वपि सर्वस्य त्रिविधो भवति प्रियः ।

यज्ञस्तपस्तथा दानं तेषां भेदमिमं शृणु ॥ ७ ॥
}} }} }}

The food also which is dear to each is threefold, as also sacrifice, austerity and almsgiving. Hear thou the distinction of these. {{float right|{{larger|(7)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}<noinclude></noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader|230|THE BHAGAVAD-GITA.|}}</noinclude>{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
आयुःसत्त्वबलारोग्यसुखप्रीतिविवर्धनाः ।

रस्याः स्निग्धाः स्थिरा हृद्या आहाराः सात्त्विकप्रियाः ॥ ८ ॥
}} }} }}

The foods that augment vitality, energy, vigour, health, joy and cheerfulness, delicious, bland, substantial and agreeable, are dear to the pure. {{float right|{{larger|(8)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
कट्‌वम्ललवणात्युष्णतीक्ष्णरूक्षविदाहिनः ।

आहारा राजसस्येष्टा दुःखशोकामयप्रदाः ॥ ९ ॥
}} }} }}

The passionate desire foods that are bitter, sour, saline, over-hot, pungent, dry and burning and which produce pain, grief and sickness. {{float right|{{larger|(9)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
यातयामं गतरसं पूति पर्युषितं च यत् ।

उच्छिष्टमपि चामेध्यं भोजनं तामसप्रियम् ॥ १० ॥
}} }} }}

That which is stale and flat, putrid and corrupt, leavings also and unclean, is the food dear to the dark. {{float right|{{larger|(10)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
अफलाकाङ्क्षिभिर्यज्ञो विधिदृष्टोय इज्यते ।

यष्टव्यमेवेति मनः समाधाय स सात्त्विकः ॥ ११ ॥
}} }} }}
{{nop}}<noinclude></noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader||SEVENTEENTH DISCOURSE.|231}}</noinclude>The sacrifice which is offered by men without desire for fruit, as enjoined by the ordinances, under the firm belief that sacrifice is a duty, that is pure. {{float right|{{larger|(11)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
अभिसन्धाय तु फलं दम्भार्थमपि चैव यत् ।

इज्यते भरतश्रेष्ठ तं यज्ञं विद्धि राजसम् ॥ १२ ॥
}} }} }}

The sacrifice offered with a view verily to fruit, and also indeed for self-glorification, O best of the Bhâratas; know thou that to be of passion. {{float right|{{larger|(12)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
विधिहीनमसृष्टान्नं मन्त्रहीनमदक्षिणम् ।

श्रद्धाविरहितं यज्ञं तामसं परिचक्षते ॥ १३ ॥
}} }} }}

The sacrifice contrary to the ordinances, without distributing food, devoid of words of power<ref>Mantras.</ref> and without gifts<ref>To the officiating priests.</ref>, empty of faith, is said to be of darkness. {{float right|{{larger|(13)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
देवद्विजगुरुप्राज्ञपूजनं शौचमार्जवम् ।

ब्रह्मचर्यमहिंसा च शारीरं तप उच्यते ॥ १४ ॥
}} }} }}
{{nop}}<noinclude>{{rule}}
{{smallrefs}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader|232|THE BHAGAVAD-GITA.|}}</noinclude>Worship given to the Gods, to the twice-born, to the teachers<ref>Gurus.</ref> and to the wise, purity, straightforwardness, continence and harmlessness, are called the austerity of the body. {{float right|{{larger|(14)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
अनुद्वेगकरं वाक्यं सत्यं प्रियहितं च यत् ।

स्वाध्यायाभ्यसनं चैव वाङ्मयं तप उच्यते ॥ १५ ॥
}} }} }}

Speech causing no annoyance, truthful, pleasant and beneficial, the practice of the study of the Scriptures, are called the austerity of speech. {{float right|{{larger|(15)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
मनःप्रसादः सौम्यत्वं मौनमात्मविनिग्रहः ।

भावसंशुद्धिरित्येतत्तपो मानसमुच्यते ॥ १६ ॥
}} }} }}

Mental happiness, equilibrium, silence, self-control, purity of nature—these are called the austerity of the mind<ref>Manah.</ref>. {{float right|{{larger|(16)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
श्रद्धया परया तप्तं तपस्तत्त्रिविधं नरैः ।

अफलाकाङ्क्षिभिर्युक्तैः सात्त्विकं परिचक्षते ॥ १७ ॥
}} }} }}
{{nop}}<noinclude>{{rule}}
{{smallrefs}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader||SEVENTEENTH DISCOURSE.|233}}</noinclude>This threefold austerity, performed by men with the utmost faith, without desire for fruit, harmonised, is said to be pure. {{float right|{{larger|(17)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
सत्कारमानपूजार्थं तपो दम्भेन चैव यत् ।

क्रियते तदिह प्रोक्तं राजसं चलमध्रुवम् ॥ १८ ॥
}} }} }}

The austerity which is practised with the object of gaining respect, honour and worship, and for ostentation, is said to be of passion, unstable and fleeting. {{float right|{{larger|(18)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
मूढग्राहेणात्मनो यत्पीडया क्रियते तपः ।

परस्योत्सादनार्थं वा तत्तामसमुदाहृतम् ॥ १९ ॥
}} }} }}

That austerity done under a deluded understanding, with self-torture, or with the object of destroying another, that is declared of darkness. {{float right|{{larger|(20)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
दातव्यमिति यद्दानं दीयतेऽनुपकारिणे ।

देशे काले च पात्रे च तद्दानं सात्त्विकं स्मृतम् ॥ २० ॥
}} }} }}
{{nop}}<noinclude></noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader|234|THE BHAGAVAD-GITA.|}}</noinclude>That alms given to one who does nothing in return, believing that a gift ought to be made in a fit place and time to a worthy person, that alms is accounted pure. {{float right|{{larger|(20)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
यत्तु प्रत्युपकारार्थं फलमुद्दिश्य वा पुनः ।

दीयते च परिक्लिष्टं तद्दानं राजसं स्मृतम् ॥ २१ ॥
}} }} }}

That given with a view to receiving in return, or looking for fruit again, or grudgingly, that alms is accounted of passion. {{float right|{{larger|(21)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
अदेशकाले यद्दानमपात्रेभ्यश्च दीयते ।

असत्कृतमवज्ञातं तत्तामसमुदाहृतम् ॥ २२ ॥
}} }} }}

That alms given at unfit place and time, and to unworthy persons, disrespectfully and contemptuously, that is declared of darkness. {{float right|{{larger|(22)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
ओं तत्सदिति निर्देशो ब्रह्मणस्त्रिविधः स्मृतः ।

ब्राह्मणास्तेन वेदाश्च यज्ञाश्च विहिताः पुरा ॥ २३ ॥
}} }} }}

"{{sc|Aum Tat Sat}}," this has been considered to be the threefold designation of the {{sc|Eternal}}. By<noinclude></noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader||SEVENTEENTH DISCOURSE.|235}}</noinclude>that were ordained of old Brâhmanas, Vedas and sacrifices. {{float right|{{larger|(23)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
तस्मादोमित्युदाहृत्य यज्ञदानतपःक्रियाः ।

प्रवर्तन्ते विधानोक्ताः सततं ब्रह्मवादिनाम् ॥ २४ ॥
}} }} }}

Therefore with the pronunciation of "{{sc|Aum}}" the acts of sacrifice, gift and austerity as laid down in the ordinances are always commenced by the knowers of the {{sc|Eternal}}. {{float right|{{larger|(24)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
तदित्यनभिसन्धाय फलं यज्ञतपःक्रियाः ।

दानक्रियाश्च विविधाः क्रियन्ते मोक्षकाङ्क्षिभिः ॥ २५ ॥
}} }} }}

With the pronunciation of "{{sc|Tat}}" and without aiming at fruit are performed the various acts of sacrifice, austerity and gift, by those desiring liberation. {{float right|{{larger|(25)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
सद्भावे साधुभावे च सदित्येतत्प्रयुज्यते ।

प्रशस्ते कर्मणि तथा सच्छब्दः पार्थ युज्यते ॥ २६ ॥
}} }} }}

"{{sc|Sat}}" is used in the sense of reality and<noinclude></noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader|236|THE BHAGAVAD-GITA.|}}</noinclude>goodness; likewise, O Pârtha, the word "{{sc|Sat}}" is used in the sense of a good work. {{float right|{{larger|(26)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
यज्ञे तपसि दाने च स्थितिः सदिति चोच्यते ।

कर्म चैव तदर्थीयं सदित्येवाभिधीयते ॥ २७ ॥
}} }} }}

Steadfastness in sacrifice, austerity and gift is also called "{{sc|Sat}}", and action for the sake of the Supreme<ref>{{sc|Tat}}.</ref> is also named "{{sc|Sat}}." {{float right|{{larger|(27)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
अश्रद्धया हुतं दत्तं तपस्तप्तं कृतं च यत् ।

असदित्युच्यते पार्थ न च तत्प्रेत्य नो इह ॥ २८ ॥
}} }} }}

Whatsoever is wrought without faith, oblation, gift, austerity, or other deed, "Asat" it is called, O Pârtha; it is nought, here or hereafter. {{float right|{{larger|(28)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
इति श्रीमद्भगवद्गीता॰ श्रद्धात्रयविभागयोगो नाम सप्तदशोऽध्यायः ।
}} }} }}
{{nop}}<noinclude>{{rule}}
{{smallrefs}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="4" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader||SEVENTEENTH DISCOURSE.|237}}</noinclude>{{fine block|Thus in the glorious Upanishads of the {{sc|Bhagavad-Gita}}, the science of the {{sc|Eternal}}, the scripture of Yoga, the dialogue between Shrî Krishna and Arjuna, the seventeenth discourse, entitled:}}

{{c|THE YOGA OF THE DIVISION OF THREEFOLD FAITH.}}


{{rule|3em}}<noinclude></noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" /></noinclude>{{dhr}}
{{c|{{larger|EIGHTEENTH DISCOURSE.}}}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
{{c|अर्जुन उवाच ।}}

संन्यासस्य महाबाहो तत्त्वमिच्छामि वेदितुम् ।

त्यागस्य च हृषीकेश पृथक्केशिनिषूदन ॥ १ ॥
}} }} }}

{{c|Arjuna said:}}

I desire, O mighty-armed, to know severally the essence of renunciation,<ref>Sannyâsa.</ref> O Hrishîkesha, and of relinquishment<ref>Tyâga.</ref>, O Keshinishûdana<ref>Slayer of Keshi, a demon.</ref>. {{float right|{{larger|(1)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
{{c|श्रीभगवानुवाच ।}}

काम्यानां कर्मणां न्यासं संन्यासं कवयो विदुः ।

सर्वकर्मफलत्यागं प्राहुस्त्यागं विचक्षणाः ॥ २ ॥
}} }} }}

{{c|The Blessed Lord said:}}

Sages have known as renunciation the renouncing of works with desire; the relinquishing of the fruit of all actions is called relinquishment by the wise. {{float right|{{larger|(2)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}<noinclude>{{rule}}
{{smallrefs}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader||EIGHTEENTH DISCOURSE.|239}}</noinclude>{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
त्याज्यं दोषवदित्येके कर्म प्राहुर्मनीषिणः ।

यज्ञदानतपः कर्म न त्याज्यमिति चापरे ॥  ३ ॥
}} }} }}

"Action should be relinquished as an evil,"<ref>Some read: "Because it is evil."</ref> declare some thoughtful men; "acts of sacrifice, gift and austerity should not be relinquished," say others. {{float right|{{larger|(3)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
निश्चयं शृणु मे तत्र त्यागे भरतसत्तम ।

त्यागो हि पुरुषव्याघ्र त्रिविधः सम्प्रकीर्तितः ॥ ४ ॥
}} }} }}

Hear my conclusions as to that relinquishment, O best of the Bhâratas; since relinquishment, O tiger of men, has been explained as threefold. {{float right|{{larger|(4)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
यज्ञदानतपः कर्म न त्याज्यं कार्यमेव तत् ।

यज्ञो दानं तपश्चैव पावनानि मनीषिणाम् ॥ ५ ॥
}} }} }}

Acts of sacrifice, gift and austerity should not be relinquished, but should be performed;<noinclude>{{rule}}
{{smallrefs}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader|240|THE BHAGAVAD-GITA.|}}</noinclude>sacrifice, gift and also austerity are the purifiers of the intelligent. {{float right|{{larger|(5)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
एतान्यपि तु कर्माणि सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा फलानि च ।

कर्तव्यानीति मे पार्थ निश्चितं मतमुत्तमम् ॥ ६ ॥
}} }} }}

But even these actions should be done leaving aside attachment and fruit, O Pârtha; that is my certain and best belief. {{float right|{{larger|(6)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
नियतस्य तु संन्यासः कर्मणो नोपपद्यते ।

मोहात्तस्य परित्यागस्तामसः परिकीर्तितः ॥ ७ ॥
}} }} }}

Verily renunciation of actions that are prescribed is not proper; the relinquishment thereof from delusion is said to be of darkness. {{float right|{{larger|(7)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
दुःखमित्येव यत्कर्म कायक्लेशभयात्त्यजेत् ।

स कृत्वा राजसं त्यागं नैव त्यागफलं लभेत् ॥ ८ ॥
}} }} }}

He who relinquisheth an action from fear of physical suffering, saying "Painful," thus performing a passionate relinquishment, obtaineth not the fruit of relinquishment. {{float right|{{larger|(8)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}<noinclude></noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader||EIGHTEENTH DISCOURSE.|241}}</noinclude>{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
कार्यमित्येव यत्कर्म नियतं क्रियतेऽर्जुन ।

सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा फलं चैव स त्यागः सात्त्विको मतः ॥ ९ ॥
}} }} }}

He who performeth a prescribed action, saying, "it ought to be done," O Arjuna, relinquishing attachment and also fruit, that relinquishment is regarded as pure. {{float right|{{larger|(9)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
न द्वेष्ट्यकुशलं कर्म कुशले नानुषज्जते ।

त्यागी सत्त्वसमाविष्टो मेधावी छिन्नसंशयः ॥ १० ॥
}} }} }}

The relinquisher pervaded by purity, intelligent and with doubts cut away, hateth not unpleasurable action nor is attached to pleasurable. {{float right|{{larger|(10)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
न हि देहभृता शक्यं त्यक्तुं कर्माण्यशेषतः ।

यस्तु कर्मफलत्यागी स त्यागीत्यभिधीयते ॥ ११ ॥
}} }} }}

Nor indeed can embodied beings completely relinquish action; verily he who relinquisheth the fruit of action, he is said to be a relinquisher. {{float right|{{larger|(11)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}<noinclude></noinclude>
