<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader|242|THE BHAGAVAD-GITA.|}}</noinclude>{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
अनिष्टमिष्टं मिश्रं च त्रिविधं कर्मणः फलम् ।

भवत्यत्यागिनां प्रेत्य न तु संन्यासिनां क्वचित् ॥ १२ ॥
}}}}}}

Good, evil and mixed—threefold is the fruit of action hereafter for the non-relinquisher; but there is none ever for the renouncer. {{float right|{{larger|(12)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
पञ्चैतानि महाबाहो कारणानि निबोध मे ।

साङ्ख्ये कृतान्ते प्रोक्तानि सिद्धये सर्वकर्मणाम् ॥ १३ ॥
}} }} }}

These five causes, O mighty-armed, learn of Me as declared in the [[w:Samkhya|Sâñkhya]] system for the accomplishment of all actions: {{float right|{{larger|(13)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
अधिष्ठानं तथा कर्ता करणं च पृथग्विधम् ।

विविधाश्च पृथक्चेष्टा दैवं चैवात्र पञ्चमम् ॥ १४ ॥
}} }} }}

The body, the actor, the various organs, the diverse kinds of energies, and the presiding deities also, the fifth. {{float right|{{larger|(15)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
शरीरवाङ्‌मनोभिर्यत्कर्म प्रारभते नरः ।

न्याय्यं वा विपरीतं वा पञ्चैते तस्य हेतवः ॥ १५ ॥
}} }} }}
{{nop}}<noinclude></noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader||EIGHTEENTH DISCOURSE.|243}}</noinclude>Whatever action a man performeth by his body, speech and mind,<ref name="p243Manah">Manah.</ref> whether right or the reverse, these five are the cause thereof. {{float right|{{larger|(15)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
तत्रैवं सति कर्तारमात्मानं केवलं तु यः ।

पश्यत्यकृतबुद्धित्वान्न स पश्यति दुर्मतिः ॥ १६ ॥
}} }} }}

That being so, he verily who—owing to untrained Reason<ref name="p243Buddhi">Buddhi.</ref>—looketh on his {{sc|Self}}, which is isolated, as the actor, he of perverted intelligence, seeth not. {{float right|{{larger|(16)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
यस्य नाहंकृतो भावो बुद्धिर्यस्य न लिप्यते ।

हत्वाऽपि स इमाँल्लोकान्न हन्ति न निबध्यते ॥ १७ ॥ 
}} }} }}

He who is free from the egoistic notion, whose Reason<ref name="p243Buddhi" /> is not affected, though he slay these peoples, he slayeth not, nor is bound. {{float right|{{larger|(17)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
ज्ञानं ज्ञेयं परिज्ञाता त्रिविधा कर्मचोदना ।

करणं कर्म कर्तेति त्रिविधः कर्मसङ्ग्रहः ॥ १८ ॥
}} }} }}

Knowledge, the knowable and the knower,<noinclude>{{rule}}
{{smallrefs}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader|244|THE BHAGAVAD-GITA.|}}</noinclude>the threefold impulse to action; the organ, the action, the actor, the threefold constituents of action. {{float right|{{larger|(18)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
ज्ञानं कर्म च कर्ता च त्रिधैव गुणभेदतः ।

प्रोच्यते गुणसङ्ख्याने यथावच्छृणु तान्यपि ॥ १९ ॥
}} }} }}

Knowledge, action and actor in the category of qualities<ref name="p244Gunas">Gunas.</ref> are also said to be severally threefold, from the difference of qualities<ref name="p244Gunas" />; hear thou duly these also. {{float right|{{larger|(19)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
सर्वभूतेषु येनैकं भावमव्ययमीक्षते ।

अविभक्तं विभक्तेषु तज्ज्ञानं विद्धि सात्त्विकम् ॥ २० ॥
}} }} }}

That by which one indestructible Being is seen in all beings, inseparate in the separated, know thou that knowledge as pure. {{float right|{{larger|(20)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
पृथक्त्वेन तु यज्ज्ञानं नानाभावान्पृथग्विधान् ।

वेत्ति सर्वेषु भूतेषु तज्ज्ञानं विद्धि राजसम् ॥ २१ ॥
}} }} }}

But that knowledge which regardeth the<noinclude>{{rule}}
{{smallrefs}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader||EIGHTEENTH DISCOURSE.|245}}</noinclude>several manifold existences in all beings as separate, that knowledge know thou as of passion; {{float right|{{larger|(21)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
यत्तु कृत्स्नवदेकस्मिन् कार्ये सक्तमहैतुकम् ।

अतत्त्वार्थवदल्पं च तत्तामसमुदाहृतम् ॥ २२ ॥
}} }} }}

While that which clingeth to each one thing as if it were the whole, without reason, without grasping the reality, narrow, that is declared to be dark. {{float right|{{larger|(22)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
नियतं सङ्गरहितमरागद्वेषतः कृतम् ।

अफलप्रेप्सुना कर्म यत्तत्सात्त्विकमुच्यते ॥ २३ ॥
}} }} }}

An action which is ordained, done by one undesirous of fruit, devoid of attachment, without love or hate, that is called pure. {{float right|{{larger|(23)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
यत्तु कामेप्सुना कर्म साहङ्कारेण वा पुनः ।

क्रियते बहुलायासं तद्राजसमुदाहृतम् ॥ २४ ॥
}} }} }}

But that action that is done by one longing for<noinclude></noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader|246|THE BHAGAVAD-GITA.|}}</noinclude>desires, or again with egoism, or with much effort, that is declared to be passionate. {{float right|{{larger|(24)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
अनुबन्धं क्षयं हिंसामनपेक्ष्य च पौरुषम् ।

मोहादारभ्यते कर्म यत्तत्तामसमुच्यते ॥ २५ ॥
}} }} }}

The action undertaken from delusion, without regard to capacity and consequences—loss and injury to others—that is declared to be dark. {{float right|{{larger|(25)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
मुक्तसङ्गोऽनहंवादी धृत्युत्साहसमन्वितः ।

सिद्ध्यसिद्ध्योर्निर्विकारः कर्त्ता सात्त्विक उच्यते ॥ २६ ॥
}} }} }}

Liberated from attachment, not egoistic, endued with firmness and confidence, unchanged by success or failure, that actor is called pure. {{float right|{{larger|(26)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
रागी कर्मफलप्रेप्सुर्लुब्धो हिंसात्मकोऽशुचिः ।

हर्षशोकान्वितः कर्ता राजसः परिकीर्तितः ॥ २७ ॥
}} }} }}

Impassioned, desiring to obtain the fruit of actions, greedy, harmful, impure, moved by joy and sorrow, such an actor is pronounced passionate. {{float right|{{larger|(27)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}<noinclude></noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader||EIGHTEENTH DISCOURSE.|247}}</noinclude>{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
अयुक्तः प्राकृतः स्तब्धः शठो नैष्कृतिकोऽलसः ।

विषादी दीर्घसूत्री च कर्ता तामस उच्यते ॥ २८ ॥
}} }} }}

Discordant, vulgar, stubborn, cheating, malicious, indolent, despairful, procrastinating, that actor is called dark. {{float right|{{larger|(28)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
बुद्धेर्भेदं धृतेश्चैव गुणतस्त्रिविधं शृणु ।

प्रोच्यमानमशेषेण पृथक्त्वेन धनञ्जय ॥ २९ ॥
}} }} }}

The division of Reason<ref name="p247Buddhi">Buddhi.</ref> and of firmness also, threefold according to the qualities<ref>Gunas.</ref>, hear thou related, unreservedly and severally, O Dhananjaya. {{float right|{{larger|(29)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
प्रवृत्तिं च निवृत्तिं च कार्याकार्ये भयाभये ।

बन्धं मोक्षं च या वेत्ति बुद्धिः सा पार्थ सात्त्विकी ॥ ३० ॥
}} }} }}

That which knoweth energy and abstinence, what ought to be done and what ought not to be done, fear and fearlessness, bondage and liberation, that Reason<ref name="p247Buddhi" /> is pure, O Pârtha. {{float right|{{larger|(30)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}<noinclude>{{rule}}
{{smallrefs}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader|248|THE BHAGAVAD-GITA.|}}</noinclude>{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
यया धर्ममधर्मं च कार्यं चाकार्यमेव च ।

अयथावत्प्रजानाति बुद्धिः सा पार्थ राजसी ॥ ३१ ॥
}} }} }}

That by which one understandeth away Right and Wrong<ref>Dharma and Adharma, Right and Wrong in the widest sense, law and lawlessness.</ref> and also what ought to be done and what ought not to be done, that Reason,<ref name="p248Buddhi">Buddhi.</ref> O Pârtha, is passionate. {{float right|{{larger|(31)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
अधर्मं धर्ममिति या मन्यते तमसा वृता ।

सर्वार्थान् विपरीतांश्च बुद्धिः सा पार्थ तामसी ॥ ३२ ॥
}} }} }}

That which, enwrapped in darkness, thinketh wrong<ref>Adharma.</ref> to be right<ref>Dharma.</ref> and seeth all things subverted, that Reason<ref name="p248Buddhi" />, O Pârtha, is of darkness. {{float right|{{larger|32)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
धृत्या यया धारयते मनःप्राणेन्द्रियक्रियाः ।

योगेनाव्यभिचारिण्या धृतिः सा पार्थ सात्त्विकी ॥ ३३ ॥
}} }} }}

The unwavering firmness by which, through Yoga, one restraineth the activity of the mind<ref>Manah.</ref>,<noinclude>{{rule}}
{{smallrefs}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader||EIGHTEENTH DISCOURSE.|249}}</noinclude>of the life breaths and of the sense-organs, that firmness, O Pârtha, is pure. {{float right|{{larger|(33)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
यया तु धर्मकामार्थान् धृत्या धारयतेऽर्जुन ।

प्रसङ्गेन फलाकाङ्क्षी धृतिः सा पार्थ राजसी ॥ ३४ ॥
}} }} }}

But the firmness, O Arjuna, by which, from attachment desirous of fruit, one holdeth fast duty<ref>Dharma.</ref>, desire and wealth, that firmness, O Pârtha, is passionate. {{float right|{{larger|(34)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
यया स्वप्नं भयं शोकं विषादं मदमेव च ।

न विमुञ्चति दुर्मेधा धृतिः सा पार्थ तामसी ॥ ३५ ॥
}} }} }}

That by which one from stupidity doth not abandon sleep, fear, grief, despair, and also vanity, that firmness, O Pârtha, is dark. {{float right|{{larger|(35)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
सुखं त्विदानीं त्रिविधं शृणु मे भरतर्षभ ।

अभ्यासाद्रमते यत्र दुःखान्तं च निगच्छति ॥ ३६ ॥
}} }} }}

And now the threefold kinds of pleasure hear<noinclude>{{rule}}
{{smallrefs}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader|250|THE BHAGAVAD-GITA.|}}</noinclude>thou from Me, O bull of the Bhâratas. That in which one by practice rejoiceth, and which putteth an end to pain; {{float right|{{larger|(36)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
यत्तदग्रे विषमिव परिणामेऽमृतोपमम् ।

तत्सुखं सात्त्विकं प्रोक्तमात्मबुद्धिप्रसादजम् ॥ ३७ ॥
}} }} }}

Which at first is as venom but in the end is as nectar; that pleasure is said to be pure, born of the blissful knowledge of the {{sc|Self}}. {{float right|{{larger|(37)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
विषयेन्द्रियसंयोगाद्यत्तदग्रेऽमृतोपमम् ।

परिणामे विषमिव तत्सुखं राजसं स्मृतम् ॥ ३८ ॥
}} }} }}

That which from the union of the senses with their objects at first is as nectar, but in the end is like venom, that pleasure is accounted passionate. {{float right|{{larger|(38)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
यदग्रे चानुबन्धे च सुखं मोहनमात्मनः ।

निद्रालस्यप्रमादोत्थं तत्तामसमुदाहृतम् ॥ ३९ ॥
}} }} }}

That pleasure which both at first and afterwards is delusive of the self, arising from sleep,<noinclude></noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader||EIGHTEENTH DISCOURSE.|251}}</noinclude>indolence and heedlessness, that is declared dark. {{float right|{{larger|(39)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
न तदस्ति पृथिव्यां वा दिवि देवेषु वा पुनः ।

सत्त्वं प्रकृतिजैर्मुक्तं यदेभिः स्यात्त्रिभिर्गुणैः ॥ ४० ॥
}} }} }}

There is not an entity, either on the earth or again in heaven among the Shining Ones, that is liberated from these three qualities,<ref name="p251Gunas">Gunas.</ref> born of Matter<ref>Prakriti.</ref>. {{float right|{{larger|(40)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
ब्राह्मणक्षत्रियविशां शूद्राणां च परन्तप ।

कर्माणि प्रविभक्तानि स्वभावप्रभवैर्गुणैः ॥ ४१ ॥
}} }} }}

Of Brâhmanas, Kshattriyas, Vaishyas and Shûdras, O Parantapa, the duties<ref>Karma; it is action arising from the nature fashioned by past thoughts and desires.</ref> have been distributed, according to the qualities<ref name="p251Gunas" /> born of their own natures. {{float right|{{larger|(41)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
शमो दमस्तपः शौचं क्षान्तिरार्जवमेव च ।

ज्ञानं विज्ञानमास्तिक्यं ब्रह्मकर्म स्वभावजम् ॥ ४२ ॥
}} }} }}
{{nop}}<noinclude>{{rule}}
{{smallrefs}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader|252|THE BHAGAVAD-GITA.|}}</noinclude>Serenity, self-restraint, austerity, purity, forgiveness and also uprightness, wisdom, knowledge, belief in God, are the Brâhmana duty<ref name="p252Karma">Karma.</ref>, born of his own nature. {{float right|{{larger|(42)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
शौर्यं तेजो धृतिर्दाक्ष्यं युद्धे चाप्यपलायनम् ।

दानमीश्वरभावश्च क्षात्रं कर्म स्वभावजम् ॥ ४३ ॥
}} }} }}

Prowess, splendour, firmness, dexterity, and also not flying from battle, generosity, the nature of a ruler, are the Kshattriya duty<ref name="p252Karma" />, born of his own nature. {{float right|{{larger|(43)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
कृषिगौरक्ष्यवाणिज्यं वैश्यकर्म स्वभावजम् ।

परिचर्यात्मकं कर्म शूद्रस्यापि स्वभावजम् ॥ ४४ ॥
}} }} }}

Ploughing, protection of kine, and trade are the Vaishya duty<ref name="p252Karma" />, born of his own nature. Action of the nature of service is the Shûdra duty,<ref name="p252Karma" /> born of his own nature. {{float right|{{larger|(44)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}<noinclude>{{rule}}
{{smallrefs}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader||EIGHTEENTH DISCOURSE.|253}}</noinclude>{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
स्वे स्वे कर्मण्यभिरतः संसिद्धिं लभते नरः ।

स्वकर्मनिरतः सिद्धिं यथा विन्दति तच्छृणु ॥ ४५ ॥
}} }} }}

Man reacheth perfection by each being intent on his own duty<ref name="p252Karma" />. Listen thou how perfection is won by him who is intent on his own duty<ref name="p252Karma" />. {{float right|{{larger|(45)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
यतः प्रवृत्तिर्भूतानां येन सर्वमिदं ततम् ।

स्वकर्मणा तमभ्यर्च्य सिद्धिं विन्दति मानवः ॥ ४६ ॥
}} }} }}

He from whom is the emanation of beings, by Whom all This is pervaded, by worshipping Him in his own duty<ref name="p252Karma" /> a man winneth perfection. {{float right|{{larger|(46)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
श्रेयान् स्वधर्मो विगुणः परधर्मात्स्वनुष्ठितात् ।

स्वभावनियतं कर्म कुर्वन्नाप्नोति किल्बिषम् ॥ ४७ ॥
}} }} }}

Better is one's own duty<ref name="p253Dharma">Dharma. There is a subtle difference in these words, here used almost interchangeably. Karma arises from the past; Dharma also so arises, but implies also the law by which the next step in evolution is made.</ref> though destitute of merits than the well-executed duty<ref name="p253Dharma" /> of another.<noinclude>{{rule}}
{{smallrefs|refx=<ref name="p252Karma">Karma.</ref>}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader|254|THE BHAGAVAD-GITA.|}}</noinclude>He who doeth the duty<ref name="p252Karma" /> laid down by his own nature incurreth not sin. {{float right|{{larger|(47)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
सहजं कर्म कौन्तेय सदोषमपि न त्यजेत् ।

सर्वारम्भा हि दोषेण धूमेनाग्निरिवावृताः ॥ ४८ ॥
}} }} }}

Congenital duty<ref name="p252Karma" />, O son of Kunti, though defective, ought not to be abandoned. All undertakings indeed are clouded by defects as fire by smoke. {{float right|{{larger|(48)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
असक्तबुद्धिः सर्वत्र जितात्मा विगतस्पृहः ।

नैष्कर्म्यसिद्धिं परमां संन्यासेनाधिगच्छति ॥ ४९ ॥
}} }} }}

He whose Reason<ref name="p254Buddhi">Buddhi.</ref> is everywhere unattached, the self-subdued, dead to desires, he goeth by renunciation to the supreme perfection of freedom from obligation.<ref name="p252Karma" /> {{float right|{{larger|(49)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}<noinclude>{{rule}}
{{smallrefs|refx=<ref name="p252Karma">Karma.</ref>}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader||EIGHTEENTH DISCOURSE.|255}}</noinclude>{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
सिद्धिं प्राप्तो यथा ब्रह्म तथाऽऽप्नोति निबोध मे ।

समासेनैव कौन्तेय निष्ठा ज्ञानस्य या परा ॥ ५० ॥
}} }} }}

How he who hath attained perfection obtaineth the {{sc|Eternal}}, that highest state of wisdom, learn thou from Me only succinctly, O Kaunteya. {{float right|{{larger|(50)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
बुद्ध्या विशुद्धया युक्तो धृत्याऽऽत्मानं {{SIC|नियस्य|नियम्य}} च ।

शब्दादीन्विषयांस्त्यक्त्वा रागद्वेषौ व्युदस्य च ॥ ५१ ॥
}} }} }}

United to this Reason,<ref name="p254Buddhi" /> purified, controlling the self by firmness, having abandoned sound and the other objects of the senses, having laid aside passion and malice, {{float right|{{larger|(51)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
विविक्तसेवी लघ्वाशी यतवाक्कायमानसः ।

ध्यानयोगपरो नित्यं वैराग्यं समुपाश्रितः ॥ ५२ ॥
}} }} }}

Dwelling in solitude, abstemious, speech, body and mind<ref>Manah.</ref> subdued, constantly fixed in meditation and yoga<ref>Some read "dhyânayoga", Yoga of "meditation."</ref>, taking refuge in dispassion, {{float right|{{larger|(52)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}<noinclude>{{rule}}
{{smallrefs|refx=<ref name="p254Buddhi">Buddhi.</ref>}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader|256|THE BHAGAVAD-GITA.|}}</noinclude>{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
अहङ्कारं बलं दर्पं कामं क्रोधं परिग्रहम् ।

विमुच्य निर्ममः शान्तो ब्रह्मभूयाय कल्पते ॥ ५३ ॥
}} }} }}

Having cast aside egoism, violence, arrogance, desire, wrath, covetousness, selfless and peaceful—he is fit to become the {{sc|Eternal}}. {{float right|{{larger|(53)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
ब्रह्मभूतः प्रसन्नात्मा न शोचति न काङ्क्षति ।

समः सर्वेषु भूतेषु मद्भक्तिं लभते पराम् ॥ ५४ ॥
}} }} }}

Becoming the {{sc|Eternal}}, serene in the {{sc|Self}}, he neither grieveth nor desireth; the same to all beings, he obtaineth supreme devotion unto Me. {{float right|{{larger|(54)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
भक्त्या मामभिजानाति यावान्यश्चास्मि तत्त्वतः ।

ततो मां तत्त्वतो ज्ञात्वा विशते तदनन्तरम् ॥ ५५ ॥
}} }} }}

By devotion he knoweth Me in essence, who and what I am; having thus known Me in essence he forthwith entereth into the Supreme.<ref>{{sc|That}}.</ref> {{float right|{{larger|(55)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
सर्वकर्माण्यपि सदा कुर्वाणो मद्व्यपाश्रयः ।

मत्प्रसादादवाप्नोति शाश्वतं पदमव्ययम् ॥ ५६ ॥
}} }} }}
{{nop}}<noinclude>{{rule}}
{{smallrefs}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader||EIGHTEENTH DISCOURSE.|257}}</noinclude>Though ever performing all actions, taking refuge in Me, by My grace he obtaineth the eternal indestructible abode. {{float right|{{larger|(56)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
चेतसा सर्वकर्माणि मयि संन्यस्य मत्परः ।

बुद्धियोगमुपाश्रित्य मच्चित्तः सततं भव ॥ ५७ ॥
}} }} }}

Renouncing mentally all works in Me, intent on Me, resorting to the yoga of discrimination<ref>Buddhi-yoga.</ref>, have thy thought ever on Me. {{float right|{{larger|(57)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
मच्चित्तः सर्वदुर्गाणि मत्प्रसादात्तरिष्यसि ।

अथ चेत्त्वमहङ्कारान्न श्रोष्यसि विनङ्क्ष्यसि ॥ ५८ ॥
}} }} }}

Thinking on Me, thou shalt overcome all obstacles by My grace: but if from egoism thou wilt not listen, thou shalt be destroyed utterly. {{float right|{{larger|(58)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
यदहङ्कारमाश्रित्य न योत्स्य इति मन्यसे ।

मिथ्यैष व्यवसायस्ते प्रकृतिस्त्वां नियोक्ष्यति ॥ ५९ ॥
}} }} }}

Entrenched in egoism, thou thinkest, "I will<noinclude>{{rule}}
{{smallrefs}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader|258|THE BHAGAVAD-GITA.|}}</noinclude>not fight;" to no purpose thy determination; nature will constrain thee. {{float right|{{larger|(59)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
स्वभावजेन कौन्तेय निबद्धः स्वेन कर्मणा ।

कर्तुं नेच्छसि यन्मोहात्करिष्यस्यवशोऽपि तत् ॥ ६० ॥
}} }} }}

O son of Kuntî, bound by thine own duty<ref>Karma.</ref> born of thine own nature, that which from delusion thou desirest not to do, even that helplessly thou shalt perform. {{float right|{{larger|(60)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
ईश्वरः सर्वभूतानां हृद्देशेऽर्जुन तिष्ठति ।

भ्रामयन्सर्वभूतानि यन्त्रारूढानि मायया ॥ ६१ ॥
}} }} }}

The Lord dwelleth in the hearts of all beings, O Arjuna, by His illusive Power<ref>Mâyâ.</ref> causing all beings to revolve, as though mounted on a potter's wheel. {{float right|{{larger|(61)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
तमेव शरणं गच्छ सर्वभावेन भारत ।

तत्प्रसादात्परां शान्तिं स्थानं प्राप्स्यसि शाश्वतम् ॥ ६२ ॥
}} }} }}

Flee unto Him for shelter with all thy being, O Bhârata; by His grace thou shalt obtain supreme peace, the everlasting dwelling-place. {{float right|{{larger|(62)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}<noinclude>{{rule}}
{{smallrefs}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader||EIGHTEENTH DISCOURSE.|259}}</noinclude>{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
इति ते ज्ञानमाख्यातं गुह्याद्‌गुह्यतरं मया ।

विमृश्यैतदशेषेण यथेच्छसि तथा कुरु ॥ ६३ ॥
}} }} }}

Thus hath wisdom, more secret than secrecy itself, been declared unto thee by Me; having reflected on it fully, then act thou as thou listest. {{float right|{{larger|(63)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
सर्वगुह्यतमं भूयः शृणु मे परमं वचः ।

इष्टोऽसि मे दृढमिति ततो वक्ष्यामि ते हितम् ॥ ६४ ॥
}} }} }}

Listen thou again to My supreme word, most secret of all; beloved art thou of Me, and steadfast of heart, therefore will I speak for thy benefit. {{float right|{{larger|(64)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
मन्मना भव मद्भक्तो मद्याजी मां नमस्कुरु ।

मामेवैष्यसि सत्यं ते प्रतिजाने प्रियोऽसि मे ॥ ६५ ॥
}} }} }}

Merge thy mind<ref>Manah.</ref> in Me, be my devotee, sacrifice to Me, prostrate thyself before Me, thou shalt come even to Me. I pledge thee My troth; thou art dear to Me. {{float right|{{larger|(65)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}<noinclude>{{rule}}
{{smallrefs}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader|260|THE BHAGAVAD-GITA.|}}</noinclude>{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
सर्वधर्मान्परित्यज्य मामेकं शरणं व्रज ।

अहं त्वां सर्वपापेभ्यो मोक्षयिष्यामि मा शुचः ॥ ६६ ॥
}} }} }}

Abandoning all duties<ref>Dharmas.</ref> come unto Me alone for shelter; sorrow not, I will liberate thee from all sins. {{float right|{{larger|(66)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
इदं ते नातपस्काय नाभक्ताय कदाचन ।

न चाशुश्रूषवे वाच्यं न च मां योऽभ्यसूयति ॥ ६७ ॥
}} }} }}

Never is this to be spoken by thee to anyone who is without asceticism, nor without devotion, nor to one who desireth not to listen, nor yet to him who speaketh evil of Me. {{float right|{{larger|(67)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
य इदं परमं गुह्यं मद्भक्तेष्वभिधास्यति ।

भक्तिं मयि परां कृत्वा मामेवैष्यत्यसंशयम् ॥ ६८ ॥
}} }} }}

He who shall declare this supreme secret among My devotees, having shown the highest devotion for Me, without doubt he shall come to Me.<ref>Some read "asamsayah," which would mean "being freed from doubts."</ref> {{float right|{{larger|(68)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}<noinclude>{{rule}}
{{smallrefs}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader||EIGHTEENTH DISCOURSE.|261}}</noinclude>{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
न च तस्मान्मनुष्येषु कश्चिन्मे प्रियकृत्तमः ।

भविता न च मे तस्मादन्यः प्रियतरो भुवि ॥ ६९ ॥
}} }} }}

Nor is there any among men who performeth dearer service to Me than he, nor any other shall be more beloved by Me on earth than he. {{float right|{{larger|(69)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
अध्येष्यते च य इमं धर्म्यं संवादमावयोः ।

ज्ञानयज्ञेन तेनाहमिष्टः स्यामिति मे मतिः ॥ ७० ॥
}} }} }}

And he who shall study this sacred dialogue of ours, by him I shall be worshipped with the sacrifice of wisdom. Such is My mind. {{float right|{{larger|(70)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
श्रद्धावाननसूयश्च शृणुयादपि यो नरः ।

सोऽपि मुक्तः शुभांल्लोकान्प्राप्नुयात्पुण्यकर्मणाम् ॥ ७१ ॥
}} }} }}

The man also who, full of faith, merely heareth it unreviling, even he, freed from evil, obtaineth the radiant worlds of the righteous. {{float right|{{larger|(71)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
कच्चिदेतच्छ्रुतं पार्थ त्वयैकाग्रेण चेतसा ।

कच्चिदज्ञानसम्मोहः प्रणष्टस्ते धनञ्जय ॥ ७२ ॥
}} }} }}
{{nop}}<noinclude></noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader|262|THE BHAGAVAD-GITA.|}}</noinclude>Hath this been heard, O son of Prithâ, with one-pointed mind? Has thy delusion, caused by unwisdom, been destroyed, O Dhananjaya? {{float right|{{larger|(72)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
{{c|अर्जुन उवाच ।}}

नष्टो मोहः {{SIC|स्मूतिर्लब्धा|स्मृतिर्लब्धा}} त्वत्प्रसादान्मयाऽच्युत ।

स्थितोऽस्मि गतसन्देहः करिष्ये वचनं तव ॥ ७३ ॥
}} }} }}

{{c|Arjuna said:}}

Destroyed is my delusion. I have gained knowledge<ref>Literally "memory".</ref> through Thy grace, O Immutable one. I am firm, my doubts have fled away. I will do according to Thy word. {{float right|{{larger|(73)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
{{c|सञ्जय उवाच ।}}

इत्यहं वासुदेवस्य पार्थस्य च महात्मनः ।

संवादमिममश्रौषमद्भुतं रोमहर्षणम् ॥ ७४ ॥
}} }} }}

{{c|Sanjaya said:}}

I heard this marvellous dialogue of Vâsudeva, and of the great-souled Partha, causing my hair to stand on end. {{float right|{{larger|(74)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}<noinclude>{{rule}}
{{smallrefs}}</noinclude>

<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Hrishikes" />{{RunningHeader||EIGHTEENTH DISCOURSE.|263}}</noinclude>{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
व्यासप्रसादाच्छ्रुतवानेतद् गुह्यमहं परम् ।

योगं योगेश्वरात्कृष्णात्साक्षात्कथयतः स्वयम् ॥ ७५ ॥
}} }} }}

By the favour of Vyâsa I listened to this secret and supreme yoga from the Lord of Yoga, Krishna Himself, speaking before mine eyes. {{float right|{{larger|(75)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
राजन्संस्मृत्य संस्मृत्य संवादमिममद्भुतम् ।

केशवार्जुनयोः पुण्यं हृष्यामि च मुहुर्मुहुः ॥ ७६ ॥
}} }} }}

O King, remembering, remembering this marvellous and holy dialogue between Keshava and Arjuna, I rejoice again and again. {{float right|{{larger|(76)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
तच्च संस्मृत्य संस्मृत्य रूपमत्यद्भुतं हरेः ।

विस्मयो मे महान् राजन् हृष्यामि च पुनः पुनः ॥ ७७ ॥
}} }} }}

Remembering, remembering, also that most marvellous form of Hari, great is my wonder, O King. I rejoice, again and again. {{float right|{{larger|(77)}}}}
{{-}}
{{dhr}}

{{block center|{{larger block|{{lang block|sa|
यत्र योगेश्वरः कृष्णो यत्र पार्थो धनुर्धरः ।

तत्र श्रीर्विजयो भूतिर्ध्रुवा नीतिर्मतिर्मम ॥ ७८ ॥
}} }} }}

Wherever is Krishna, Yoga's Lord, wherever<noinclude></noinclude>

{{RunningHeader|264|THE BHAGAVAD-GITA.|}}is Pârtha, the archer, assured are there prosperity, victory and happiness. '''Contents.'''—Hymn to Hari; The Ten- Versed Hymn; Hyma to Dakshinamurti; Direct Realisation; The Century of Verses; Knowledge of Self; Commentary on the Text; Definition of cue's own Self.

'''Preface.'''—The main object of this publication is to present, in simple English, some of the works of Sri Sankaraeharya in which he tried to expound, in a popular style, the philosophy of the non-dualistic Vedanta of which he was the well-known founder. With this view the present translation has been rendered free of technical words and phrases. It is hoped that the juxtaposition of the Sanskrit test and the English translation will serve the double object of enabling the student of Sanskrit to understand the text better and to correct, by a reference to the text, any defect; of expression in the translation as an inevitable result of the attempt to garb it! a popular style. To those that have had no training in metaphysics or dialectics and have neither the leisure nor the capacity to read the original standard works of Sankara, a publication of this kind should be specially helpful for a proper understanding of the broad outline of Baukara's philosophy of non-dualism.
